gasteria.care_tips: Water when soil is dry (every 1-2 weeks). More frequent than desert succulents. Bright indirect to medium light preferred; tolerates lower light than most succulents. Medium humidity preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Repot every 2-3 years. Shade-tolerant and easy-care. Related to Haworthia. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

graptopetalum.description: Also known as: Mother-of-pearl plant. Succulents in the Crassulaceae family with rosette-forming leaves, often called ghost plants.
graptopetalum.care_tips: Water when soil is completely dry (every 2-3 weeks). Very drought tolerant. Bright indirect to direct light preferred - more light enhances coloration. Low humidity is fine. Fertilize 2-3 times per year during growing season with succulent fertilizer at quarter strength. Well-draining soil essential. Repot every 2-3 years. Rosette-forming with beautiful coloration. Often called ghost plants. Remove withered leaves at the base and thin excess offsets as needed.

graptoveria.description: Intergeneric hybrid between Graptopetalum and Echeveria, forming compact rosettes with thick, fleshy leaves in pastel hues that intensify with sun stress.
graptoveria.care_tips: Water thoroughly using the soak-and-dry method; allow soil to dry completely between waterings. Provide bright indirect to direct morning light for best coloration — insufficient light causes etiolation. Use a fast-draining cactus or succulent mix with added perlite. Fertilize once in spring and once in mid-summer with a diluted succulent fertilizer. Protect from frost below 5°C. Non-toxic to pets. Remove flower stems and any damaged or rotting leaves promptly.

scientific_names: Haworthiopsis fasciata (syn. Haworthia fasciata; Zebra plant)
haworthia.description: Small rosette succulents that tolerate lower light than most succulents, perfect for windowsills.
haworthia.care_tips: Water when soil is dry (every 1-2 weeks). More frequent than desert succulents. Bright indirect to medium light preferred; tolerates lower light than most succulents. Medium humidity preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Repot every 2-3 years. Perfect for windowsills. Small rosette-forming succulents. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

jade plant.description: Also known as: Money plant, Lucky plant. Classic succulent with thick, glossy green leaves, can live for decades and grow into a small tree.
jade plant.care_tips: Water when soil is completely dry (every 2-3 weeks). Water deeply but infrequently. Bright indirect to direct light preferred - needs good light to maintain compact growth. Low humidity is fine. Fertilize 2-3 times per year during growing season with balanced fertilizer at quarter strength. Can live for decades and grow into small tree. Prune to maintain shape. Repot every 2-3 years. Symbol of good luck. Overwatering causes root rot. Toxic to pets.

paddle plant.description: Also known as: Flapjack. Succulent with flat, paddle-shaped leaves that blush red at edges in bright light; monocarpic (dies after flowering).
paddle plant.care_tips: Water when soil is dry (every 1-2 weeks). Bright light enhances red edges. Low humidity fine. Fertilize sparingly. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or dry leaves at the base. Prune leggy stems for compact growth; let cuttings callus before replanting.

scientific_names: various species with different colors and patterns
lithops.description: Stone-like succulents that mimic pebbles in their native habitat, have specific dormancy periods when they should not be watered.
lithops.care_tips: Water sparingly in fall when new leaves emerge. Keep dry in summer dormancy and during winter/spring splitting. Very minimal watering even when active (every 2-4 weeks); water from below and let the pot drain fully. Bright direct light essential. Low humidity preferred. Fertilize very sparingly during active growth only. Repot every 3-5 years in very well-draining soil. Stone-like appearance mimics pebbles. Very specific care requirements. Leave the old leaf pair in place until it is completely papery, then remove it.

pachyphytum.description: Also known as: Moonstones. Adorable succulents with plump, egg-shaped leaves in pastel shades of lavender, pink, and blue-grey, often covered in a powdery farina coating.
pachyphytum.care_tips: Water only when soil is completely dry; soak and drain method works best. Bright indirect to gentle direct light—too much harsh sun can sunburn delicate leaves. Low humidity preferred—prone to rot in damp conditions. Gritty, fast-draining succulent mix essential. Fertilize once in spring with diluted cactus fertilizer. Avoid touching leaves—the farina coating doesn't grow back. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

elephant bush.description: Also known as: Spekboom. Small-leaved succulent often confused with jade; drought-tolerant, can be bonsai-trained. Native to South Africa.
elephant bush.care_tips: Water when soil is dry (every 1-2 weeks). Bright indirect to direct light. Low humidity fine. Fertilize 2-3 times per year. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

sedum.description: Large genus of succulents in the Crassulaceae family, includes both trailing and upright varieties.
sedum.care_tips: Water when soil is completely dry (every 2-3 weeks). Very drought tolerant. Bright indirect to direct light preferred. Low humidity is fine. Fertilize 2-3 times per year during growing season with succulent fertilizer at quarter strength. Well-draining soil essential. Repot every 2-3 years. Many varieties available - trailing and upright. Very easy-care succulents. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

sempervivum.description: Also known as: Hen and chicks. Hardy succulents in the Crassulaceae family known as hen and chicks, form rosettes and produce offsets. Extremely cold hardy and drought tolerant. Excellent for rock gardens, alpine gardens, and containers.
sempervivum.care_tips: Water when soil is completely dry (every 2-3 weeks). Very drought tolerant. Bright indirect to direct light preferred. Low humidity is fine. Fertilize sparingly (2-3 times per year) with succulent fertilizer at quarter strength. Well-draining soil essential. Produces offsets (chicks) around parent plant (hen). Repot every 2-3 years. Very cold-hardy succulents. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

scientific_names: Curio rowleyanus (syn. Senecio rowleyanus; String of pearls)
Curio radicans (syn. S. radicans; String of bananas)
Curio repens (syn. Senecio serpens; Blue chalk sticks)
Curio talinoides subsp. mandraliscae (syn. Senecio mandraliscae)
senecio.description: Large genus of succulents in the Asteraceae family, includes trailing varieties like string of pearls (many reclassified to Curio).
senecio.care_tips: Water when soil is completely dry (every 2-3 weeks). Very drought tolerant. Bright indirect to direct light preferred. Low humidity is fine. Fertilize 2-3 times per year during growing season with succulent fertilizer at quarter strength. Well-draining soil essential. Many are trailing plants. Repot every 2-3 years. Large genus with many varieties. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

split rock.description: Stone-mimicking succulent that resembles a split boulder, closely related to lithops but slightly larger. Native to South Africa.
split rock.care_tips: Water ONLY when old leaves have fully dried and absorbed into the new pair - typically only 2-4 times per year. Overwatering causes stacking (extra leaf pairs) and rot. Bright direct light essential - at least 5 hours daily. Very low humidity preferred. Do not fertilize. Excellent drainage essential - use mostly mineral substrate (pumice, perlite). Bottom watering preferred. Repot every 3-5 years. Very specific watering requirements similar to lithops. Remove flower stems and any damaged or rotting leaves promptly.

string of bananas.description: Trailing succulent with banana-shaped leaves, faster growing than String of Pearls.
string of bananas.care_tips: Water when leaves show slight wrinkling - this indicates thirst. Avoid overwatering which causes rot. Bright indirect light preferred. Low to medium humidity is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with succulent fertilizer at half strength. Faster growing than String of Pearls. Perfect for hanging baskets. Repot every 2-3 years. Handle carefully to avoid leaf drop. Banana-shaped leaves. Toxic to pets. Trim trailing stems to the desired length and remove any shriveled or dry sections.

string of dolphins.description: Also known as: Dolphin Plant, Dolphin Succulent. Trailing succulent with leaves shaped like leaping dolphins.
string of dolphins.care_tips: Water when leaves show slight wrinkling - this indicates thirst. Avoid overwatering which causes rot. Bright indirect light preferred. Low to medium humidity is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with succulent fertilizer at half strength. Unique dolphin-shaped leaves. Perfect for hanging baskets. Repot every 2-3 years. Handle carefully. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or dried leaves from the base. Prune leggy stems to promote compact growth. Allow cuts to callus before replanting.

string of hearts.description: Trailing succulent with heart-shaped leaves and purple undersides, produces tubers along stems.
string of hearts.care_tips: Water when soil is dry (every 1-2 weeks). More drought tolerant than String of Pearls due to tubers along stems. Bright indirect light preferred. Low to medium humidity is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Produces tubers along stems for storage. Perfect for hanging baskets. Repot every 2-3 years. Heart-shaped leaves with purple undersides. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

string of needles.description: Delicate trailing succulent with thin, needle-like leaves along wiry stems. Related to string of hearts but with a finer, more airy appearance.
string of needles.care_tips: Water when soil is completely dry. Bright indirect light preferred; tolerates some direct morning sun. Low humidity is fine. Very susceptible to overwatering — use well-draining succulent mix. Fertilize lightly spring through summer. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

string of pearls.description: Trailing succulent with bead-like leaves, perfect for hanging baskets.
string of pearls.care_tips: Water when pearls (leaves) show slight wrinkling - this indicates thirst. Avoid overwatering which causes rot. Bright indirect light preferred. Low to medium humidity is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with succulent fertilizer at half strength. Perfect for hanging baskets. Repot every 2-3 years. Bead-like leaves are delicate - handle carefully. Very popular trailing succulent. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

string of rubies.description: Trailing succulent with bean-shaped leaves that turn deep ruby-red in bright light; stems are purple-tinged.
string of rubies.care_tips: Water thoroughly when soil is completely dry; drought-tolerant. Bright indirect to direct light brings out intense red coloring—green in low light. Low humidity fine. Use well-draining succulent/cactus mix. Fertilize sparingly 2-3 times during growing season at quarter strength. Propagates easily from stem cuttings. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

string of turtles.description: Also known as: Turtle vine. Trailing peperomia with small, patterned leaves resembling turtle shells, slower growing than other string plants.
string of turtles.care_tips: Water when top 2 inches of soil is dry. Keep slightly more moist than other string plants but still avoid overwatering. Bright indirect light preferred. High humidity (60%+) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Slower growing than other string plants. Perfect for hanging baskets. Repot every 2-3 years. Small patterned leaves resembling turtle shells. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

black gem aloe.description: Compact aloe with dark green to black-tinted leaves; same care as aloe vera. Toxic to pets.
black gem aloe.care_tips: Water when soil is dry (every 2-3 weeks). Bright indirect to direct light. Low humidity fine. Fertilize 2-3 times per year. Toxic to pets. Remove dried lower leaves and detach offsets once they are about a third the size of the parent.

echeveria lola.description: Hybrid echeveria with lavender-pink rosettes; powdery farina. Non-toxic to pets.
echeveria lola.care_tips: Water when soil is dry (every 1-2 weeks). Water at base to avoid farina. Bright light preferred. Low humidity fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or dried leaves from the base. Prune leggy stems to promote compact growth. Allow cuts to callus before replanting.

echeveria perle von n rnberg.description: Also known as: PVN. Popular echeveria with purple-pink rosettes and powdery farina; classic succulent. Non-toxic to pets.
echeveria perle von n rnberg.care_tips: Water when soil is dry (every 1-2 weeks). Water at base to avoid farina. Bright light enhances color. Low humidity fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or dried leaves from the base. Prune leggy stems to promote compact growth. Allow cuts to callus before replanting.

haworthia cooperi.description: Also known as: Window plant. Haworthia with translucent "window" leaves; tolerates lower light than most succulents. Non-toxic to pets.
haworthia cooperi.care_tips: Water when soil is dry (every 1-2 weeks). Bright indirect to medium light—tolerates lower light. Medium humidity fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

succulents.description: Drought-adapted plants with water-storing leaves, need excellent drainage.
succulents.care_tips: Water when soil is completely dry (every 1-3 weeks depending on conditions). Water deeply but infrequently. Excellent drainage is essential - use cactus/succulent mix. Bright indirect to direct light preferred. Low humidity is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with succulent fertilizer at half strength. Repot every 2-3 years. Drought-adapted plants with water-storing leaves. Remove dead or dried leaves from the base. Prune leggy stems to promote compact growth. Allow cuts to callus before replanting.

scientific_names: Kroenleinia grusonii (syn. Echinocactus grusonii) (Golden barrel cactus)
barrel cactus.description: Also known as: Golden barrel cactus. Round, barrel-shaped cacti that can grow quite large, very low-maintenance.
barrel cactus.care_tips: Water when soil is completely dry (every 3-4 weeks in summer, less in winter). Very drought tolerant. Full sun to bright indirect light preferred. Low humidity is fine. Fertilize 2-3 times per year during growing season with cactus fertilizer at quarter strength. Well-draining soil essential. Can grow quite large. Repot every 3-5 years. Very low-maintenance. Handle with care - sharp spines. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

cacti.description: Desert plants in the Cactaceae family with spines and areoles, need excellent drainage and bright light.
cacti.care_tips: Water when soil is completely dry (every 3-6 weeks). Water deeply but infrequently. Reduce significantly or stop watering in winter dormancy (November-February). Bright direct light essential - full sun preferred. Low humidity preferred. Fertilize 2-3 times per year during growing season with cactus fertilizer at quarter strength. Excellent drainage essential. Repot every 3-5 years. Handle with care - spines are sharp. Remove any dead or damaged pads or segments with clean, sharp tools. Minimal pruning needed.

christmas cactus.description: Also known as: True Christmas cactus. Forest cactus that blooms around Christmas, requires cool temperatures and reduced light to flower, has rounded leaf segments.
christmas cactus.care_tips: Keep soil slightly moist spring through summer. Reduce watering in fall (September-October) to encourage blooms - this triggers bud formation. More frequent watering than desert cacti. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct hot sun. High humidity (50-60%) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Cool temperatures (15-18°C) and reduced light in fall encourage flowering. Repot every 2-3 years. Rounded leaf segments distinguish from Thanksgiving cactus. Remove any dead or damaged pads or segments with clean, sharp tools. Minimal pruning ne

scientific_names: Rhipsalidopsis gaertneri (syn. Rhipsalidopsis gaertneri (syn. Hatiora gaertneri)
easter cactus.description: Forest cactus that blooms in spring, with rounded leaf segments.
easter cactus.care_tips: Keep soil slightly moist spring through summer. Reduce watering in winter (December-February) to encourage spring blooms. Bright indirect light preferred. High humidity (50-60%) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Cool temperatures in winter encourage flowering. Repot every 2-3 years. Rounded leaf segments. Blooms in spring (Easter time). Remove spent flowers after blooming. Prune segments to shape after flowering.

easter lily cactus.description: Round or columnar cacti that produce large, funnel-shaped flowers in white, pink, or red, often opening at night.
easter lily cactus.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright light with several hours of direct sun. Low humidity is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with cactus fertilizer. Large flowers bloom spring through summer. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

orchid cactus.description: Epiphytic woodland cactus with flat, leaf-like stems that produce spectacular nocturnal flowers in many colors.
orchid cactus.care_tips: Keep soil slightly moist spring through summer; reduce watering in winter. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid strong midday sun. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Epiphytic—use well-draining mix. Repot every 2-3 years. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

forest cacti.description: Epiphytic cacti native to tropical forests, require different care from desert cacti with higher humidity needs.
forest cacti.care_tips: Keep soil slightly moist spring through summer. More frequent watering than desert cacti. Reduce watering in fall for bloom induction. Bright indirect light preferred; some direct morning sun is fine. High humidity (50-60%) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Epiphytic cacti native to tropical forests. Repot every 2-3 years in well-draining mix. Different care from desert cacti. Remove any dead or damaged pads or segments with clean, sharp tools. Minimal pruning needed.

chin cactus.description: Also known as: Moon cactus. Small, round cacti with chin-like notches above each areole; Moon cactus is a colorful grafted form.
chin cactus.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid intense direct sun. Low to medium humidity is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with cactus fertilizer. Moon cactus is grafted—keep colorful top from burning. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

pincushion cactus.description: Compact, round cacti with spiral tubercles and a crown of small flowers in spring.
pincushion cactus.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect or direct light preferred. Low to medium humidity is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with cactus fertilizer. Flowers form a ring around the crown in spring. Well-draining soil essential. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

old lady cactus.description: Round, woolly cactus covered in white hairs, produces pink flowers.
old lady cactus.care_tips: Water when soil is completely dry (every 3-4 weeks in summer, less in winter). Very drought tolerant. Bright indirect to direct light preferred. Low humidity is fine. Fertilize 2-3 times per year during growing season with cactus fertilizer. Well-draining soil essential. Covered in white hairs giving woolly appearance. Produces pink flowers in spring. Repot every 3-5 years. Compact, round growth habit. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

bunny ears cactus.description: Flat-padded cactus with glochids (tiny barbed spines) instead of large spines; handle with care.
bunny ears cactus.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect to direct light preferred. Low to medium humidity is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with cactus fertilizer. Handle with extreme care—glochids detach easily and are very irritating. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

ball cactus.description: Round, ribbed cacti that produce yellow or golden flowers from the crown.
ball cactus.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect or direct light preferred. Low to medium humidity is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with cactus fertilizer. Golden flowers bloom spring through summer. Well-draining soil essential. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

prickly pear.description: Flat-padded cacti in the Opuntia genus, can produce edible fruit, very low-maintenance.
prickly pear.care_tips: Water when soil is completely dry (every 3-4 weeks in summer, less in winter). Very drought tolerant. Full sun to bright indirect light preferred. Low humidity is fine. Fertilize 2-3 times per year during growing season with cactus fertilizer. Well-draining soil essential. Flat, pad-like stems. Can produce edible fruit. Repot every 3-5 years. Handle with extreme care - tiny glochids are very irritating. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

scientific_names: Aporocactus flagelliformis (syn. Disocactus flagelliformis; Rat tail cactus)
rat tail cactus.description: Trailing cactus with long, thin stems covered in spines, produces bright pink or red flowers.
rat tail cactus.care_tips: Water when soil is completely dry (every 2-3 weeks in summer, less in winter). More water-tolerant than some cacti. Bright indirect to direct light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with cactus fertilizer at half strength. Trailing growth habit - perfect for hanging baskets. Produces bright pink or red flowers. Repot every 2-3 years. Long, thin trailing stems. Remove any dead or damaged pads or segments with clean, sharp tools. Minimal pruning needed.

rhipsalis.description: Epiphytic jungle cacti with branching, often pendulous stems; spineless and ideal for hanging baskets.
rhipsalis.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct sun. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Epiphytic—well-draining mix. Trailing habit suits hanging baskets. Repot every 2-3 years. Remove any dead or damaged pads or segments with clean, sharp tools. Minimal pruning needed.

saguaro cactus.description: Also known as: Giant cactus. Iconic columnar cactus of the Sonoran Desert, growing up to 12m tall with arm-like branches. Extremely slow-growing; takes 10 years to reach 2.5cm.
saguaro cactus.care_tips: Water deeply but infrequently — every 2-4 weeks in summer, monthly or less in winter. Requires full sun and excellent drainage. Use cactus mix with extra perlite. Extremely slow grower; indoor specimens rarely exceed 30cm. Tolerates extreme heat but protect from frost below -5°C. Fertilize once in spring with dilute cactus fertilizer. Non-toxic to pets. Remove any dead or damaged pads or segments with clean, sharp tools. Minimal pruning needed.

star cactus.description: Small, round cactus with star-shaped pattern, very slow-growing and rare.
star cactus.care_tips: Water when soil is completely dry (every 3-4 weeks in summer, very little in winter). Very drought tolerant. Bright indirect to direct light preferred. Low humidity is fine. Fertilize sparingly (2-3 times per year) with cactus fertilizer at quarter strength. Well-draining soil essential. Very slow-growing. Star-shaped pattern on top. Produces yellow flowers. Repot every 3-5 years. Rare and protected in wild. Remove spent flowers and keep the body free of debris.

thanksgiving cactus.description: Also known as: Crab cactus. Forest cactus that blooms in late fall, similar to Christmas cactus but with pointed leaf segments.
thanksgiving cactus.care_tips: Keep soil slightly moist spring through summer. Reduce watering in fall (September-October) to encourage blooms. Bright indirect light preferred. High humidity (50-60%) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Pointed leaf segments distinguish from Christmas cactus. Blooms in late fall (Thanksgiving time). Repot every 2-3 years. Remove spent flowers after blooming. Prune segments to shape after flowering.

scientific_names: various cultivars with different flower colors
african violets.description: Compact flowering plants in the Gesneriaceae family with fuzzy leaves and colorful blooms, avoid getting water on leaves. Includes various cultivars with different flower colors, single, double, or ruffled flowers.
african violets.care_tips: Keep soil lightly moist. Always water from bottom or avoid wetting leaves - water on leaves causes permanent spots. Use room temperature water. Bright indirect light preferred; direct sun burns leaves. High humidity (50-60%) preferred. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with African violet fertilizer to encourage continuous blooms. Repot annually in spring. Remove spent flowers. Crown rot is common - avoid overwatering. Remove spent flowers and yellowing leaves to encourage reblooming.

flamingo flower.description: Classic tropical houseplant with glossy, heart-shaped spathes in red, pink, white, or coral that bloom year-round with proper care.
flamingo flower.care_tips: Water when top 2-3 cm of soil is dry; keep slightly moist but never soggy. Bright indirect light—direct sun bleaches spathes. High humidity (60%+) preferred; mist regularly or use a pebble tray. Well-draining, chunky aroid mix. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with quarter-strength phosphorus-rich fertilizer to promote flowering. Wipe leaves to remove dust. Toxic to pets (calcium oxalate crystals). Remove any rotting roots and damaged leaves promptly.

angel wing begonia.description: Cane begonias with wing-shaped spotted leaves and pendent flower clusters in red, pink, or white.
angel wing begonia.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred; some morning sun is fine. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer. Prune leggy stems to encourage bushiness. Toxic to pets. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container.

begonia ferox.description: Dramatic rhizomatous begonia with dark, textured leaves covered in cone-shaped black spikes (bullae). One of the most unusual-looking houseplants available. Native to limestone caves in Vietnam.
begonia ferox.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry; avoid getting water on leaves. Bright indirect light — avoid direct sun. High humidity (60-70%) essential for best spike development. Extremely well-draining, chunite soil mix (perlite, bark, pumice). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with dilute balanced fertilizer. Grows naturally on limestone — benefits from slightly alkaline water or occasional crushed oyster shell in soil. Small white flowers appear in clusters. Cool to intermediate temperatures preferred — struggles above 27°C. Sensitive to root rot. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage pr

polka dot begonia.description: Cane begonia with silver-spotted leaves, red undersides, and white flower clusters. The most commonly sold form is the 'Wightii' cultivar.
polka dot begonia.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct sun. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer. Leaf spots fade in low light. Toxic to pets. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

rex begonia.description: Rhizomatous begonia grown for its spectacular, multicolored foliage in swirling patterns of silver, purple, pink, red, and green. One of the most ornamental houseplant species.
rex begonia.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist, never let dry completely. High humidity (60-70%) preferred — use pebble tray or humidifier. Bright indirect light maintains vibrant leaf colors; direct sun fades colors. Avoid wetting leaves which causes powdery mildew and spots. Water from bottom when possible. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Repot every 1-2 years. Ensure good air circulation. May go dormant in winter — reduce watering. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

aechmea bromeliads.description: Also known as: Silver vase plant. Bromeliads with pink flower spikes and silver-banded leaves.
aechmea bromeliads.care_tips: Keep central cup (tank) filled with water at all times. Water soil when dry. Change cup water monthly to prevent stagnation and mosquito breeding. Bright indirect light preferred. High humidity (50-60%) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall by adding diluted fertilizer to cup water. Flower spike lasts months. After flowering, plant produces offsets (pups) - parent plant dies but pups can be separated and repotted. Remove the spent flower spike and dead outer leaves; separate pups once they are a third the size of the parent.

guzmania bromeliads.description: Colorful bromeliads with bright, long-lasting flower spikes.
guzmania bromeliads.care_tips: Keep central cup (tank) filled with water at all times. Water soil when dry. Change cup water monthly to prevent stagnation. Bright indirect light preferred. High humidity (50-60%) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall by adding diluted fertilizer to cup water. Bright, long-lasting flower spikes. After flowering, plant produces offsets (pups) - parent dies but pups can be separated and repotted. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

neoregelia bromeliad.description: Tank bromeliads with colorful central cups that hold water. Leaves form a rosette; flowers emerge from the center. Epiphytic in nature.
neoregelia bromeliad.care_tips: Keep central cup (tank) filled with water - change weekly to prevent stagnation. Water soil when nearly dry. Bright indirect light. High humidity (50%+) preferred. Fertilize monthly by adding diluted fertilizer to tank. Use well-draining orchid or bromeliad mix. Good air circulation. Pup (offset) removal after flowering. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

bromeliads.description: Tropical plants in the Bromeliaceae family with rosette growth and central cups (tanks) that hold water.
bromeliads.care_tips: Keep central cup (tank) filled with water at all times. Water soil when dry. Change cup water monthly to prevent stagnation and mosquito breeding. Bright indirect light preferred. High humidity (50-60%) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall by adding diluted fertilizer to cup water. After flowering, plant produces offsets (pups) - parent dies but pups can be separated. Most bloom once then produce pups. Remove the spent flower spike and dead outer leaves; separate pups once they are a third the size of the parent.

clivia.description: Shade-tolerant flowering plant with strap-like leaves and striking orange or yellow flower clusters.
clivia.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Needs a cool, dry rest period (6-8 weeks in fall) with minimal watering to trigger blooming. Bright indirect light preferred; tolerates low light. Keep slightly pot-bound to encourage flowering. Fertilize monthly spring through summer. Toxic to pets. Remove spent flower stalks and yellowing leaves at the base.

coffee plant.description: Glossy-leaved shrub that can produce white flowers and red coffee cherries indoors.
coffee plant.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred. High humidity (50-60%+) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer. Berries need several years to ripen. Acidic soil preferred. Toxic to pets. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Prune lightly in spring to maintain shape.

crown of thorns.description: Thorny succulent shrub with colorful bracts that bloom year-round in bright light.
crown of thorns.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect to direct light preferred. Low humidity is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer. Milky sap is irritating—handle with care. Toxic to pets. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

cyclamen.description: Tuberous flowering plants in the Primulaceae family with heart-shaped leaves and upswept flowers.
cyclamen.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist but not soggy. Water from bottom to avoid wetting leaves and crown. Cool temperatures (60-65°F) extend bloom time. Bright indirect light preferred. Medium humidity (50%) preferred. Fertilize every 2 weeks during flowering with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Goes dormant after flowering - reduce watering and allow foliage to die back. Repot when dormant. Upswept, colorful flowers. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

cymbidium.description: Also known as: Boat orchid. Terrestrial and semi-terrestrial orchids in the Orchidaceae family with grassy leaves and tall sprays of long-lasting waxy flowers in winter and spring; the big hybrids are florist staples, while the small Chinese species have been cultivated for their fragrance for over two thousand years.
cymbidium.care_tips: Water thoroughly when the top of the mix dries, roughly weekly in summer and every 10-14 days in winter; the pseudobulbs should never shrivel. Bright light, more than most orchids, with light shade from midday summer sun; leaves should be yellow-green, not dark green. Grow at 10-27°C, and give a drop to 10-14°C on autumn nights to set flower spikes; standard hybrids will not bloom in constantly warm rooms. Medium humidity (40-60%). Feed every 2 weeks spring to summer with a balanced orchid fertilizer, switching to a low-nitrogen formula in late summer. Pot in a coarse bark mix in a snug pot; r

gardenia.description: Also known as: Cape jasmine. Fragrant flowering shrubs in the Rubiaceae family with glossy leaves and white blooms, require high humidity.
gardenia.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist but well-drained (water when top inch is dry). Acidic soil essential (pH 5.0-6.5). Bright indirect light preferred; some direct morning sun is fine. High humidity (60%+) essential - use humidifier. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks spring through fall with acid-loving plant fertilizer. Very fragrant white flowers. Prune after flowering. Can be finicky - requires consistent care. Repot every 2-3 years. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

gerbera daisy.description: Also known as: Transvaal Daisy, Barberton Daisy. Cheerful flowering perennial from South Africa with large, vibrant daisy-like blooms in many colors.
gerbera daisy.care_tips: Bright indirect light or morning sun with afternoon shade. Water when top inch of soil dries — avoid wetting the crown to prevent rot. Well-draining, slightly acidic soil (pH 5.5-6.5). Keep at 15-21°C for best flowering; avoid temperatures above 29°C. Deadhead spent blooms to encourage continuous flowering. Non-toxic to pets.

gloxinia.description: Also known as: Florist's Gloxinia, Sinningia. Tuberous flowering plants in the Gesneriaceae family with velvety leaves and large, bell-shaped flowers.
gloxinia.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist but not soggy. Water from bottom to avoid wetting leaves. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct sun. High humidity (60%+) preferred. Fertilize every 2 weeks during flowering with high-phosphorus fertilizer. Goes dormant after flowering - reduce watering and allow foliage to die back. Repot when dormant. Large, bell-shaped velvety flowers. Velvety leaves. Deadhead spent blooms; once the foliage dies back, store the tuber dry until spring.

goldfish plant.description: Trailing gesneriad with waxy, tubular flowers resembling goldfish in orange, red, or yellow; ideal for hanging baskets.
goldfish plant.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct sun. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Cooler, drier winter rest encourages spring blooming. Prune after flowering to maintain shape. Non-toxic to pets. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container.

tropical hibiscus.description: Also known as: Chinese hibiscus. Showy shrub with large, colorful trumpet flowers that last one day but bloom repeatedly.
tropical hibiscus.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect to direct light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize weekly spring through fall with bloom fertilizer. Bud drop from stress or pests. Non-toxic to pets. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

hoya carnosa.description: Also known as: Wax plant. Classic wax plant with thick, waxy leaves and fragrant star-shaped flowers.
hoya carnosa.care_tips: Water when most of pot is dry (every 1-2 weeks). More drought tolerant than many houseplants. Bright indirect light preferred; some direct morning sun encourages flowering. Medium humidity (40-50%) is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Don't remove spent flower stems (peduncles) - they rebloom. Repot every 2-3 years. Fragrant star-shaped flowers. Can trail or climb. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

hoya kerrii.description: Heart-shaped hoya often sold as single leaves, slow-growing but charming.
hoya kerrii.care_tips: Water when most of pot is dry (every 1-2 weeks). Bright indirect light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%) is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Very slow-growing - single leaves may never grow into full plant. If you have a stem cutting (not just leaf), it will grow. Repot every 2-3 years. Charming heart-shaped leaves. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

hoyas.description: Epiphytic vines in the Apocynaceae family with waxy leaves and fragrant star-shaped flowers, also called wax plants.
hoyas.care_tips: Water when most of pot is dry (every 1-2 weeks). More drought tolerant than many houseplants. Reduce watering in winter when growth slows. Bright indirect light preferred; some direct morning sun encourages flowering. Medium humidity (40-50%) is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Don't remove spent flower stems - they rebloom. Repot every 2-3 years. Fragrant star-shaped flowers. Can trail or climb. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

ixora.description: Also known as: Flame of the woods. Tropical shrub producing dense clusters of tiny star-shaped flowers in vibrant red, orange, yellow, or pink.
ixora.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist during growing season; reduce in winter. Bright direct to indirect light for best flowering. Medium humidity preferred. Acidic soil essential (pH 5.0-6.0)—iron chlorosis (yellow leaves) in alkaline soil. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with acid-forming fertilizer. Prune after flowering to maintain shape.

jasmine.description: Also known as: Pink jasmine. Fragrant flowering vines in the Oleaceae family, popular for their sweet-smelling blooms.
jasmine.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist (water when top inch is dry). Bright indirect to direct light preferred - more light encourages flowering. High humidity (60%+) preferred. Fertilize every 2 weeks spring through fall with high-phosphorus fertilizer to encourage flowering. Provide support for climbing. Prune after flowering. Very fragrant flowers. Can be grown as houseplant or outdoor in warm climates. Repot every 1-2 years.

kalanchoe.description: Also known as: Flaming Katy, Florist Kalanchoe. Colorful succulent houseplants with clusters of long-lasting blooms in red, pink, orange, yellow, and white. The most popular species is K. blossfeldiana.
kalanchoe.care_tips: Water when soil is completely dry — very drought tolerant. Bright indirect to direct light. Low humidity preferred. Well-draining succulent mix. Fertilize monthly during growing season. K. blossfeldiana needs short days (14+ hours darkness) for 6 weeks to rebloom. Deadhead spent flowers. Toxic to pets — contains cardiac glycosides.

lipstick plant.description: Also known as: Lipstick vine. Trailing gesneriad with tubular red flowers emerging from dark calyxes like lipstick.
lipstick plant.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred; some morning sun encourages blooms. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Trailing habit suits hanging baskets. Non-toxic to pets. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Prune back after flowering to keep it bushy; it blooms on new growth.

mandevilla.description: Vining plant with trumpet flowers in pink, red, or white; blooms from spring through fall.
mandevilla.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect to direct light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize weekly spring through fall with bloom fertilizer. Provide trellis or support for climbing. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

medinilla.description: Also known as: Rose Grape. Dramatic tropical houseplant with large, leathery leaves and cascading clusters of pink flowers that can last for months.
medinilla.care_tips: Water when top 2-3 cm of soil is dry; reduce watering in winter. Bright indirect light—avoid direct sun which scorches leaves. High humidity (60%+) essential; mist daily or use a humidifier. Use well-draining, slightly acidic potting mix. Fertilize every 2 weeks spring through summer with half-strength balanced fertilizer. Needs a cool dry rest period (16-18°C) in winter to trigger reblooming. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

slipper orchid.description: Also known as: Lady's slipper orchid. Terrestrial orchids prized for their distinctive pouch-shaped lip that traps pollinating insects, with blooms in rich earth tones, greens, and dramatic spotted or striped patterns.
slipper orchid.care_tips: Keep potting mix evenly moist but never soggy; water when top layer feels slightly dry. Medium indirect light—no direct sun; mottled-leaf types tolerate lower light than plain-leaf types. High humidity (60%+) essential. Use fine-grade bark orchid mix with perlite and sphagnum; they are terrestrial, not epiphytic like most orchids. Fertilize weakly every 2 weeks with balanced orchid fertilizer (flush monthly to prevent salt buildup). Do not mist water into the pouch—causes rot. Repot every 1-2 years when medium breaks down. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

peace lilies.description: Aroids with white spathes and dark green foliage, excellent air purifiers, droop dramatically when thirsty as a watering indicator. Includes various cultivars ranging from compact to large.
peace lilies.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist but not soggy, water when leaves droop slightly. Fertilize every 6-8 weeks during growing season. Remove spent flowers to encourage new blooms. Repot when roots fill container, typically every 1-2 years. Toxic to pets and humans if ingested; causes mouth irritation. Remove any rotting roots and damaged leaves promptly.

scientific_names: various hybrid cultivars in many colors
phalaenopsis orchids.description: Also known as: Moth orchid. Moth orchids, most common and beginner-friendly orchid genus in the Orchidaceae family with long-lasting blooms. Available in various colors.
phalaenopsis orchids.care_tips: Soak roots weekly for 15-20 minutes, then allow to dry between waterings. Never let sit in water. Avoid getting water in crown (center) which causes fatal crown rot. Use well-draining orchid bark mix, never regular potting soil. Bright indirect light preferred; direct sun burns leaves. High humidity (50-70%) preferred. Fertilize weekly spring through fall with orchid fertilizer at quarter strength. Repot every 1-2 years when bark breaks down. Blooms last 2-3 months. Most beginner-friendly orchid. After blooming, cut the spent spike above a node to encourage a secondary spike, or at the base on

poinsettia.description: Also known as: Christmas star, Mexican flame leaf. Winter-flowering shrub in the Euphorbiaceae family whose showy red, pink, white, or marbled bracts surround tiny yellow flowers; the classic holiday houseplant.
poinsettia.care_tips: Water when the top inch of soil is dry; never let the pot sit in water or in a sealed foil sleeve. Bright indirect light for at least 6 hours a day. Keep at 18-24°C and away from cold drafts, radiators, and windowpanes; chilling below 10°C drops leaves. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly at half strength only while in active growth; stop while bracts are colored. Bracts color only after 14 hours of total darkness nightly for 8-10 weeks from early autumn. Cut stems back to 10-15 cm in spring to rebloom. Mildly toxic to pets; may cause GI upset, and the milky sap can irritate skin. Prun

stephanotis.description: Also known as: Madagascar jasmine, Wax flower. Twining vine with waxy, tubular white flowers of exquisite fragrance, traditionally used in wedding bouquets.
stephanotis.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist spring through fall; reduce in winter but don't let it dry out completely. Bright indirect light—some morning sun beneficial. High humidity (50-60%+) preferred. Well-draining potting mix. Fertilize every 2 weeks spring through summer with half-strength balanced fertilizer. Provide a trellis or hoop for climbing. Avoid moving once buds form—bud drop is common from changes in position or light. Cool winter rest (13-16°C) promotes flowering. Mildly toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

cape primrose.description: Gesneriad with strappy leaves and trumpet flowers in blue, purple, pink, or white.
cape primrose.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct sun. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Long blooming season. Non-toxic to pets. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

tuberous begonias.description: Flowering begonias grown from tubers, often with large showy blooms in various colors.
tuberous begonias.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist during active growth (spring through fall). Reduce watering significantly during dormancy period (winter) when leaves die back. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct hot sun. High humidity (50-60%) preferred. Fertilize every 2 weeks during active growth with high-phosphorus fertilizer to encourage blooms. Store tubers dry in winter. Repot tubers in spring. Large showy blooms in various colors. Toxic to pets. Deadhead spent blooms to encourage reblooming. Prune leggy growth after flowering season.

zebra plant.description: Tropical plant with bold white-veined leaves and showy yellow bract flowers; requires consistent moisture and high humidity.
zebra plant.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist but not soggy. Bright indirect light essential. High humidity (60-70%) required—use pebble tray or humidifier. Fertilize monthly spring through fall. Prone to leaf drop if care is inconsistent. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

calathea freddie.description: Compact prayer plant with light green leaves featuring bold dark green striping along the veins; folds leaves upward at night.
calathea freddie.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist but never soggy; use filtered or distilled water as sensitive to minerals and chlorine. Low to bright indirect light—no direct sun which scorches leaves. High humidity essential (60%+); use humidifier or pebble tray. Fertilize monthly spring through fall at quarter strength. Sensitive to drafts and temperature changes. Non-toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

calathea makoyana.description: Also known as: Peacock plant, Cathedral windows. Prayer plant with oval leaves featuring peacock-like patterns, leaves fold up at night.
calathea makoyana.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist but not soggy. High humidity (60%+) essential - use humidifier or pebble tray. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct sun. Use distilled or filtered water to prevent leaf browning. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Leaves fold up at night (prayer plant behavior). Repot every 1-2 years. Peacock-like pattern on leaves. Non-toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

calathea medallion.description: Popular prayer plant with dark green leaves and purple undersides, requires high humidity, leaves fold up at night.
calathea medallion.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist, never let dry. High humidity (60-70%) essential - use humidifier or pebble tray. Use only distilled or filtered water to prevent leaf browning from minerals. Bright indirect light preferred; direct sun burns leaves. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Leaves fold up at night (nyctinasty). Repot every 1-2 years. Wipe leaves monthly. Sensitive to tap water and low humidity. Non-toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

calathea musaica.description: Stunning prayer plant with an intricate mosaic-like network pattern on its leaves that resembles stained glass or circuit boards, one of the most visually complex leaf patterns in nature.
calathea musaica.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged; very sensitive to drying out. Bright indirect light—no direct sun. High humidity (60%+) essential; leaf edges brown quickly in dry air. Use filtered or distilled water—sensitive to fluoride and chlorine in tap water. Well-draining, peat-based mix. Fertilize monthly spring through fall at quarter strength. Leaves fold up at night (nyctinasty). Non-toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

calathea orbifolia.description: Also known as: Round-leaved calathea. Large prayer plant with silver-striped round leaves, requires high humidity, leaves fold up at night (nyctinasty).
calathea orbifolia.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist, never let dry. High humidity (60-70%) essential - use humidifier. Use only distilled or filtered water to prevent leaf browning. Bright indirect light preferred; direct sun fades silver stripes. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Leaves fold up at night (nyctinasty). Repot every 1-2 years. One of the larger calathea varieties. Wipe large leaves monthly. Non-toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

pin stripe calathea.description: Also known as: Pin-stripe plant. Elegant prayer plant with dark green, glossy leaves adorned with thin pink or white pinstripes that fade to cream with age.
pin stripe calathea.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist; water when the top inch feels slightly dry. Medium indirect light is ideal — avoid direct sun, which scorches the delicate leaves. Maintain humidity above 60%; mist regularly or use a humidifier. Use filtered, distilled, or rainwater to prevent brown leaf edges from mineral sensitivity. Fertilize monthly during the growing season with a diluted balanced liquid fertilizer. Non-toxic to pets. Trim brown leaf edges with clean scissors. Remove yellowing leaves at the stem. Prune leggy stems to encourage fullness.

scientific_names: Goeppertia insignis (syn. Calathea lancifolia; Rattlesnake plant)
calathea rattlesnake.description: Prayer plant with wavy, patterned leaves resembling a rattlesnake's tail.
calathea rattlesnake.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist, never let dry. High humidity (60-70%) essential - use humidifier. Use distilled or filtered water to prevent leaf browning. Bright indirect light preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Wavy, patterned leaves resembling rattlesnake's tail. Repot every 1-2 years. Wipe leaves monthly. Sensitive to tap water and low humidity. Non-toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

scientific_names: G. roseopicta 'Dottie' (nearly black leaves with pink outline)
calathea roseopicta.description: Also known as: Rose painted calathea. Prayer plant with oval leaves featuring a bold pink or cream border on dark green, with purple undersides. Multiple popular cultivars.
calathea roseopicta.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is slightly dry; keep consistently moist. Use filtered water. Medium indirect light preferred. High humidity (60%+) essential — brown leaf edges indicate low humidity. Non-toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

calathea vittata.description: Prayer plant with delicate white pinstripes on bright green, elliptical leaves. More compact than Calathea ornata with finer, more numerous stripes.
calathea vittata.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is slightly dry; keep consistently moist but not soggy. Use filtered water — sensitive to fluoride and chlorine. Medium indirect light; direct sun scorches leaves. High humidity (60%+) essential. Non-toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

scientific_names: Goeppertia lietzei 'White Fusion' (syn. Calathea lietzei 'White Fusion')
calathea white fusion.description: Prayer plant with variegated leaves in white, green, and lavender; leaves fold up at night.
calathea white fusion.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist, never let dry. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct sun. High humidity (60%+) essential—variegation reverts in low humidity. Use distilled or filtered water to prevent leaf browning. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Non-toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

calathea white star.description: Prayer plant with bold white stripes on dark green leaves; leaves fold up at night.
calathea white star.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist, never let dry. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct sun. High humidity (60%+) preferred. Use distilled or filtered water to prevent leaf browning. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Non-toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

scientific_names: Goeppertia zebrina (syn. Calathea zebrina; Zebra plant)
zebra calathea.description: Prayer plant with velvety stripes alternating dark and light green; leaves fold up at night.
zebra calathea.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist, never let dry. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct sun. Medium to high humidity (50-60%). Use distilled or filtered water to prevent leaf browning. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Leaves fold at night. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Non-toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

ctenanthe.description: Also known as: Fishbone prayer plant. Prayer plants in the Marantaceae family with patterned leaves that fold up at night, more tolerant than some prayer plants.
ctenanthe.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist but not soggy. High humidity (60%+) preferred - more tolerant than some prayer plants. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct sun. Use distilled or filtered water to prevent leaf browning. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Leaves fold up at night (prayer plant behavior). Patterned leaves. Repot every 1-2 years. Trim brown leaf edges with clean scissors. Remove yellowing leaves at the stem. Prune leggy stems to encourage fullness.

scientific_names: M. leuconeura var. erythroneura (Red prayer plant)
maranta prayer plant.description: Also known as: Herringbone plant. Classic prayer plant with red-veined leaves that fold up at night.
maranta prayer plant.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist, never let dry. High humidity (60-70%) preferred - use humidifier or pebble tray. Use distilled or filtered water to prevent leaf browning. Bright indirect light preferred; direct sun burns leaves. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Red-veined leaves fold up at night (nyctinasty). Repot every 1-2 years. Wipe leaves monthly. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

prayer plants.description: Plants in Marantaceae family with leaves that fold up at night (nyctinasty), require high humidity.
prayer plants.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist, never let dry. High humidity (60-70%) essential - use humidifier. Use only distilled or filtered water to prevent leaf browning from minerals. Bright indirect light preferred; direct sun burns leaves. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Leaves fold up at night (nyctinasty). Repot every 1-2 years. Wipe leaves monthly. Sensitive to tap water, low humidity, and drafts. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

scientific_names: Stromanthe thalia 'Triostar' (syn. S. sanguinea 'Triostar'; Tricolor stromanthe)
stromanthe.description: Prayer plants in the Marantaceae family with colorful, patterned leaves that fold up at night.
stromanthe.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist but not soggy. High humidity (60%+) essential - use humidifier or pebble tray. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct sun. Use distilled or filtered water to prevent leaf browning. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Leaves fold up at night (prayer plant behavior). Colorful, patterned leaves. Repot every 1-2 years. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

baby s tears.description: Also known as: Mind-your-own-business, Angel's tears. Creeping Mediterranean perennial in the Urticaceae family that forms a dense, bright-green carpet of tiny round leaves; grown as a terrarium and pot-topping houseplant and as a shade groundcover in mild climates.
baby s tears.care_tips: Keep the soil consistently moist but never soggy; it wilts dramatically when dry and usually recovers after watering. Water from below or at the soil line; wet foliage left in the dark can rot. Bright indirect light; direct sun scorches it. Comfortable at 10-24°C; frost kills the top growth outdoors. High humidity (50%+) keeps it lush, which is why it thrives in terrariums. Feed monthly in spring and summer at half strength. Perennial outdoors in zones 9-11, where it can become invasive. Non-toxic to pets. Trim with scissors any time to keep the mat tidy and to stop it smothering neighbors.

rex begonia vine.description: Tropical climbing vine with stunning elongated leaves featuring silver, green, and purple coloring with deep red-purple undersides, not a true begonia despite the common name.
rex begonia vine.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist but not soggy; sensitive to both drought and overwatering. Bright indirect light—direct sun fades the stunning leaf colors. High humidity (60%+) essential—drops leaves rapidly in dry air. Well-draining potting mix. Fertilize monthly spring through fall at half strength. Provide a trellis or moss pole. May go semi-dormant in winter, losing some leaves—reduce watering. Non-toxic to pets. Prune back leggy growth in spring and remove damaged leaves promptly.

dischidia.description: Also known as: String of nickels. Epiphytic succulents related to Hoya, with coin-shaped or heart-shaped leaves; trailing or climbing habit.
dischidia.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Epiphytic—well-draining mix. Trailing habit suits hanging baskets. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

english ivy.description: Classic trailing vine with lobed leaves, can be grown indoors or outdoors.
english ivy.care_tips: Keep soil slightly moist. Cooler temperatures (60-70°F) preferred. Bright indirect light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Prone to spider mites - mist regularly and inspect leaves. Prune to control length. Repot every 1-2 years. Can be grown indoors or outdoors. Toxic to pets.

grape ivy.description: Also known as: Venezuela Treebine. Trailing vine with glossy, grape-like trifoliate leaves. Excellent low-maintenance houseplant that tolerates lower light conditions and adapts well to indoor environments. Can trail from hanging baskets or climb a moss pole.
grape ivy.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Allow to dry between waterings. Bright indirect light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%) is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Prune to control length. Repot every 1-2 years. Easy-care houseplant. Grape-like leaves. Can trail or climb with support.

hoya australis.description: Vining Hoya with waxy, oval leaves and fragrant white flowers with red centers.
hoya australis.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Allow soil to dry between waterings. Repot every 2-3 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

hoya bella.description: Compact, trailing hoya with small, pointed leaves and clusters of star-shaped, fragrant white flowers with pink or purple centers. One of the most popular hoyas for hanging baskets.
hoya bella.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light encourages blooming. Do not remove spent flower stalks (peduncles) — new flowers emerge from the same spurs. Average to high humidity preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through summer. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

hoya callistophylla.description: Distinctive Hoya species with long, pointed leaves featuring prominent dark veining on a light green background, giving a stained-glass appearance. A highly sought-after collector Hoya.
hoya callistophylla.care_tips: Allow soil to dry between waterings. Bright indirect light for best leaf coloring; tolerates medium light. Do not remove flower peduncles as they rebloom from the same stalk. Well-draining aroid or orchid mix with bark and perlite. Fertilize monthly spring through fall. Slow to moderate grower. Leaves develop best venation pattern with good light. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

hoya compacta.description: Hoya carnosa cultivar with twisted, curled leaves creating a rope-like appearance; Hindu rope.
hoya compacta.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Slow-growing. Waxy pink flowers when mature. Repot every 2-3 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

hoya cumingiana.description: Compact Hoya species with small, thick oval leaves and fragrant yellow star-shaped flower clusters. One of the easier Hoyas to bring into bloom.
hoya cumingiana.care_tips: Allow soil to dry out between waterings — water thoroughly when dry. Bright indirect light encourages blooming; tolerates medium light. Do not remove spent flower stalks as new blooms emerge from the same peduncle. Well-draining mix essential — orchid bark, perlite, and peat. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

hoya curtisii.description: Trailing Hoya with small, silver-mottled leaves; ideal for hanging baskets.
hoya curtisii.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Compact growth. Repot every 2-3 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

hoya krimson queen.description: Also known as: Variegated wax plant. Popular variegated Hoya carnosa cultivar with creamy white to pink margins on waxy, semi-succulent leaves.
hoya krimson queen.care_tips: Allow soil to dry out between waterings; water thoroughly when the top 2-3 cm feel dry. Bright indirect light is essential to maintain variegation — some morning sun encourages pink tones on new growth. Use a well-draining, chunky mix with orchid bark and perlite. Maintain 40-60% humidity; tolerates average home humidity. Fertilize monthly in spring and summer with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Do not remove spent flower peduncles, as they rebloom from the same spurs. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

hoya linearis.description: Trailing Hoya with long, narrow, fuzzy leaves; pendulous habit suits hanging baskets.
hoya linearis.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Fragrant white flowers. Repot every 2-3 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

hoya mathilde.description: Compact Hoya with silver-flecked leaves; hybrid of H. serpens × H. carnosa.
hoya mathilde.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Slow-growing. Repot every 2-3 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

hoya obovata.description: Large, round-leaved Hoya with thick, often silver-splashed foliage. Splash markings are the standard form. Produces fragrant star-shaped flower clusters.
hoya obovata.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Pink flowers in clusters. Repot every 2-3 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

hoya pubicalyx.description: Fast-growing Hoya with silver-flecked leaves and fragrant dark pink or red flowers.
hoya pubicalyx.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Prolific bloomer. Repot every 2-3 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

hoya wayetii.description: Trailing hoya with narrow, elongated leaves edged in red or dark maroon, producing clusters of fragrant star-shaped flowers when mature.
hoya wayetii.care_tips: Allow soil to dry mostly between waterings (every 1-2 weeks). Bright indirect light preferred—some direct morning sun enhances leaf color. Medium humidity (40-50%) fine. Well-draining mix with perlite and orchid bark. Fertilize monthly spring through fall at half strength. Don't remove old flower stems (peduncles)—they rebloom. Let it become slightly rootbound for flowering. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

philodendron brasil.description: Also known as: Lemon-lime philodendron. Variegated heart-leaf philodendron with green and yellow-chartreuse leaves, easy-care trailing plant.
philodendron brasil.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Very forgiving of inconsistent care. Bright indirect light maintains variegation; tolerates low light but may lose variegation. Medium humidity (40-50%) is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Fast-growing trailing plant. Prune to control length. Repot every 1-2 years. Green and yellow-chartreuse variegation. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

purple passion plant.description: Also known as: Velvet plant, Purple velvet plant, Gynura. Trailing houseplant in the Asteraceae family whose green leaves are covered in iridescent purple hairs that glow in bright light; the small orange flowers smell unpleasant and are usually pinched off.
purple passion plant.care_tips: Water when the top 2-3 cm of soil is dry; keep slightly moist but never soggy, and water the soil rather than the fuzzy leaves, which spot and rot when wet. Bright indirect light keeps the purple intense; direct sun scorches and low light turns it green. Comfortable at 16-27°C; keep above 13°C. Medium humidity (40-60%). Feed every 2-4 weeks in spring and summer at half strength. Well-draining, peat-based potting mix. Aphids and spider mites hide in the hairs, so inspect often. Short-lived; take cuttings every year or two to replace leggy plants. Non-toxic to pets. Pinch stem tips regularly to

scindapsus.description: Also known as: Silver pothos. Trailing aroids often called satin pothos, with silvery-splotched leaves, easy-care houseplants.
scindapsus.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Very forgiving of inconsistent care. Bright indirect light maintains silvery variegation; tolerates low light. Medium humidity (40-50%) is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Trailing growth habit. Prune to control length. Repot every 1-2 years. Silvery-splotched leaves. Often called satin pothos but not a true pothos. Mildly toxic to pets -- causes mouth and skin irritation.

satin pothos.description: Also known as: Silver satin pothos, Silver vine. Trailing vine with heart-shaped, matte green leaves covered in silvery spots and patches. Not a true pothos despite the common name; belongs to the genus Scindapsus.
satin pothos.care_tips: Water when top 1-2 inches of soil is dry. Bright indirect light brings out the silver markings. Average humidity is fine but higher humidity encouraged for larger leaves. Let dry out slightly between waterings. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

scientific_names: P. australis (name often used in the trade)
swedish ivy.description: Also known as: Swedish begonia, Creeping Charlie (houseplant). Easy trailing houseplant in the Lamiaceae family with glossy, scalloped round leaves and occasional spikes of pale lavender flowers; neither Swedish nor an ivy, it became famous on the White House Oval Office mantel.
swedish ivy.care_tips: Water when the top 2-3 cm of soil is dry; it tolerates occasional neglect and wilts rather than rots. Bright indirect light; some morning sun is fine, but hot afternoon sun scorches. Comfortable at 15-27°C; keep above 10°C. Medium humidity. Feed monthly in spring and summer at half strength. Any well-draining potting mix. Stems root wherever they touch soil and cuttings root in a glass of water within a week. Perennial outdoors only in zones 10-11; grown in hanging baskets elsewhere. Non-toxic to pets. Pinch stem tips often to prevent legginess and cut back hard in spring if it becomes sparse.

tradescantia.description: Also known as: Spiderwort. Fast-growing trailing plants in the Commelinaceae family with colorful striped or solid leaves.
tradescantia.care_tips: Keep soil lightly moist, allow to dry slightly between waterings. Very fast-growing - may need frequent pruning. Bright indirect light maintains vibrant colors; low light causes leggy growth. Medium humidity (40-50%) is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Pinch tips to encourage bushiness. Repot every 1-2 years. Perfect for hanging baskets. Easy to propagate from cuttings. Mildly toxic to pets -- causes mouth and skin irritation.

tradescantia nanouk.description: Trailing plant with thick, striped leaves in pink, green, and cream; compact, upright-then-cascading habit.
tradescantia nanouk.care_tips: Keep soil lightly moist. Bright indirect light maintains pink stripes. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Fast-growing. Mildly toxic to pets -- causes mouth and skin irritation. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Trim trailing stems to desired length. Prune leggy growth to encourage branching. Pinch growing tips for bushier growth.

purple heart.description: Trailing plant with vivid purple foliage and small pink flowers; can be grown indoors or outdoors.
purple heart.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect to direct light enhances purple color. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Mildly toxic to pets -- causes mouth and skin irritation. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

vines trailing plants.description: Houseplants with trailing or climbing growth habits, popular for hanging baskets and shelves. Many are fast-growing and easy to propagate.
vines trailing plants.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Most are forgiving of occasional missed waterings. Bright indirect to medium light preferred — most tolerate lower light but may lose variegation. Medium humidity (40-50%) is fine for most species. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength. Prune to control length and encourage bushier growth — cuttings root easily in water. Provide support (moss pole, trellis) for climbing species. Research specific species for exact requirements.

ficus altissima.description: Tall fig tree with leathery, variegated leaves in shades of green and yellow. Also called council tree. Easier to care for than fiddle leaf fig.
ficus altissima.care_tips: Water when top 1-2 inches of soil is dry. Bright indirect to direct light preferred. Average humidity is fine. Avoid moving frequently — can drop leaves from environmental changes. Fertilize monthly spring through fall. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

ficus audrey.description: The more forgiving cousin of the Fiddle Leaf Fig, with velvety, oval leaves and pale trunk, increasingly popular as a statement houseplant.
ficus audrey.care_tips: Water when top 2-5 cm of soil is dry; more forgiving than Fiddle Leaf Fig but still dislikes soggy soil. Bright indirect light preferred—tolerates some direct morning sun. Medium humidity fine. Well-draining potting mix. Fertilize monthly spring through fall at half strength. Wipe velvety leaves with damp cloth to remove dust. Less prone to leaf drop than Fiddle Leaf Fig but still dislikes being moved. Toxic to pets (milky latex sap). Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

weeping fig.description: Classic indoor tree with arching branches and glossy, pointed leaves; can grow quite tall. Sensitive to relocation and drafts.
weeping fig.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred. Avoid moving once established—leaf drop often follows. Medium humidity preferred; mist if leaves drop. Fertilize monthly spring through fall. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

ficus tineke.description: Variegated rubber plant cultivar with striking cream, green, and pink-edged leaves, more colorful than the standard rubber plant while retaining its easy-care nature.
ficus tineke.care_tips: Water when top 2-5 cm of soil is dry; reduce in winter. Bright indirect light essential to maintain variegation—too little light causes green reversion. Medium humidity fine. Well-draining potting mix. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Wipe large leaves with damp cloth to remove dust. Prune to control height and encourage branching. Rotate regularly for even growth. Toxic to pets (milky latex sap).

chinese banyan.description: Ficus with glossy oval leaves, popular for bonsai; can develop aerial roots.
chinese banyan.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light. Often grown as bonsai. Avoid moving once established. Fertilize monthly spring through fall. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

fiddle leaf fig.description: Also known as: FLF. Popular but finicky ficus with large violin-shaped leaves, requires consistent care and stable environment.
fiddle leaf fig.care_tips: Water when top 2-3 inches of soil is dry. Very sensitive to overwatering and location changes - may drop leaves. Avoid drafts and sudden temperature changes. Bright indirect light essential - rotate regularly for even growth. High humidity (60%+) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Wipe large leaves monthly. Repot every 2-3 years. Popular but finicky - requires consistent care and stable environment. Toxic to pets. Remove old, yellowing, or diseased leaves promptly.

rubber plant.description: Popular ficus with large, glossy dark green or burgundy leaves, can grow into a tree.
rubber plant.care_tips: Water when top 2-3 inches of soil is dry. Avoid overwatering which causes root rot. Sensitive to location changes - may drop leaves when moved. Bright indirect light preferred; some direct morning sun is fine. Medium to high humidity (50-60%) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Wipe large glossy leaves monthly. Prune to control height. Repot every 2-3 years. Can grow into a tree. Toxic to pets.

burgundy rubber plant.description: Ficus elastica cultivar with dark burgundy, nearly black leaves; bold statement plant.
burgundy rubber plant.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred; tolerates low light. Medium humidity (40-50%). Wipe leaves to remove dust. Toxic to pets. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Remove yellowing or damaged leaves promptly.

ruby rubber plant.description: Striking Ficus elastica cultivar with tricolored leaves in deep green, cream, and vivid ruby-pink, especially vibrant on new growth.
ruby rubber plant.care_tips: Water when the top 2-3 cm of soil feel dry; avoid overwatering which causes leaf drop. Bright indirect light is crucial to maintain the pink and cream variegation — low light causes reversion to green. Wipe the large, glossy leaves monthly with a damp cloth to keep them dust-free. Average room humidity is adequate. Fertilize monthly during spring and summer with balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength. Prune to control height and encourage branching. Toxic to pets—the milky sap irritates skin and mouth if chewed.

scientific_names: S. nicolai (Giant white bird of paradise
bird of paradise.description: Also known as: Crane flower. Large tropical plants in the Strelitziaceae family with distinctive bird-like flowers and banana-like leaves.
