Pinch back when young to encourage bushiness. Excellent for containers, hanging baskets, and borders. Plant after last frost. Research variety type for growth habit (upright vs trailing). Annual; grown for one season; no winter watering needed.

moss rose.description: Succulent-like leaves with bright flowers in many colors; thrives in hot, dry, poor soil.
moss rose.care_tips: Water when soil is dry; avoid overwatering. Full sun essential. Sandy, well-draining soil preferred. Fertilize sparingly. Drought tolerant. Self-seeds. Ideal for containers and rock gardens. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

snapdragon.description: Spikes of dragon-mouth flowers in many colors; cool-season annual, excellent for cutting.
snapdragon.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist. Full sun in cool weather; partial shade when hot. Fertilize every 2 weeks. Deadhead to prolong bloom. Cool-season performer—plant in fall or early spring. Stake tall varieties.

statice.description: Also known as: Wavyleaf statice. Papery, brightly colored flower clusters on wiry stems; a classic everlasting flower prized for fresh and dried arrangements.
statice.care_tips: Water sparingly once established; drought-tolerant and sensitive to overwatering. Full sun is essential for strong stems and vibrant flower color. Sandy, well-draining soil mimicking its coastal origins is ideal. Fertilize lightly once or twice during the growing season. Harvest for drying when most florets in a cluster have opened. Excellent salt tolerance; suitable for coastal gardens. Non-toxic to pets. Deadhead regularly to prolong blooming. Pinch growing tips early for bushier plants.

stock.description: Also known as: Common stock. Sweetly fragrant cool-season annual or biennial with dense spikes of double or single flowers in white, pink, purple, red, and cream; prized for its intoxicating clove-like scent.
stock.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil evenly moist; inconsistent watering causes premature bolting. Full sun to partial shade; prefers cool temperatures and performs poorly above 25°C. Rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil is ideal. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with balanced liquid fertilizer during bloom. Plant in early spring or fall for best results; a true cool-season flower that thrives when nights are cool. Deadhead spent blooms to prolong flowering. Night-scented stock (M. longipetala) is a separate species with smaller flowers but an incredible evening fragrance. Non-toxic to pets.

strawflower.description: Also known as: Everlasting, Paper daisy, Golden everlasting. Australian daisy in the Asteraceae family whose papery, straw-textured bracts in gold, orange, red, pink, and white keep their color for years when dried; the classic everlasting for wreaths and dried bouquets.
strawflower.care_tips: Water when the top 3 cm of soil is dry; drought tolerant once established and prone to rot in wet soil. Full sun. Loves heat at 15-32°C; perennial in zones 8-11 and grown as an annual elsewhere. Low humidity preferred, as humid, rainy summers cause mildew and rot. Feed sparingly, monthly at most. Sandy or gritty, well-draining soil of low to moderate fertility. Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; press onto the surface, as light aids germination. For drying, cut stems when the outer bracts have opened but the center is still tight, then hang upside down. Non-toxic to pets. Dead

sunflower.description: Annual and perennial flowers in the Asteraceae family with large, cheerful yellow blooms that follow the sun.
sunflower.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week during growing season. Consistent moisture important during flowering. Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun essential. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Stake tall varieties. Deadhead to encourage side blooms or leave for birds. Large, cheerful yellow blooms. Attract birds and bees. Annual; grown for one season; no winter watering needed.

sweet pea.description: Beloved annual climbing flower prized for its fragrant, ruffled blooms in a wide range of pastel colors. A cottage garden classic.
sweet pea.care_tips: Water regularly — keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged. Full sun with cool roots. Plant early in spring — prefers cool weather and fades in heat. Provide support for climbing. Deadhead spent flowers to prolong blooming. Seeds are toxic if ingested. Toxic to pets.

sweet potato vine.description: Trailing foliage plant in lime, purple, or bronze; grown for leaves, not tubers; fast-growing.
sweet potato vine.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks. Prune to control size; very vigorous. Generally considered non-toxic to pets (ASPCA). Ideal for containers and baskets as spillover.

garden verbena.description: Clusters of small flowers in purple, pink, red, or white; heat-tolerant, butterfly-friendly.
garden verbena.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun essential. Well-draining soil. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks. Deadhead to encourage rebloom. Drought tolerant once established. Trailing or mounding habits. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

viola.description: Also known as: Johnny-jump-up. Small pansy-like flowers with distinctive markings; Johnny-jump-up and violas are cold-tolerant.
viola.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist. Full sun in cool weather; partial shade when hot. Fertilize every 2 weeks. Deadhead to prolong bloom. Cool-season annual. Smaller than pansies but more prolific.

warm season annuals.description: Annual flowers that thrive in summer heat, provide continuous blooms throughout warm season.
warm season annuals.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (daily watering may be needed in hot weather). Water at base to avoid wetting flowers which can cause disease. Consistent moisture prevents wilting. Full sun to partial shade depending on species. Thrive in summer heat. Fertilize every 2 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Deadhead spent flowers to encourage continuous blooms. Mulch to retain moisture. Annual - replant each season. Provide continuous blooms throughout warm season.

zinnia.description: Also known as: Youth-and-old-age. Annual flowers in the Asteraceae family with bright, daisy-like blooms in many colors, easy to grow from seed.
zinnia.care_tips: Water at base regularly (2-3 times per week). Avoid wetting leaves to prevent powdery mildew. Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun essential. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Deadhead spent flowers to encourage continuous blooms. Easy to grow from seed. Bright, daisy-like blooms in many colors. Attract butterflies. Annual; grown for one season; no winter watering needed.

scientific_names: 'Arizona Dark Red'; T. grandiflora (Blue sky vine) is the large tropical cousin
black eyed susan vine.description: Also known as: Clock vine, Thunbergia. Fast twining vine in the Acanthaceae family with heart-shaped leaves and cheerful orange, yellow, or white flowers with dark purple-black throats from summer to frost; grown as an annual on trellises and in hanging baskets.
black eyed susan vine.care_tips: Keep the soil evenly moist; container plants may need daily water in hot weather. Full sun, with afternoon shade in very hot climates. Grows best at 15-30°C; killed by frost but perennial in zones 10-11. Medium humidity. Feed every 2-3 weeks with a balanced liquid fertilizer. Rich, well-draining soil. Provide a trellis, netting, or obelisk; it climbs 2-3 m in a season by twining. Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; germination is slow. Non-toxic to pets. Pinch young plants to encourage branching and trim wayward stems any time; cut back by half in late summer to refresh.

boston ivy.description: Deciduous vine with three-lobed leaves that turn brilliant red in fall; clings to walls via adhesive pads.
boston ivy.care_tips: Water regularly during establishment. Full sun to partial shade. Tolerates most soils. Fertilize in spring. Prune to control growth—can be aggressive. Spectacular fall color. Toxic to pets. Remove from masonry if concerned about damage.

bougainvillea.description: Vigorous tropical vine with brilliant papery bracts in magenta, purple, red, orange, white, or pink that surround tiny true flowers, thriving in hot, dry climates.
bougainvillea.care_tips: Allow soil to dry between waterings; drought stress actually promotes more prolific blooming. Full sun essential—at least 6 hours of direct sun for best color. Well-drained soil critical; does not tolerate wet feet. Fertilize with high-phosphorus fertilizer during growing season. Prune after flowering to shape. Frost-sensitive—protect below 5°C. Thorny—handle with gloves. Mildly toxic to pets.

carolina jessamine.description: Evergreen vine with fragrant yellow trumpet flowers in early spring; state flower of South Carolina.
carolina jessamine.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun to partial shade. Well-draining soil. Fertilize in spring after bloom. Prune after flowering. Highly toxic—all parts. Hummingbird attractant. Toxic to pets.

clematis.description: Climbing perennials in the Ranunculaceae family with large, showy flowers, require support and specific pruning.
clematis.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist, especially during flowering. Prefer cool roots and sunny tops - mulch around base. Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize in spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune according to type - some bloom on new growth, others on old wood. Provide support for climbing. Large, showy flowers. Research specific type for exact pruning requirements. Deciduous varieties: reduce watering when dormant in winter. Pruning varies by group: Group 1 (spring bloomers) minimal pruning; Group 2 (repeat bloomers) light pruning after first flush; Group 3 (summer/fall blo

climbers.description: Plants that climb using tendrils, twining stems, or aerial roots, require support structures like trellises or fences.
climbers.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (weekly deep watering). Water at base to avoid wetting leaves. Mulch around base to retain moisture especially for root zones. Full sun to partial shade depending on species. Provide support structures (trellises, fences, arbors) for climbing. Fertilize monthly during growing season. Prune according to species - some bloom on new growth, others on old wood. Research specific species for exact requirements. Evergreen; reduce watering in winter when growth slows.

climbing hydrangea.description: Deciduous vine with lacecap flowers and aerial roots; slow to establish but vigorous once rooted.
climbing hydrangea.care_tips: Keep soil moist, especially when establishing. Partial shade preferred; tolerates full shade. Rich, well-draining soil. Fertilize in spring. Prune after flowering—blooms on old wood. Patient—may take 3–5 years to take off. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

climbing rose.description: Roses with long canes that need support; repeat-blooming or once-blooming depending on cultivar.
climbing rose.care_tips: Water deeply 1–2 times per week. Full sun essential (6+ hours). Fertilize every 2–3 weeks during bloom. Prune after flowering—most bloom on old wood. Provide strong trellis or arbor. Mulch to retain moisture.

crossvine.description: Evergreen to semi-evergreen vine with orange-red trumpet flowers in spring; hummingbird magnet.
crossvine.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun to partial shade. Tolerates various soils. Fertilize in spring. Prune after flowering to control size. Fast-growing once established. Drought tolerant.

honeysuckle.description: Climbing and shrubby plants in the Caprifoliaceae family with fragrant, tubular flowers, some species can be invasive.
honeysuckle.care_tips: Water regularly during establishment, then reduce to weekly. Drought tolerant once established. Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize in spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune after flowering to control growth. Provide support for climbing varieties. Fragrant, tubular flowers. Attract hummingbirds. Some species can be invasive - check local regulations. Evergreen; reduce watering in winter when growth slows. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

hyacinth bean.description: Also known as: Lablab, Dolichos bean, Egyptian bean, Indian bean. Vigorous twining vine in the Fabaceae family grown as an ornamental for its purple-tinged leaves, fragrant lilac pea flowers, and glossy magenta pods, and as a vegetable in Asia and Africa for its young pods and cooked beans.
hyacinth bean.care_tips: Water deeply once or twice a week; it tolerates heat and short dry spells once established. Full sun. Needs warmth at 18-35°C and a long season; sow after the soil warms or start indoors. Perennial in zones 10-11, grown as an annual elsewhere. Medium humidity. Feed lightly; it fixes nitrogen, and too much fertilizer gives leaves instead of flowers. Well-draining, average soil. Provide a sturdy 3-4 m trellis, arch, or fence; it climbs fast by twining. Pick vegetable pods young and tender. Toxic to pets and humans raw; mature beans contain cyanogenic glycosides and must be boiled in several chan

ivy.description: Evergreen climbing and groundcover plants in the Araliaceae family, can be invasive, excellent for covering walls and ground.
ivy.care_tips: Water regularly during establishment (first year), then reduce to weekly. Drought tolerant once established. Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun to full shade depending on species. Fertilize in spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune to control growth - can be invasive. Excellent for covering walls and ground. Evergreen foliage. Research specific species for exact requirements. Evergreen; reduce watering in winter when growth slows. Toxic to pets.

japanese wisteria.description: Vigorous, long-lived climbing vine famous for its cascading clusters of fragrant purple, blue, pink, or white flowers in spring. Iconic in Japanese gardens, particularly the famous wisteria tunnels.
japanese wisteria.care_tips: Water regularly when young; drought tolerant once established. Full sun essential for best flowering. Very vigorous grower — requires strong support structure (arbor, pergola). Prune twice yearly (summer and winter) to control growth and encourage flowering. May take 3-5 years to bloom. Seeds and pods are toxic. Toxic to pets.

moonflower.description: Vigorous tropical vine with large, fragrant, pure white flowers that open at dusk and close at dawn. The nocturnal companion to morning glory.
moonflower.care_tips: Water regularly during active growth. Full sun essential for best flowering; the vine itself grows in partial shade but needs sun for buds. Well-drained, moderately fertile soil — too-rich soil produces foliage at the expense of flowers. Provide a sturdy trellis or support (grows 3-5m in a season). Annual in most climates; perennial in frost-free zones. Soak or nick seeds before planting to aid germination. Flowers are intensely fragrant at night — plant near patios and windows to enjoy the scent. Related to morning glory. All parts toxic, especially seeds — toxic to pets. Remove dead or damag

morning glory.description: Fast-growing annual and perennial vines in the Convolvulaceae family with trumpet-shaped flowers that open in morning.
morning glory.care_tips: Water regularly (2-3 times per week). Keep consistently moist during flowering. Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun essential. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Provide support for climbing. Deadhead to prevent self-seeding if desired. Fast-growing vines. Trumpet-shaped flowers open in morning. Can be invasive - check local regulations. Annual; grown for one season; no winter watering needed. Toxic to pets.

passion flower.description: Exotic vines with intricate purple, blue, or white flowers; some species produce edible passion fruit.
passion flower.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun preferred. Well-draining soil. Fertilize every 2 weeks during growth. Prune in late winter. Provide support. Passiflora edulis is the edible species. Mildly toxic—unripe fruit and leaves.

star jasmine.description: Also known as: Confederate jasmine. Evergreen twining vine with intensely fragrant, pinwheel-shaped white flowers in spring and summer, excellent as groundcover or wall climber.
star jasmine.care_tips: Water regularly during establishment; moderately drought-tolerant once mature. Full sun to partial shade—flowers best in full sun. Well-drained soil. Fertilize in spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune after flowering to control size and shape. Can be trained on trellises, walls, or used as groundcover. Evergreen in mild climates. Mildly toxic to pets (milky latex sap).

trumpet honeysuckle.description: Native vine with red or orange tubular flowers; non-invasive alternative to Japanese honeysuckle.
trumpet honeysuckle.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun to partial shade. Well-draining soil. Fertilize in spring. Prune after flowering. Hummingbird favorite. Berries attract birds. Semi-evergreen in mild climates. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

trumpet vine.description: Also known as: Trumpet creeper. Vigorous vine with orange-red trumpet flowers; very fast-growing, can be invasive.
trumpet vine.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun essential. Tolerates poor soil. Fertilize sparingly. Prune aggressively in late winter to control. Hummingbird magnet. Can damage structures—use strong support. Spreads by suckers. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

virginia creeper.description: Deciduous vine with five leaflets; spectacular red fall color, often confused with poison ivy.
virginia creeper.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun to full shade. Tolerates most soils. Fertilize in spring. Prune to control—can be aggressive. Five leaflets (not three like poison ivy). Berries toxic to humans. Stunning fall color. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

wisteria.description: Vigorous climbing vines in the Fabaceae family with cascading clusters of fragrant flowers, require strong support.
wisteria.care_tips: Water regularly during establishment, then reduce to weekly. Drought tolerant once established. Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun essential for flowering. Fertilize sparingly in spring - too much nitrogen reduces blooms. Prune twice yearly - summer and winter. Requires strong support - can damage structures. Cascading clusters of fragrant flowers. Very vigorous - can be invasive. Deciduous varieties: reduce watering when dormant in winter. Toxic to pets.

ajuga.description: Also known as: Bugleweed. Low groundcover with blue flower spikes and bronze or green foliage; spreads by runners.
ajuga.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist. Partial shade preferred; tolerates full sun in cool climates. Well-draining soil. Fertilize in spring. Divide every 2–3 years to control spread. Mildly toxic to pets. Can be invasive in favorable conditions. Shear off spent flower spikes after blooming and trim runners to control spread.

bamboo.description: Fast-growing grasses in the Poaceae family, can be clumping or running types, popular for screening and containers. Not related to lucky bamboo, which is a Dracaena.
bamboo.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist (2-3 times per week). Running types spread aggressively - contain with barriers or plant in containers. Clumping types are more manageable. Full sun to partial shade depending on species. Fertilize monthly during growing season with high-nitrogen fertilizer. Prune to control height and remove old canes. Container-grown bamboo needs regular repotting. Research clumping vs running types before planting. Some species are invasive - check local regulations.

big bluestem.description: Tall native prairie grass with blue-green stems that turn reddish in fall; three-forked seed heads.
big bluestem.care_tips: Water when top 2 inches dry; very drought-tolerant once established. Full sun essential. Adapts to most soils. No fertilizer—lean soil keeps it compact. The dominant grass of the tallgrass prairie (6-8 ft). Copper-bronze fall color. Turkey-foot seed heads. Cut back in late winter.

blue fescue.description: Compact ornamental grass with blue-gray foliage; forms neat mounds, ideal for borders and rock gardens.
blue fescue.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun essential for best color. Well-draining soil; drought tolerant. Fertilize sparingly. Comb or shear in early spring to remove dead foliage. Short-lived—replace every 3–4 years. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

blue grama.description: Low native prairie grass with distinctive horizontal flower spikes resembling eyelashes; drought tolerant.
blue grama.care_tips: Water sparingly; extremely drought-tolerant once established. Full sun essential. Well-draining, lean soil. Never fertilize—causes floppy growth. Short (12-18 in.) warm-season grass with distinctive eyelash-like seed heads. Excellent for xeriscaping and native lawns. Mow to 3 inches or leave natural. Cut back in late winter before new growth.

creeping jenny.description: Also known as: Moneywort. Fast-spreading groundcover with round, coin-shaped leaves. Golden variety (Aurea) is one of the most popular container and hanging basket trailing plants.
creeping jenny.care_tips: Water regularly — prefers consistently moist to wet soil; thrives at pond edges and in rain gardens. Partial shade to full sun; golden variety needs more sun for best color but scorches in intense heat. Adaptable to most soils. Minimal fertilization needed. Spreads rapidly by rooting at stem nodes — can become invasive in moist conditions. Excellent in containers, hanging baskets, and between stepping stones. Golden variety is less aggressive than the green species. Tolerates light foot traffic. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

creeping phlox.description: Also known as: Moss phlox, Moss pink. Low-growing perennial groundcover in the Polemoniaceae family with masses of spring flowers, excellent for rock gardens.
creeping phlox.care_tips: Water regularly during establishment, then reduce to weekly. Drought tolerant once established. Well-drained soil essential. Full sun preferred. Fertilize in spring with balanced fertilizer. Shear after flowering to maintain shape. Excellent for rock gardens and slopes. Masses of spring flowers. Forms dense mats. Herbaceous perennials die back; reduce watering when dormant. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

grasses.description: Ornamental grasses in the Poaceae family, add texture and movement to landscapes, many are drought tolerant.
grasses.care_tips: Occasional deep watering (every 2-3 weeks once established). Most are drought tolerant once established. Water regularly during establishment period (first year). Full sun preferred for most species. Fertilize sparingly in spring. Cut back in late winter/early spring before new growth. Divide every 3-5 years to maintain vigor. Add texture and movement to landscapes. Research specific species for exact requirements. Herbaceous perennials die back; reduce watering when dormant.

groundcovers.description: Low-growing plants that spread to cover ground, useful for erosion control and reducing maintenance.
groundcovers.care_tips: Light watering once established (every 1-2 weeks). Keep moist during establishment period (first 3-6 months). Most are drought tolerant after rooting. Full sun to partial shade depending on species. Fertilize sparingly in spring. Prune to control spread if needed. Useful for erosion control and reducing maintenance. Mulch between plants during establishment. Research specific species for exact requirements. Evergreen; reduce watering in winter when growth slows.

ice plant.description: Low-growing succulent groundcover with brilliant daisy-like flowers in neon pink, purple, orange, yellow, and white that open in full sun. Excellent for xeriscaping and dry slopes.
ice plant.care_tips: Water sparingly — ice plants are extremely drought tolerant and rot in wet conditions. Full sun essential; flowers only open in direct sunlight. Excellent drainage critical — sandy, gravelly, or rocky soil. Do not fertilize — excess nutrients reduce flowering. Spreads via trailing stems. Delosperma species are cold-hardy (to -20°C for some); Carpobrotus is frost-tender. Carpobrotus edulis is extremely invasive in coastal California and Mediterranean regions. Delosperma cooperi is the best choice for gardens. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

indian grass.description: Tall native prairie grass with golden fall color and feathery bronze seed heads; warm-season grass.
indian grass.care_tips: Water when top 2 inches dry; drought-tolerant once established. Full sun essential. Adapts to most soils including clay. No fertilizer needed. Golden-bronze plume-like seed heads in fall. Tall (4-7 ft). Beautiful winter interest. Cut back in late winter before new growth.

japanese forest grass.description: Graceful, cascading grass with gold or green variegation; thrives in shade.
japanese forest grass.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist. Partial to full shade preferred; bleaches in full sun. Rich, well-draining soil. Fertilize in spring. Cut back in late winter. Slow-growing. Golden forms need some light for color.

lamb s ear.description: Fuzzy, silver-gray foliage that feels like lamb's wool; purple flower spikes in summer.
lamb s ear.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun preferred; needs good drainage. Drought tolerant. Avoid overhead watering—fuzzy leaves rot when wet. Remove flower stalks to maintain compact foliage. Divide when center dies out. Remove spent flower stalks and damaged leaves; divide when the center dies out.

dead nettle.description: Also known as: Lamium. Low-growing shade groundcover with silver-marked, heart-shaped leaves and small hooded flowers in pink, purple, or white. Not a true nettle — does not sting.
dead nettle.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil evenly moist; tolerates brief dry spells once established. Shade to partial shade — one of the best groundcovers for dry shade once established. Adaptable to most soils; thrives in average garden conditions. Fertilize lightly in spring. Can be sheared back after flowering to tidy and encourage fresh growth. L. galeobdolon (yellow archangel) is aggressive and potentially invasive — spotted dead nettle (L. maculatum) is better behaved. Silver leaf markings brighten dark garden areas. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

lawn turf.description: Grass species maintained as lawns, require regular mowing and maintenance for healthy growth.
lawn turf.care_tips: Frequent deep watering (1-1.5 inches per week, 2-3 times per week). Water early morning (before 10am) to reduce evaporation and prevent disease. Avoid shallow frequent watering which encourages shallow roots. Full sun to partial shade depending on grass type. Fertilize 3-4 times per year with lawn fertilizer. Mow regularly at appropriate height for grass type. Aerate annually. Overseed in fall for cool-season grasses. Research specific grass type for exact requirements. Evergreen; reduce watering in winter when growth slows.

liriope.description: Also known as: Lilyturf. Shade-tolerant evergreen groundcover with grass-like foliage and spikes of purple or white flowers followed by dark berries.
liriope.care_tips: Water regularly during establishment; drought-tolerant once mature. Full sun to deep shade—extremely adaptable. Tolerates a wide range of soils. Fertilize in spring with balanced fertilizer. Mow or cut back old foliage in late winter before new growth emerges. Divide clumps every few years. Deer resistant. Non-toxic to pets.

little bluestem.description: Native prairie grass with blue-green summer foliage turning orange-red in fall; compact, drought tolerant.
little bluestem.care_tips: Water when top 1-2 inches dry; very drought-tolerant once established. Full sun essential. Well-draining, lean soil—rich soil causes floppy growth. Never fertilize. Stunning mahogany-red fall and winter color with fluffy white seed heads. Cut back in late spring. Named 2022 Perennial Plant of the Year.

miscanthus.description: Tall ornamental grass with silvery plumes and arching foliage; can be invasive.
miscanthus.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun preferred. Tolerates most soils. Fertilize in spring. Cut back in late winter before new growth. Choose sterile cultivars to avoid seeding. Some cultivars invasive—check local regulations.

mondo grass.description: Low-growing evergreen groundcover with fine, dark green grass-like foliage, including the dramatic black-leaved variety used as an accent in modern gardens.
mondo grass.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist during establishment; moderately drought-tolerant once mature. Partial shade preferred; tolerates full shade. Moist, well-drained soil with organic matter. Fertilize in spring with balanced fertilizer. Very low maintenance once established. Slow to fill in but forms dense mats over time. Black mondo grass needs some morning sun to maintain dark color. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

pachysandra.description: Evergreen groundcover in the Buxaceae family with glossy leaves, excellent for shady areas and erosion control.
pachysandra.care_tips: Water regularly during establishment (first year), then reduce to weekly. Prefer consistently moist but well-drained soil. Partial to full shade preferred. Fertilize in spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune to control spread if needed. Excellent for shady areas. Glossy evergreen leaves. Spreads by rhizomes. Excellent for erosion control. Evergreen; reduce watering in winter when growth slows. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

pampas grass.description: Also known as: Silver Pampas Grass. Towering ornamental grass with feathery silver-white plumes, widely used in landscaping and home décor.
pampas grass.care_tips: Full sun — minimum 6 hours direct sunlight daily. Drought-tolerant once established; water occasionally during dry spells. Avoid overwatering — susceptible to root rot. Well-drained soil in wide pH range. Cut back old foliage to 30 cm in late winter before new growth. Wear gloves — leaf edges are razor-sharp. Check local regulations as invasive in warm climates. Non-toxic but leaf edges can cause cuts.

fountain grass.description: Ornamental grass with bottlebrush flower plumes; arching foliage in green, burgundy, or variegated.
fountain grass.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun preferred. Well-draining soil. Fertilize in spring. Cut back in late winter. Drought tolerant. Perennial in mild climates; treat as annual in cold zones. Avoid invasive P. setaceum.

pink muhly grass.description: Ornamental grass with airy pink to purple clouds of flowers in fall; drought tolerant, striking display.
pink muhly grass.care_tips: Water when top 1-2 inches dry; drought-tolerant once established. Full sun for best flowering. Well-draining soil; tolerates sand and clay. Light spring fertilizer optional. Spectacular cotton-candy pink flower plumes September-November. Cut back in late winter. Low-maintenance ornamental grass.

prairie dropseed.description: Fine-textured native prairie grass with fragrant fall blooms; forms neat mounds, excellent for borders.
prairie dropseed.care_tips: Water when top 2 inches dry; very drought-tolerant once established. Full sun essential. Well-draining, lean soil. Never fertilize. Fine-textured arching foliage with delicate seed heads that smell like buttered popcorn or cilantro. Golden-orange fall color. Extremely long-lived (100+ years). Cut back in late spring.

scientific_names: Phedimus kamtschaticus (syn. Sedum kamtschaticum; Orange stonecrop)
Phedimus spurius (syn. Sedum spurium; Two-row stonecrop)
creeping sedum.description: Low, mat-forming succulents with small leaves; yellow or pink flowers, drought-tolerant.
creeping sedum.care_tips: Water when soil is dry; very drought tolerant. Full sun preferred. Poor, well-draining soil OK. Fertilize sparingly. Excellent for rock gardens and green roofs. Propagate by division. Tolerates neglect. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

side oats grama.description: Native prairie grass with oat-like flowers arranged along one side of the stem; state grass of Texas.
side oats grama.care_tips: Water sparingly; extremely drought-tolerant once established. Full sun essential. Well-draining, lean soil including rocky or sandy. Never fertilize. Named for oat-like seeds that hang to one side of the stem. State grass of Texas. Short (18-30 in.) warm-season grass. Excellent for native meadows. Cut back in late winter before new growth.

sweet woodruff.description: Low-growing shade groundcover with whorls of bright green leaves and tiny white star-shaped spring flowers. Dried leaves have sweet vanilla-hay scent; traditional flavoring for May wine.
sweet woodruff.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist. Full shade to partial shade — one of the best groundcovers for deep shade. Spreads by runners; can become vigorous in ideal conditions. Shear back after flowering if needed. Minimal fertilizer required. Extremely cold-hardy. Deer and rabbit resistant. Mildly toxic in large quantities — safe as culinary herb in moderation. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

switchgrass.description: Tall native prairie grass with airy flower panicles; blue-green or red cultivars; important biofuel crop.
switchgrass.care_tips: Water when top 1-2 inches dry; drought-tolerant once established. Full sun essential. Adapts to most soils including clay and wet areas. No fertilizer needed. Upright growth (3-6 ft) with airy seed heads. Excellent winter interest. Cut back in late winter. Deep roots prevent erosion.

vinca.description: Evergreen groundcover in the Apocynaceae family with glossy leaves and spring flowers, can be invasive.
vinca.care_tips: Water regularly during establishment, then reduce to weekly. Drought tolerant once established. Well-drained soil preferred. Partial shade to full shade preferred. Fertilize in spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune to control spread if needed. Glossy evergreen leaves. Spring flowers. Spreads by runners. Can be invasive - check local regulations. Evergreen; reduce watering in winter when growth slows. Toxic to pets.

amaranth.description: Also known as: Chinese spinach. Heat-tolerant leafy green and grain crop in the Amaranthaceae family; nutritious leaves and edible seeds, thrives in summer heat.
amaranth.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun preferred. Drought tolerant once established. Fertilize regularly during growing season. Harvest young leaves for greens; seeds for grain. Mulch to retain moisture. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

arugula.description: Also known as: Rocket, Roquette. Fast-growing leafy green in the Brassicaceae family with peppery flavor, also known as rocket or roquette.
arugula.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture prevents bitterness and bolting. Water at base. Full sun to partial shade. Prefer cooler temperatures - plant in spring or fall. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest leaves when young for best flavor. Fast-growing. Peppery flavor. Can bolt in heat - provide shade in summer. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

beet greens.description: Edible leaves and stems of the beet root; nutritious, quick-growing, and harvested before or alongside the root.
beet greens.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Full sun to partial shade. Fertile, well-drained soil. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks. Harvest outer leaves when 4-6 inches; inner leaves continue growing. Both greens and roots edible. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

bok choy.description: Also known as: Pak choi. Leafy green vegetable in the Brassicaceae family, fast-growing and mild-flavored, popular in Chinese cuisine.
bok choy.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture prevents bitterness and bolting. Water at base. Full sun to partial shade. Prefer cooler temperatures - plant in spring or fall. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest whole heads or individual leaves. Fast-growing. Can bolt in heat - provide shade in summer. Watch for cabbage worms. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Harvest outer leaves first, allowing center to continue growing. Remove yellowing leaves.

cabbage.description: Leafy vegetables in the Brassicaceae family, form tight heads, prefer cool weather.
cabbage.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture important for head formation. Well-drained, fertile soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Harvest when heads are firm and reach desired size. Prefer cool weather - plant in spring or fall. Can be stored for months. Watch for cabbage worms. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Harvest outer leaves first, allowing center to continue growing. Remove yellowing leaves.

choy sum.description: Also known as: Chinese flowering cabbage. Leafy green vegetables in the Brassicaceae family, popular in Chinese cuisine with tender stems and small yellow flowers.
choy sum.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture important. Well-drained, fertile soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Harvest whole plant or individual leaves. Prefer cool weather - plant in spring or fall. Popular in Chinese cuisine. Fast-growing. Can bolt in heat. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Harvest outer leaves first, allowing center to continue growing. Remove yellowing leaves.

collard greens.description: Also known as: Collards. Leafy green vegetable in the Brassicaceae family, cold-hardy and can overwinter in mild climates.
collard greens.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture ensures tender leaves. Water at base. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Harvest outer leaves regularly to encourage new growth. Cold-hardy - flavor improves after frost. Can overwinter in mild climates. Watch for cabbage worms and aphids. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Harvest outer leaves first, allowing center to continue growing. Remove yellowing leaves.

dandelion greens.description: Edible greens from the common dandelion; slightly bitter, nutritious, best when young. Roots and flowers also edible.
dandelion greens.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun for tender leaves. Harvest young leaves before flowers for milder flavor. Blanch by covering to reduce bitterness. Wild or cultivated; ensure no pesticide use. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

endive.description: Also known as: Frisée. Curly-leaved chicory in the Asteraceae family; slightly bitter, crisp leaves for salads. Distinct from escarole (broad-leaved).
endive.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist. Full sun to partial shade. Prefer cool weather; plant spring or fall. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks. Blanch by covering heads 1-2 weeks before harvest for milder flavor. Harvest when leaves reach desired size. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

escarole.description: Also known as: Broad-leaved endive. Broad-leaved chicory in the Asteraceae family; milder than curly endive, with flat, tender leaves for salads and cooking.
escarole.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist. Full sun to partial shade. Prefer cool weather; plant spring or fall. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks. Blanch inner leaves for milder flavor. Harvest outer leaves or whole head. Less bitter than curly endive. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

gai lan.description: Also known as: Chinese broccoli, Kai-lan, Chinese kale. Chinese broccoli in the Brassicaceae family with thick stems and small flower heads, essential in Chinese cuisine.
gai lan.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture important. Well-drained, fertile soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Harvest when flower buds are just forming. Both stems and leaves are edible. Prefer cool weather. Essential in Chinese cuisine. Watch for cabbage worms. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Harvest outer leaves first, allowing center to continue growing. Remove yellowing leaves.

scientific_names: Glebionis coronaria (syn. Chrysanthemum coronarium; Garland chrysanthemum
garland chrysanthemum.description: Also known as: Tong ho, Shungiku, Crown daisy, Chop suey greens. Cool-season leafy vegetable in the Asteraceae family with aromatic, slightly bitter leaves used in hot pot, stir-fries, and sukiyaki; small yellow daisies appear if left to bolt.
garland chrysanthemum.care_tips: Keep the soil evenly moist; dry soil makes the leaves tough and bitter. Full sun in cool weather, light shade in warm spells. Grows best at 10-25°C; bolts quickly above 25°C, so sow in early spring and again in late summer. Medium humidity. Feed every 2-3 weeks with a nitrogen-rich fertilizer for leafy growth. Loose, fertile, well-draining soil. Sow thickly and thin to 10-15 cm; the thinnings are edible. Harvest young leaves at 10-20 cm by cutting the whole plant or picking outer leaves for cut-and-come-again. Non-toxic to pets. Pinch out flower buds to prolong the leaf harvest, or let a few b

kale.description: Cold-hardy leafy green in the Brassicaceae family, flavor improves after frost, can overwinter in mild climates.
kale.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture ensures tender leaves. Water at base to avoid wetting leaves. Mulch around plants to retain moisture and keep leaves clean. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Harvest outer leaves regularly to encourage new growth. Flavor improves after frost. Can overwinter in mild climates. Watch for cabbage worms and aphids. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Harvest outer leaves first, allowing center to continue growing. Remove yellowing leaves.

leafy greens.description: Vegetables grown primarily for their edible leaves. Many are cool-season crops that bolt in heat. Quick to harvest and ideal for successive planting.
leafy greens.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist — water every 1-2 days in warm weather. Mulch to retain moisture and keep roots cool. Partial shade to full sun — most prefer cooler conditions and bolt (go to seed) in heat. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with nitrogen-rich fertilizer for lush leaf growth. Harvest outer leaves first (cut-and-come-again) for continuous production. Succession plant every 2-3 weeks for ongoing harvest. Best grown in spring and fall — provide shade cloth in summer. Ready in 30-60 days depending on variety. Research specific vegetable for exact requirements. Remove dead or damaged foliage p

lettuce.description: Fast-growing leafy greens in the Asteraceae family, prefer cooler temperatures and can bolt (flower) in heat.
lettuce.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (daily watering may be needed in hot weather). Consistent moisture prevents bitterness and bolting (premature flowering). Water at base to avoid wetting leaves which can cause disease. Partial shade in hot climates helps prevent bolting. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Harvest outer leaves regularly or cut whole head. Fast-growing - ready in 45-60 days. Prefer cooler temperatures - plant in spring and fall. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

malabar spinach.description: Heat-loving vining herb in the Basellaceae family; succulent leaves and stems. Thrives in summer when true spinach bolts.
malabar spinach.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist. Full sun. Trellis or support for vining habit. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks. Harvest young leaves and shoot tips. Heat-tolerant; grows when other greens struggle. Red-stemmed variety (B. alba 'Rubra') ornamental. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

mizuna.description: Japanese mustard green in the Brassicaceae family; feathery, serrated leaves with mild peppery flavor. Popular in salads and stir-fries.
mizuna.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Full sun to partial shade. Prefer cool weather; plant spring or fall. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks. Cut-and-come-again harvest. Fast-growing; ready in 40-50 days. Mild flavor; can bolt in heat. Harvest outer leaves first, allowing center to continue growing. Remove yellowing leaves.

mustard greens.description: Leafy green vegetables in the Brassicaceae family with peppery flavor, fast-growing and cold-hardy.
mustard greens.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture ensures tender leaves. Water at base. Full sun to partial shade. Prefer cooler temperatures - plant in spring or fall. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Harvest outer leaves regularly. Fast-growing. Peppery flavor. Cold-hardy. Can bolt in heat. Watch for cabbage worms and aphids. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

napa cabbage.description: Also known as: Chinese cabbage, Wombok, Pe-tsai. Chinese cabbage in the Brassicaceae family with elongated, barrel-shaped heads, essential in Chinese cuisine.
napa cabbage.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture important for head formation. Well-drained, fertile soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Prefer cool weather - plant in spring or fall. Harvest when heads are firm. Essential in Chinese cuisine. Can bolt in heat. Watch for cabbage worms. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Harvest outer leaves first, allowing center to continue growing. Remove yellowing leaves.

purslane.description: Succulent annual in the Portulacaceae family; fleshy leaves high in omega-3. Often foraged as a weed; cultivated for salads and cooking.
purslane.care_tips: Drought tolerant; water when soil is dry. Full sun. Poor soil acceptable. Harvest stems and leaves when young. Self-sows; can become weedy. Tangy, slightly lemony flavor. Popular in Mediterranean and Asian cuisines. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

radicchio.description: Also known as: Chioggia, Treviso, Castelfranco. Chicory in the Asteraceae family with bitter, wine-red leaves; forms compact heads. Essential in Italian cuisine; bitterness mellows when grilled or roasted.
radicchio.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist. Full sun. Prefer cool weather; flavor improves after frost. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks. Harvest when heads are firm. Cold temperatures deepen red color. Blanch some varieties for sweeter flavor. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

spinach.description: Cool-season leafy green in the Amaranthaceae family, bolts quickly in heat, best grown in spring and fall.
spinach.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (daily watering may be needed). Consistent moisture prevents bolting (premature flowering) and ensures tender leaves. Water at base to avoid wetting leaves. Partial shade in warm climates. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Harvest outer leaves regularly or cut whole plant. Bolts quickly in heat - best grown in spring and fall. Ready in 40-50 days. Watch for leaf miners. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

swiss chard.description: Also known as: Rainbow chard. Leafy green vegetable in the Amaranthaceae family with colorful stems, can be harvested continuously throughout season.
swiss chard.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture ensures tender leaves. Water at base to avoid wetting leaves. Mulch around plants. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Harvest outer leaves regularly to encourage new growth. Colorful stems in red, yellow, orange, and white. Can harvest continuously throughout season. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

scientific_names: Brassica rapa var. rosularis (Rosette bok choy)
tatsoi.description: Asian green in the Brassicaceae family; dark green spoon-shaped leaves in a flat rosette. Mild, mustard-like flavor; cold-hardy.
tatsoi.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Full sun to partial shade. Prefer cool weather; very cold-hardy. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks. Harvest whole rosette or outer leaves. Fast-growing; ready in 45-50 days. Popular in Asian salads and stir-fries. Harvest outer leaves first, allowing center to continue growing. Remove yellowing leaves.

turnip greens.description: Edible leaves of the turnip root; nutritious, slightly peppery. Harvest before or alongside roots; flavor improves after light frost.
turnip greens.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Full sun to partial shade. Fertile, well-drained soil. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks. Harvest outer leaves when 4-6 inches; allows root to develop. Can grow for greens only or greens plus roots. Cold-hardy. Harvest outer leaves first, allowing center to continue growing. Remove yellowing leaves.

water spinach.description: Also known as: Kangkong. Semi-aquatic vine in the Convolvulaceae family; hollow stems and tender leaves. Staples in Southeast Asian and Chinese cooking.
water spinach.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist or grow in shallow water. Full sun. Rich soil or aquatic setup. Fertilize regularly. Harvest shoot tips and young leaves. Invasive in some regions; check local regulations. Quick-growing; harvest frequently. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

acorn squash.description: Small winter squash in the Cucurbitaceae family with acorn-shaped dark green fruits and sweet orange flesh, good for roasting.
acorn squash.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week during growing season. Consistent moisture important during fruit development. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Compact vines suit smaller gardens. Harvest when rind is hard and dark green. Cure before storage. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

adzuki bean.description: Also known as: Azuki bean, Red bean. Small red beans in the Fabaceae family, very popular in Chinese and Japanese cuisine, used in desserts.
adzuki bean.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Well-drained, fertile soil preferred. Full sun essential. Fertilize with low-nitrogen fertilizer. Fast-growing (90-120 days). Harvest when pods are dry and brown. Very popular in Chinese and Japanese cuisine. Used in desserts and sweet red bean paste. Warm-season crop. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove diseased foliage promptly.

armenian cucumber.description: Long, ribbed melon in the Cucurbitaceae family, eaten like cucumber when immature, mild and crisp, heat-tolerant.
armenian cucumber.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (daily in hot weather). Water at base to avoid leaf diseases. Consistent moisture prevents bitter fruit. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Provide trellis for vining habit. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks. Harvest when 12-18 inches long for best flavor. Heat-tolerant. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove diseased foliage promptly.

artichoke.description: Perennial thistle in the Asteraceae family, grown for edible flower buds before they bloom, Mediterranean origin.
artichoke.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week. Consistent moisture important during bud formation. Mulch to retain moisture. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in spring and after harvest. Perennial in zones 7–11; harvest flower buds when tight and before scales open. Mulch heavily in winter. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

asparagus.description: Also known as: Garden asparagus. Perennial vegetable with tender edible spears, takes 2-3 years to establish.
asparagus.care_tips: Water regularly during growing season. Full sun. Rich, well-drained soil. Do not harvest first year; light harvest second year. Mulch in winter. Long-lived perennial. Herbaceous perennials die back; reduce watering when dormant. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

beans.description: Fast-growing legume vegetables in the Fabaceae family, from snap and shelling beans to lima and runner beans; pole types need support while bush types are self-supporting.
beans.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Water at base to avoid wetting leaves. Consistent moisture important during flowering and pod development. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize sparingly - beans fix their own nitrogen. Pole beans need trellis or support; bush beans are self-supporting. Harvest regularly to encourage continued production. Fast-growing - ready in 50-60 days. Watch for bean beetles. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

bell peppers.description: Also known as: Sweet pepper. Sweet peppers in the Solanaceae family with blocky, thick-walled fruits, most popular pepper variety.
bell peppers.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week. Consistent moisture important during fruiting. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Stake plants if needed. Harvest when fruits reach desired size and color - green peppers are immature, colored peppers are fully ripe. Warm-season crop. Watch for aphids and pepper maggots. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

bitter melon.description: Tropical gourd in the Cucurbitaceae family with warty, bitter fruits, popular in Asian cuisine for medicinal and culinary use.
bitter melon.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week. Consistent moisture important during fruiting. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Provide trellis for vining habit. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks. Harvest when fruits are 4-6 inches; younger fruits are less bitter. Warm-season crop - requires long, hot season. Popular in Asian cuisine. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Prune side shoots and lower leaves for airflow; harvest tender fruits about 20 days after flowering.

bottle gourd.description: Also known as: Calabash, Opo squash, Lauki, Dudhi. Vigorous annual vine in the Cucurbitaceae family with white night-opening flowers; young fruits are a mild cooking vegetable across Asia and Africa, and mature fruits dry into hard-shelled containers and birdhouses.
bottle gourd.care_tips: Water deeply two or three times a week; fruit quality drops if the vine dries out. Full sun. Needs warm weather at 20-35°C and a long season; sow after all frost or start indoors. Medium humidity. Feed every 2-3 weeks with a balanced fertilizer once vines run. Rich, well-draining soil with plenty of compost. Train on a sturdy trellis or arch so fruits hang straight. Hand-pollinate the night-blooming flowers if fruit fails to set. Pick culinary fruits young (30-40 cm, tender skin); leave craft gourds until the stem browns, then cure for months. Non-toxic to pets; discard any bitter-tasting frui

broccoli.description: Cruciferous vegetables in the Brassicaceae family, harvest central head and side shoots, prefer cool weather.
broccoli.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture important for head development. Well-drained, fertile soil preferred. Full sun preferred. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Harvest central head when tight and before flowers open. Side shoots will continue to produce. Prefer cool weather - plant in spring or fall. Watch for cabbage worms and aphids. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove yellowing lower leaves and diseased foliage promptly.

brussels sprouts.description: Cruciferous vegetables in the Brassicaceae family, produce small cabbage-like sprouts along stem, flavor improves after frost.
brussels sprouts.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture important. Well-drained, fertile soil preferred. Full sun preferred. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Remove lower leaves as plant grows. Harvest sprouts from bottom up when 1-2 inches in diameter. Flavor improves after frost. Long growing season (90-100 days). Watch for cabbage worms. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove yellowing lower leaves and diseased foliage promptly.

butternut squash.description: Popular winter squash in the Cucurbitaceae family with sweet, nutty flavor, excellent for storage.
butternut squash.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week during growing season. Consistent moisture important during fruit development. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Vining plants require space. Harvest when fully mature and rind is hard. Cure in warm place for 2 weeks before storage. Excellent for storage - can last 3-6 months. Sweet, nutty flavor. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

cantaloupe.description: Also known as: Muskmelon, Rockmelon. Warm-season fruiting vegetable in the Cucurbitaceae family, also known as muskmelon, requires long growing season.
cantaloupe.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week, increase during fruit development. Consistent moisture critical during fruiting. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Vining plants require space. Harvest when stem separates easily from fruit and fruit has sweet aroma. Warm-season crop - requires long growing season. Watch for aphids and cucumber beetles. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

cape gooseberry.description: Also known as: Golden berry. Fruit in the Solanaceae family with tart-sweet berries enclosed in paper husks, also known as golden berry or ground cherry.
cape gooseberry.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Sprawling habit; may need support. Harvest when husks turn dry and papery and berries are golden. Can be eaten fresh or used in preserves. Warm-season crop. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Prune suckers and lower leaves for better air circulation. Remove diseased foliage promptly. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

cauliflower.description: Cruciferous vegetables in the Brassicaceae family, form white, purple, or orange heads, prefer cool weather.
cauliflower.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture important for head development. Well-drained, fertile soil preferred. Full sun preferred. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Blanch white varieties by tying leaves over head. Harvest when head is tight and before it separates. Prefer cool weather - very sensitive to heat. Watch for cabbage worms. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove yellowing lower leaves and diseased foliage promptly.

celery.description: Stalk vegetables in the Apiaceae family, require consistent moisture and rich soil, challenging to grow.
celery.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist (daily watering may be needed). Never allow to dry out. Rich, organic soil essential. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Blanch stalks by wrapping or hilling soil around base. Harvest outer stalks first. Challenging to grow - requires consistent care. Prefer cool weather. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

chayote.description: Also known as: Mirliton. Tender squash (mirliton) with edible fruit, shoots, and roots; vigorous vine.
chayote.care_tips: Full sun. Provide strong trellis. Keep soil moist. Harvest when fruit is 4-6 inches. Young shoots and roots also edible. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

cherry tomato.description: Small, sweet tomatoes in the Solanaceae family, prolific and easy to grow, ideal for salads and snacking.
cherry tomato.care_tips: Deep, regular watering at base (2-3 times per week). Avoid wetting leaves to prevent disease. Consistent moisture prevents blossom end rot. Full sun essential (8+ hours daily). Stake or cage indeterminate varieties. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with tomato fertilizer. Harvest when fully colored - prolific producer. Sweet and easy to grow. Prune suckers and lower leaves for better airflow; remove diseased foliage promptly. Foliage and green fruit are mildly toxic to pets; ripe fruit is safe.

corn.description: Also known as: Maize. Tall grain crop in the Poaceae family, requires pollination from wind or manual assistance, plant in blocks for better pollination.
corn.care_tips: Regular deep watering (2-3 times per week). Keep consistently moist especially during tasseling and ear development - critical for kernel development. Full sun essential (8+ hours daily). Plant in blocks (at least 4 rows) for better wind pollination. Fertilize when 12 inches tall and again when tassels appear. Tall plants - provide space. Ready in 60-100 days depending on variety. Watch for corn earworms. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

cucumbers.description: Vining fruiting vegetables in the Cucurbitaceae family, need consistent moisture and support for climbing types.
cucumbers.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (daily watering in hot weather). Water at base to avoid leaf diseases like powdery mildew. Consistent moisture prevents bitter fruit. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Provide trellis or support for vining types. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest regularly when fruits are young and tender. Ready in 50-70 days. Watch for cucumber beetles and powdery mildew. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

delicata squash.description: Also known as: Sweet potato squash. Cylindrical winter squash in the Cucurbitaceae family with creamy, sweet flesh and edible skin, stores well.
delicata squash.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week during growing season. Consistent moisture important during fruit development. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest when rind is hard and cream-colored with green stripes. Skin is edible when cooked. Cure before storage. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

edamame.description: Also known as: Green soybean. Immature soybeans harvested while still green and tender (leave pods to mature and dry for dry soybeans), a popular snack and ingredient in East Asian cuisine. Higher in protein than most vegetables.
edamame.care_tips: Water regularly — keep soil moist during flowering and pod development. Full sun. Warm weather crop; plant after last frost. Inoculate seeds with rhizobium bacteria for better nitrogen fixation. Harvest when pods are plump but still green. Non-toxic. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

eggplant.description: Also known as: Aubergine. Warm-season fruiting vegetable in the Solanaceae family, also known as aubergine, requires long growing season.
eggplant.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week. Consistent moisture important during fruiting. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Stake plants if needed. Harvest when skin is glossy and firm. Warm-season crop - start indoors in cool climates. Requires long growing season. Watch for flea beetles and aphids. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Thin out seedlings promptly and remove overcrowded leaves. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

fruiting vegetables.description: Warm-season vegetables grown for their edible fruits. Require long warm growing seasons and full sun for best production.
fruiting vegetables.care_tips: Water deeply and consistently (1-2 inches per week). Water at base to avoid wetting foliage which can cause disease. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Rich, well-drained soil with plenty of organic matter. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with balanced fertilizer — switch to higher-phosphorus when fruiting begins. Stake or cage tall varieties (tomatoes, peppers). Mulch around base to retain moisture and prevent soil splash. Harvest regularly to encourage continued production. Most are frost-tender — plant after last frost date. Research specific vegetable for exact requirements. Remove yellowing

green beans.description: Fast-growing legumes in the Fabaceae family, include bush and pole varieties, very popular vegetable.
green beans.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture important during flowering and pod development. Well-drained, fertile soil preferred. Full sun essential. Fertilize with low-nitrogen fertilizer (legumes fix nitrogen). Support pole varieties with trellis. Harvest when pods are young and tender (before seeds bulge). Fast-growing (50-60 days). Continuous harvest encourages more production. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

ground cherry.description: Small fruit in the Solanaceae family with sweet, tropical-flavored berries in paper husks, related to tomatillo.
ground cherry.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Sprawling habit. Harvest when husks turn dry and papery and berries drop - sweet when fully ripe. Use in pies, preserves, or fresh. Warm-season crop. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Prune suckers and lower leaves for better air circulation. Remove diseased foliage promptly. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

habanero.description: Very hot peppers in the Solanaceae family, among the hottest common peppers, use with extreme caution.
habanero.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week. Consistent moisture important during fruiting. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest when fully colored (orange, red, or chocolate). Extremely hot - use gloves when handling. Warm-season crop - requires long, hot season. Very hot peppers - use with extreme caution. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

honeydew.description: Green-fleshed melon in the Cucurbitaceae family with sweet, smooth flesh and pale green to white rind.
honeydew.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week, increase during fruit development. Consistent moisture critical during fruiting. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Vining plants require space. Harvest when rind turns creamy white or yellow and fruit has slight give. Warm-season crop. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

jalape o.description: Medium-hot peppers in the Solanaceae family, popular for salsas and cooking, can be mild to moderately hot.
jalape o.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week. Consistent moisture important during fruiting. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest when green for milder flavor, or when red for hotter flavor. Can be dried or smoked to make chipotle. Warm-season crop. Heat level varies by growing conditions. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

asian eggplant.description: Slender, elongated eggplant varieties popular in Asian cuisine. Includes Japanese, Chinese, and other types with thin skin, few seeds, and tender flesh that cooks quickly.
asian eggplant.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week. Consistent moisture important during fruiting. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest when skin is glossy and fruits are 6-10 inches long. Tender flesh, ideal for grilling and stir-fries. Warm-season crop. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Thin out seedlings promptly and remove overcrowded leaves. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

lemon cucumber.description: Round, yellow cucumber in the Cucurbitaceae family with mild, crisp flesh, heirloom variety.
lemon cucumber.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (daily in hot weather). Water at base to avoid leaf diseases. Consistent moisture prevents bitter fruit. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest when round and lemon-sized (2-3 inches) for best flavor. Mild, crisp, ideal for salads. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

luffa.description: Also known as: Loofah. Gourd vine in the Cucurbitaceae family; young fruit edible as vegetable; mature fruit dries into natural sponge.
luffa.care_tips: Full sun essential. Strong trellis required for vining habit. Water regularly. Harvest young for food (under 6 inches). Let mature and dry on vine for sponge. Long growing season. Popular in Asian cuisine. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Prune side shoots for airflow; harvest tender fruits about 10 days after flowering.

mung bean.description: Fast-growing legumes in the Fabaceae family, very popular in Chinese cuisine, can be sprouted.
mung bean.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Well-drained, fertile soil preferred. Full sun essential. Fertilize with low-nitrogen fertilizer (legumes fix nitrogen). Fast-growing (60-90 days). Can be harvested as green pods or dried beans. Very popular in Chinese cuisine. Can be sprouted for bean sprouts. Warm-season crop. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove diseased foliage promptly.

okra.description: Also known as: Lady's finger, Gumbo. Warm-season fruiting vegetable in the Malvaceae family with edible pods, also known as lady's finger, heat-loving.
okra.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week. Consistent moisture important during fruiting. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest pods when 2-4 inches long - daily harvesting encourages more production. Warm-season crop - very heat-loving. Tall plants may need staking. Watch for aphids and stink bugs. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

pattypan squash.description: Summer squash in the Cucurbitaceae family with scalloped, flying-saucer shape, mild flavor, harvest when small.
pattypan squash.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week. Consistent moisture important during fruiting. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest when 2-4 inches across for best flavor - tender and sweet. Bush habit, compact. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

peas.description: Also known as: Garden pea. Cool-season legume vegetables in the Fabaceae family, prefer cooler temperatures and need support for climbing varieties.
peas.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Water at base. Consistent moisture important during flowering and pod development. Full sun to partial shade. Prefer cooler temperatures - plant in early spring or fall. Provide trellis or support for climbing varieties. Fertilize sparingly - peas fix their own nitrogen. Harvest regularly when pods are plump. Ready in 60-70 days. Watch for aphids. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

scientific_names: various heat levels from sweet to very hot
peppers.description: Warm-season fruiting vegetables in the Solanaceae family, need consistent moisture and warm temperatures.
peppers.care_tips: Deep, regular watering at base (2-3 times per week). Keep consistently moist but well-drained. Avoid water stress which causes blossom drop. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Stake plants to support heavy fruit. Harvest when fruits reach desired size and color. Ready in 60-90 days. Watch for aphids and pepper maggots. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

poblano pepper.description: Mild Mexican chile pepper with wide, dark green, heart-shaped fruits that are essential in chiles rellenos, mole sauces, and when dried become the smoky-sweet ancho chile.
poblano pepper.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist; consistent watering prevents blossom end rot. Full sun essential—at least 6-8 hours daily for good fruit production. Medium humidity fine. Rich, well-draining soil. Fertilize at planting and side-dress with balanced fertilizer when first fruits set. Harvest when dark green for poblano or let ripen to red for ancho. Stake plants if heavy with fruit. Start seeds indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost. Mild heat (1,000-2,000 Scoville). Non-toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

pumpkin.description: Large winter squash in the Cucurbitaceae family, popular for Halloween decorations and cooking, require long growing season.
pumpkin.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week during growing season. Consistent moisture important during fruit development. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Vining plants require space (10+ feet). Harvest when fully mature and rind is hard. Cure in warm place for 2 weeks before storage. Warm-season crop - requires long growing season. Perfect for Halloween decorations. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

rhubarb.description: Perennial vegetable grown for its tart, red or green stalks used in pies, jams, and sauces. Only the stalks are edible — the leaves contain toxic oxalic acid.
rhubarb.care_tips: Water regularly — needs consistent moisture. Full sun to partial shade. Rich, well-draining soil with lots of compost. Do not harvest in the first year to let roots establish. Divide every 5-6 years. Leaves are toxic — only eat the stalks. Toxic to pets. Remove flower stalks as they appear so energy stays in the stalks; cut back dead foliage after frost.

roma tomato.description: Also known as: Plum tomato. Plum tomato in the Solanaceae family with meaty, low-moisture flesh, ideal for sauces, paste, and canning.
roma tomato.care_tips: Deep, regular watering at base (2-3 times per week). Avoid wetting leaves to prevent disease. Consistent moisture prevents blossom end rot. Full sun essential (8+ hours daily). Stake determinate varieties. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with tomato fertilizer. Harvest when fully red and firm. Meaty flesh, few seeds. Ideal for sauces. Prune suckers and lower leaves for better airflow; remove diseased foliage promptly. Foliage and green fruit are mildly toxic to pets; ripe fruit is safe.

serrano pepper.description: Medium-hot pepper (10,000-23,000 Scoville) commonly used in Mexican cuisine, especially salsas and pico de gallo. Smaller and hotter than jalapeños.
serrano pepper.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry; keep consistently moist during fruiting. Full sun (6-8 hours). Rich, well-draining soil. Harvest when green or red. Very productive — a single plant can yield 50+ peppers. Non-toxic. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

snap peas.description: Edible-podded peas in the Fabaceae family, entire pod is eaten, prefer cool weather.
snap peas.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture important. Well-drained, fertile soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Prefer cool weather - plant in early spring or fall. Fertilize with low-nitrogen fertilizer. Support with trellis. Harvest when pods are plump but before they become tough. Entire pod is eaten. Fast-growing (60-70 days). Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

snow peas.description: Also known as: Mangetout. Flat-podded peas in the Fabaceae family, entire pod is eaten, popular in Asian cuisine.
snow peas.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture important. Well-drained, fertile soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Prefer cool weather - plant in early spring or fall. Fertilize with low-nitrogen fertilizer. Support with trellis. Harvest when pods are flat and before seeds develop. Entire pod is eaten. Popular in Asian cuisine. Fast-growing (60-70 days). Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

spaghetti squash.description: Oval winter squash in the Cucurbitaceae family; cooked flesh separates into spaghetti-like strands, low-carb alternative.
spaghetti squash.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week during growing season. Consistent moisture important during fruit development. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest when rind is hard and pale yellow. Bake or boil; flesh strands like spaghetti. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

squash.description: Large fruiting vegetables in the Cucurbitaceae family, vining types need support or space to spread.
squash.care_tips: Regular deep watering at base (2-3 times per week). Keep consistently moist especially during fruit development. Avoid wetting leaves to prevent powdery mildew. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Vining types need support or space to spread (10+ feet). Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest summer squash when small and tender; winter squash when fully mature. Watch for squash bugs and powdery mildew. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing.
