Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

thai eggplant.description: Small, round eggplant varieties essential in Southeast Asian cuisine, producing golf-ball-sized green, white, or purple-striped fruits with a firm, slightly bitter flesh used in curries and stir-fries.
thai eggplant.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist; consistent watering is essential for fruit quality. Full sun—at least 6-8 hours daily. High humidity (60%+) preferred. Rich, well-draining soil with plenty of organic matter. Heavy feeder—fertilize every 2 weeks with balanced fertilizer once fruiting begins. Stake or cage plants as they become heavy with fruit. Harvest when fruits are firm and glossy; overripe fruits become seedy and bitter. Start seeds indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost. Leaves and stems are mildly toxic (solanine). Thin out seedlings promptly and remove overcrowded leaves.

tomatillo.description: Green husk tomato in the Solanaceae family, essential for salsa verde, tart flavor when ripe.
tomatillo.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture important during fruiting. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Plant at least two for pollination. Harvest when husks split and fruits fill the husk. Essential for salsa verde. Warm-season crop. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Sprawling, many-branched plants; stake or cage for support. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

tomatoes.description: Warm-season fruiting vegetables in the Solanaceae family, require consistent moisture and support for vining types.
tomatoes.care_tips: Deep, regular watering at base (2-3 times per week, daily in hot weather). Avoid wetting leaves to prevent disease (early blight, late blight). Consistent moisture prevents blossom end rot (calcium deficiency). Full sun essential (8+ hours daily). Stake or cage indeterminate varieties. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with tomato fertilizer. Mulch to retain moisture. Harvest when fully colored. Ready in 60-90 days. Watch for tomato hornworms and diseases. Prune suckers and lower leaves for better airflow; remove diseased foliage promptly. Foliage and green fruit are mildly toxic to pets; ripe fruit i

watermelon.description: Warm-season fruiting vegetable in the Cucurbitaceae family, large vining plants require space and a long growing season; yellow- and orange-fleshed cultivars are also grown.
watermelon.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week, increase during fruit development. Consistent moisture critical during fruiting. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Large vining plants require space. Harvest when tendril near stem turns brown and bottom sounds hollow when tapped. Warm-season crop - requires long growing season. Watch for aphids and cucumber beetles. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

yellow watermelon.description: Cultivar of watermelon in the Cucurbitaceae family with sweet yellow or orange flesh instead of red.
yellow watermelon.care_tips: Water deeply and consistently, providing 1-2 inches per week - critical during fruit development to prevent cracking and hollow heart. Full sun essential (8+ hours daily); needs long, hot growing season. Fertilize at planting with balanced fertilizer, then switch to a low-nitrogen, high-potassium formula when vines begin to flower. Give vines plenty of room to sprawl (6-10 feet in each direction) or train on a strong trellis with sling support for fruit. Ripe when the tendril nearest the fruit turns brown and dry, and the ground spot turns creamy yellow. Mulch heavily with straw to suppress we

winter melon.description: Also known as: Wax gourd. Large gourd in the Cucurbitaceae family with waxy coating, mild flavor, popular in Asian soups and stir-fries.
winter melon.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week. Consistent moisture important during fruiting. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Provide strong trellis for heavy fruits. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks. Harvest when fully sized; waxy coating aids storage. Popular in Asian cuisine. Warm-season crop. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

yard long bean.description: Also known as: Yard-long bean. Long Asian bean in the Fabaceae family, can reach 3 feet, similar to green beans but more heat-tolerant.
yard long bean.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture important during flowering and pod development. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Provide trellis for climbing habit. Fertilize with low-nitrogen fertilizer (legumes fix nitrogen). Harvest when pods are pencil-thick, before seeds bulge. Heat-tolerant. Popular in Asian cuisine. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove diseased foliage promptly.

zucchini.description: Also known as: Summer squash, Courgette. Summer squash in the Cucurbitaceae family, fast-growing and prolific, harvest when small for best flavor.
zucchini.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week. Consistent moisture important during fruiting. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest when 6-8 inches long for best flavor - daily harvesting encourages more production. Fast-growing and prolific. Male and female flowers. Watch for squash bugs and vine borers. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

beets.description: Also known as: Garden beet, Red beet. Root vegetables in the Amaranthaceae family, both roots and greens are edible, prefer cool weather.
beets.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture prevents woody roots. Water at base. Well-drained, loose soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize with balanced fertilizer. Thin seedlings to 3-4 inches apart. Harvest roots when 2-3 inches in diameter. Both roots and greens are edible. Prefer cool weather - plant in spring or fall. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

carrots.description: Root vegetables in the Apiaceae family, require deep, loose soil free of rocks for straight roots.
carrots.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture prevents splitting. Water deeply to encourage long roots. Deep, loose, rock-free soil essential. Full sun preferred. Fertilize with low-nitrogen fertilizer - too much nitrogen causes forked roots. Thin seedlings to 2-3 inches apart. Harvest when roots reach desired size. Can be left in ground in mild climates. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

celeriac.description: Celery root in the Apiaceae family, grown for its edible swollen stem base with celery-like flavor, popular in European cuisine.
celeriac.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture important for bulb development. Well-drained, fertile soil preferred. Full sun essential. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Hill soil around base as it grows. Harvest when bulb is 3-4 inches in diameter. Long growing season (100-120 days). Peel before cooking. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

daikon.description: Also known as: Mooli, Chinese radish. Large white radishes in the Brassicaceae family, popular in Asian cuisine, fast-growing.
daikon.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture prevents pithy roots. Well-drained, loose soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize with balanced fertilizer. Thin seedlings to 4-6 inches apart. Harvest when roots are 6-12 inches long. Fast-growing (50-70 days). Popular in Asian cuisine. Can be stored for weeks. Prefer cool weather. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

fennel.description: Also known as: Finocchio. Bulb vegetables in the Apiaceae family with licorice flavor, both bulb and fronds are edible.
fennel.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture important for bulb development. Well-drained, fertile soil preferred. Full sun essential. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest when bulb is 3-4 inches in diameter. Both bulb and fronds are edible. Licorice flavor. Can bolt in heat - plant in spring or fall. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

garlic.description: Essential culinary bulb in the Allium family, planted in fall and harvested the following summer; hardneck types produce flavorful scapes, softneck types store longer.
garlic.care_tips: Plant individual cloves in fall, 6-8 weeks before the ground freezes, pointed end up, 5-8 cm deep, 15 cm apart. Water consistently during spring growth; keep soil evenly moist but not waterlogged. Stop watering 2-3 weeks before harvest when lower leaves turn brown. Full sun is essential. Fertile, well-drained loamy soil amended with compost is ideal. Cut hardneck scapes in early summer to direct energy to bulb formation. Harvest when lower third of leaves have browned. Cure in a warm, dry, ventilated area for 2-3 weeks. Toxic to pets — all Alliums are harmful to cats and dogs. Remove dead or d

horseradish.description: Perennial root in the Brassicaceae family with pungent, spicy roots used for condiments, can spread aggressively.
horseradish.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Well-drained, deep soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize sparingly. Perennial - harvest roots in fall after frost. Can become invasive; consider containers or barriers. Grate roots when fresh for strongest flavor. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

jerusalem artichoke.description: Also known as: Sunchoke. Perennial sunflower relative in the Asteraceae family, grown for edible tubers (sunchokes), nutty flavor, can spread readily.
jerusalem artichoke.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in spring. Perennial - harvest tubers after frost when plants die back. Can naturalize; contain with barriers if needed. Harvest as needed; stores in ground. Nutty, slightly sweet. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Cut stalks to the ground after frost; tubers can be left in the ground and dug as needed.

kohlrabi.description: Unique vegetables in the Brassicaceae family with swollen stem base, both bulb and leaves are edible, fast-growing.
kohlrabi.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture important for tender bulbs. Well-drained, fertile soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest when bulb is 2-3 inches in diameter for best flavor. Both bulb and leaves are edible. Fast-growing (45-60 days). Prefer cool weather. Watch for cabbage worms. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Trim flower stalks if they appear to redirect energy to root development.

leek.description: Mild-flavored allium with a long white shaft and fan of flat green leaves. A staple in European cooking, especially French cuisine (vichyssoise, leek and potato soup).
leek.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil consistently moist. Full sun. Rich, well-draining soil. Hill soil around the base (blanching) to extend the white edible portion. Long growing season (90-120 days). Frost tolerant. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

onions garlic.description: Bulb vegetables in the Amaryllidaceae family, reduce watering as bulbs mature to prevent rot.
onions garlic.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist during growth (2-3 times per week). Reduce watering significantly as tops begin to yellow and bulbs mature - this allows bulbs to cure and prevents rot. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize monthly with balanced fertilizer until bulbs form. Plant garlic in fall for summer harvest; onions in spring. Harvest when tops fall over. Cure bulbs in dry, airy location. Toxic to pets. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

parsnip.description: Root vegetables in the Apiaceae family, flavor improves after frost, require long growing season.
parsnip.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture prevents splitting. Deep, loose, rock-free soil essential. Full sun preferred. Fertilize with low-nitrogen fertilizer. Thin seedlings to 3-4 inches apart. Harvest after first frost for best flavor - can be left in ground over winter. Flavor improves after frost. Requires long growing season (100-120 days). Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Trim flower stalks if they appear to redirect energy to root development.

potatoes.description: Underground tuber vegetables in the Solanaceae family, require hilling (mounding soil) around stems as they grow.
potatoes.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture prevents hollow heart and ensures uniform tuber development. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Hill (mound soil) around stems as they grow to protect developing tubers from sunlight (which causes greening). Fertilize at planting and when hilling. Harvest when plants die back. Store in cool, dark place. Ready in 70-120 days depending on variety. Watch for potato beetles. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Harvest once most of the foliage has yellowed and died back. Green tubers and foliage are m

radishes.description: Fast-growing root vegetables in the Brassicaceae family, prefer cool weather and can be planted multiple times per season.
radishes.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture prevents pithy roots. Water at base. Well-drained, loose soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize with balanced fertilizer. Thin seedlings to 1-2 inches apart. Harvest when roots reach size (20-60 days depending on variety). Fast-growing. Prefer cool weather - plant in spring or fall. Can be planted multiple times per season. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

root vegetables.description: Vegetables grown for their edible underground parts, require loose well-drained soil for proper root development.
root vegetables.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture prevents splitting and ensures uniform growth. Loose, well-drained soil essential - avoid heavy clay. Full sun preferred. Thin seedlings to proper spacing for root development. Fertilize sparingly - too much nitrogen causes leafy growth at expense of roots. Harvest when roots reach desired size. Ready in 30-120 days depending on variety. Research specific vegetable for exact requirements. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

rutabaga.description: Also known as: Swede, Neep. Root vegetables in the Brassicaceae family, cross between turnip and cabbage, prefer cool weather.
rutabaga.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture prevents woody roots. Well-drained, loose soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize with balanced fertilizer. Thin seedlings to 6-8 inches apart. Harvest when roots are 3-5 inches in diameter. Prefer cool weather - plant in early spring or late summer. Flavor improves after frost. Can be stored for months. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Trim flower stalks if they appear to redirect energy to root development.

salsify.description: Also known as: Oyster plant. Root vegetable in the Asteraceae family with long white roots and oyster-like flavor.
salsify.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Deep, loose, rock-free soil essential. Full sun preferred. Fertilize with low-nitrogen fertilizer. Thin seedlings to 4-6 inches apart. Long growing season (120 days). Harvest when roots are 8-12 inches long. Oyster-like flavor when cooked. Can be left in ground over winter. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

scallion green onion.description: Allium with mild edible green tops and white bases, used fresh in many cuisines.
scallion green onion.care_tips: Keep soil moist. Full sun. Fast-growing. Harvest when tops are 6-8 inches. Can regrow from roots. Popular in Asian cooking. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly. Toxic to pets.

shallot.description: Mild, sweet-flavored member of the Allium family that forms clusters of small, elongated bulbs prized in French and Asian cuisine for their delicate flavor.
shallot.care_tips: Water regularly during active growth; keep soil moist but not waterlogged. Reduce watering as tops begin to yellow and fall over — this signals maturation. Full sun (6+ hours) is essential. Loose, well-drained, fertile soil is ideal; amend heavy soil with compost. Plant sets 15 cm apart in early spring or fall (fall planting yields larger bulbs). Fertilize at planting with balanced fertilizer; side-dress with nitrogen-rich fertilizer in mid-spring. Harvest when tops dry and fall over. Toxic to pets — all Alliums are harmful to cats and dogs. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

sweet potatoes.description: Warm-season root vegetables in the Convolvulaceae family, also commonly called yams, require long growing season.
sweet potatoes.care_tips: Water deeply 2-3 times per week during growing season. Consistent moisture important during root development. Mulch around plants. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize with low-nitrogen fertilizer. Plant slips (rooted cuttings) after soil warms. Vining plants require space. Harvest before first frost when leaves start to yellow. Cure in warm, humid place for 2 weeks. Warm-season crop - requires long growing season. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

taro.description: Also known as: Dasheen, Eddoe. Starchy root crop (corm) staple in Pacific and Asian cuisines; leaves and corms must be cooked before eating.
taro.care_tips: Wet or very moist soil. Partial sun. Warm temperatures. Harvest when leaves yellow. All parts contain calcium oxalate - must cook before eating. Toxic raw. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

turnips.description: Also known as: White turnip. Root vegetables in the Brassicaceae family, both roots and greens are edible, prefer cool weather.
turnips.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture prevents woody roots. Water at base. Well-drained, loose soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize with balanced fertilizer. Thin seedlings to 4-6 inches apart. Harvest roots when 2-3 inches in diameter. Both roots and greens are edible. Prefer cool weather - plant in spring or fall. Flavor improves after frost. Seasonal crop; watering varies by growing zone and harvest timing. Trim flower stalks if they appear to redirect energy to root development.

yam.description: Also known as: True yam, Ñame, Ube. Tropical climbing vines in the Dioscoreaceae family grown for their large starchy tubers, a staple in West Africa, the Caribbean, and Asia; unrelated to the sweet potato often called yam in North America.
yam.care_tips: Water deeply once or twice a week during the growing season; tubers rot in waterlogged soil. Full sun. Needs 8-11 frost-free months at 20-32°C; Chinese yam is the exception and is hardy to zone 5. High humidity suits the tropical species. Fertilize with a balanced fertilizer at planting and again when vines are 1 m tall. Deep, loose, well-draining soil or raised mounds for straight tubers. Provide a tall trellis or stakes for the twining vines. Harvest when the foliage yellows and dies back, digging carefully to avoid bruising. Mildly toxic to pets and humans when raw; tubers must be peeled an

apples.description: Deciduous fruit trees in the Rosaceae family, require cross-pollination for most varieties, need winter chill.
apples.care_tips: Deep soak weekly during growing season. Increase watering during fruit development. Mulch around base. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in early spring with fruit tree fertilizer. Prune in late winter/early spring to maintain shape and encourage fruiting. Most varieties need cross-pollination - plant 2+ compatible varieties nearby. Thin fruit for larger, healthier apples. Protect from late frosts during flowering. Harvest when easily twists off branch. Reduce watering when dormant in winter. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

apricot.description: Deciduous fruit trees in the Rosaceae family with velvety skin, early bloomers susceptible to frost.
apricot.care_tips: Deep soak weekly during growing season. Increase watering during fruit development. Mulch around base. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in early spring with fruit tree fertilizer. Prune in late winter/early spring. Most varieties are self-fertile. Early bloomers - very susceptible to late frosts. Harvest when fully colored and slightly soft. Requires winter chill but blooms early. Reduce watering when dormant in winter. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

avocado.description: Evergreen fruit trees in the Lauraceae family, require warm climates, popular for guacamole and salads.
avocado.care_tips: Deep soak weekly during growing season. Well-drained soil essential - avoid waterlogged conditions. Mulch around base. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in early spring and summer with avocado fertilizer. Prune to maintain size. Most varieties need cross-pollination. Harvest when mature (varies by variety). Require warm climates - protect from frost. Can be grown in containers in cooler climates. Evergreen; reduce watering in winter when growth slows. Toxic to pets.

banana.description: Tropical herb in the Musaceae family producing bunches of sweet fruits, each stem fruits once then is replaced by suckers.
banana.care_tips: Water deeply and frequently - bananas need consistently moist soil and are heavy drinkers, especially in warm weather. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Feed every 2 weeks with a potassium-rich fertilizer during the growing season, as bananas are extremely heavy feeders. Each pseudostem fruits only once; after harvest, cut the fruited stalk to the ground and allow a sucker to replace it. Mulch heavily to retain moisture and protect the shallow root system. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

blackberries.description: Also known as: Blackberry. Perennial cane fruits in the Rosaceae family, produce fruit on second-year canes, can be trailing or erect varieties.
blackberries.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (weekly deep watering). Water at base to avoid wetting fruit. Mulch around plants to retain moisture. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in early spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune fruited canes after harvest in summer. Support trailing varieties with trellis. Harvest when fully black and easily detaches. Can spread aggressively - contain with barriers. Replace plants every 8-10 years. Deciduous varieties: reduce watering when dormant in winter.

blueberries.description: Acidic soil-loving berry shrubs in the Ericaceae family, require pH 4.5-5.5 and often need cross-pollination.
blueberries.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (weekly deep watering). Use acidic water if needed to maintain soil pH. Mulch with pine needles, pine bark, or sawdust to maintain acidity and moisture. Soil pH 4.5-5.5 essential - test and amend annually. Full sun preferred (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in early spring with acid-loving plant fertilizer. Many varieties need cross-pollination - plant 2+ compatible varieties. Prune in late winter. Harvest when fully blue. Research specific variety for exact requirements. Deciduous varieties: reduce watering when dormant in winter.

calamondin.description: Also known as: Calamansi, Philippine lime, Calamondin orange. Small ornamental citrus, a natural kumquat and mandarin hybrid, that carries fragrant white flowers and tart, thin-skinned orange fruits almost year-round; a favorite indoor citrus and the souring agent of Filipino cooking.
calamondin.care_tips: Water when the top 3-5 cm of soil is dry, then soak until it drains; never let the pot stand in water. Full sun outdoors or the brightest window indoors (6+ hours), with a grow light in winter. Keep at 15-30°C; tolerates brief dips to about -2°C. Medium humidity (40-50%); mist or use a humidity tray in heated rooms. Feed every 4-6 weeks spring to autumn with a citrus fertilizer containing micronutrients; yellow leaves with green veins mean iron or magnesium deficiency. Slightly acidic, fast-draining citrus mix. Hand-pollinate indoor flowers with a soft brush for heavier crops. Fruit ripens ove

cherimoya.description: Also known as: Custard apple, Chirimoya. Subtropical fruit tree in the Annonaceae family bearing heart-shaped green fruits with creamy white flesh that tastes like banana, pineapple, and vanilla custard; related to atemoya, sugar apple, and soursop.
cherimoya.care_tips: Water deeply every week or two during the growing season and cut back during the winter leaf drop; never let the soil stay waterlogged. Full sun, with light shade for young trees in hot inland areas. Best at 10-30°C with cool nights; mature trees tolerate brief frost to about -3°C, but fruit and flowers are damaged below 0°C. Medium humidity; fruit set fails in very dry heat. Feed young trees every 2-3 months and bearing trees in spring and summer with a balanced fertilizer. Deep, well-draining loam. Flowers are rarely pollinated well by local insects, so hand-pollinate in the evening with pol

cherries.description: Deciduous fruit trees in the Rosaceae family, sweet and sour varieties, require winter chill and often need cross-pollination.
cherries.care_tips: Deep soak weekly during growing season. Consistent moisture important during fruit development. Mulch around base. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in early spring with fruit tree fertilizer. Prune in late winter/early spring. Many varieties need cross-pollination - plant compatible varieties nearby. Protect from birds with netting. Harvest when fully colored. Sweet cherries are more challenging than sour cherries. Research specific variety for exact requirements. Reduce watering when dormant in winter. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

coconut.description: Tropical palm in the Arecaceae family producing large drupes with edible meat and water, requires warm coastal climate.
coconut.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged - young palms need more frequent watering than established trees. Full sun essential (at least 6 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 months with a palm-specific fertilizer rich in potassium, manganese, and magnesium. Thrives in sandy, well-draining soil and tolerates salt spray, making it ideal for coastal areas. Requires consistently warm temperatures above 22°C year-round; will not tolerate frost. Do not prune green fronds - only remove dead brown ones. Non-toxic to pets.

cranberry.description: Low-growing evergreen shrubs in the Ericaceae family, require acidic soil and constant moisture, popular for Thanksgiving.
cranberry.care_tips: Keep soil constantly moist - never allow to dry out. Acidic soil (pH 4.0-5.5) essential. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize in spring with acid-loving plant fertilizer. Mulch with pine needles or peat moss. Can be grown in boggy conditions. Harvest in fall when berries are fully red. Popular for Thanksgiving. Very challenging to grow outside native bog conditions. Evergreen; reduce watering in winter when growth slows. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

currant.description: Also known as: Redcurrant, Blackcurrant. Deciduous shrubs in the Grossulariaceae family with red, black, or white berries, used for jams and fresh eating.
currant.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil consistently moist, especially during fruiting - about 1 inch per week. Partial shade to full sun; currants actually prefer some afternoon shade in hot climates, unlike most fruit. Fertilize in early spring with a balanced fertilizer and side-dress with compost. Prune out wood older than 3 years in late winter to encourage productive new growth. Mulch heavily to keep roots cool, as currants prefer cooler conditions. Excellent for cold-climate gardens where many fruits struggle. Non-toxic to pets.

dates.description: Date palm in the Arecaceae family producing sweet drupes, desert-adapted, requires hot dry climate.
dates.care_tips: Water deeply but infrequently once established - date palms are extremely drought tolerant and overwatering causes root rot. Full sun essential; requires intense heat for fruit to ripen properly. Fertilize 2-3 times per year with palm fertilizer. Thrives in hot, arid conditions with low humidity; fruit quality suffers in humid or rainy climates. Needs both male and female trees for pollination, or hand-pollinate for reliable fruit set. Tolerates poor, alkaline soils but requires excellent drainage. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

scientific_names: Selenicereus undatus (syn. Selenicereus undatus (syn. Hylocereus undatus); White-fleshed dragon fruit)
S. costaricensis (syn. S. costaricensis (syn. H. costaricensis); Red-fleshed)
dragon fruit.description: Also known as: White-fleshed dragon fruit. Cactus fruits in the Cactaceae family, also known as pitaya, popular tropical fruit with striking appearance.
dragon fruit.care_tips: Water deeply but infrequently (every 1-2 weeks). Very drought tolerant. Well-drained soil essential. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize monthly during growing season with cactus fertilizer. Provide support for climbing habit. Self-fertile but cross-pollination improves yield. Harvest when fully colored and slightly soft. Require warm climates. Popular tropical fruit. Evergreen; reduce watering in winter when growth slows. Remove dead or rotting sections promptly.

durian.description: Legendary tropical fruit famous for its custard-like flesh and notoriously pungent aroma—banned on public transport across Southeast Asia but revered as a delicacy.
durian.care_tips: Water regularly and deeply; needs consistent moisture during flowering and fruiting. Full sun essential for fruit production. Very high humidity (80%+) required—strictly tropical. Deep, well-draining, acidic clay-loam soil (pH 5.0-6.5). Fertilize regularly with balanced fertilizer; increase potassium during fruiting. Extremely tall tree (25-40 meters)—not practical for containers. Fruit takes 3-5 months to ripen after pollination. Pollinated by bats at night. First fruit after 5-7 years from seed. Non-toxic to pets. Prune during dormancy. Remove dead and diseased wood. Thin to improve fruit si

elderberry.description: Deciduous shrubs in the Adoxaceae family with clusters of dark berries, popular for health benefits and jellies.
elderberry.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (weekly deep watering). Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize in early spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune in late winter to remove old canes. Most varieties need cross-pollination - plant 2+ varieties. Harvest clusters when fully ripe (dark purple/black). Berries must be cooked before eating. Toxic to pets - raw berries, leaves, stems contain cyanogenic glycosides. Popular for health benefits and jellies. Deciduous varieties: reduce watering when dormant in winter.

scientific_names: Feijoa sellowiana (syn. Acca sellowiana; Pineapple guava)
feijoa.description: Also known as: Pineapple guava, Guavasteen. Evergreen shrub or small tree in the Myrtaceae family with silvery leaves, edible red-and-white flowers, and green egg-shaped fruits that taste of pineapple, guava, and mint; a backyard staple in New Zealand and a tough ornamental hedge.
feijoa.care_tips: Water deeply every week or two in summer, especially while fruit is swelling; drought stress drops fruit. Full sun for the best crop; tolerates partial shade. Hardy to about -10°C once established and tolerates heat; needs some winter chill (under 7°C) to fruit well. Medium humidity. Feed in spring and midsummer with a balanced fertilizer. Well-draining soil of any type; tolerates salt spray and wind. Plant two cultivars for reliable pollination unless self-fertile; birds pollinate by eating the sweet petals. Fruit drops when ripe in autumn, so gather from the ground. Non-toxic to pets. Prune

fig.description: Deciduous fruit trees in the Moraceae family, can be grown in containers, some varieties produce two crops.
fig.care_tips: Deep soak weekly during growing season. Consistent moisture important during fruit development. Mulch around base. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in early spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune in late winter. Self-fertile. Some varieties produce two crops (breba and main crop). Can be grown in containers. Harvest when soft and drooping. Protect from cold in winter if needed. Deciduous; reduce or withhold watering when leaves drop in fall. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

goji berry.description: Also known as: Wolfberry. Deciduous shrubs in the Solanaceae family, also known as wolfberry, popular superfood, drought-tolerant.
goji berry.care_tips: Water deeply but infrequently once established (every 1-2 weeks). Very drought tolerant. Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun essential. Fertilize in spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune in late winter to maintain shape. Self-fertile. Harvest berries when fully red. Popular superfood. Can be grown in containers. Very popular in China. Deciduous varieties: reduce watering when dormant in winter.

gooseberry.description: Deciduous shrub in the Grossulariaceae family with tart green or red berries, popular for pies and preserves.
gooseberry.care_tips: Water consistently to keep soil evenly moist, about 1 inch per week - drought stress causes premature fruit drop. Partial shade to full sun; tolerates more shade than most fruit bushes, and benefits from afternoon shade in warmer zones. Fertilize lightly in early spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune in late winter to maintain an open, goblet-shaped form for air circulation - this reduces mildew, which gooseberries are prone to. Wear thick gloves when harvesting due to sharp thorns. Mulch to keep roots cool in summer. Non-toxic to pets.

grapefruit.description: Large evergreen citrus tree producing clusters of large, tangy-sweet fruits with pink, red, or white flesh. Needs sustained heat for sweetest fruit.
grapefruit.care_tips: Water deeply every 7-10 days; consistent moisture during fruit development. Full sun essential — needs more heat than other citrus for sweetest fruit. Well-drained, acidic soil. Fertilize 3-4 times per year with citrus fertilizer. Prune to remove dead wood and maintain airflow. Fruits can remain on the tree for months after ripening. Interacts with many medications (furanocoumarins inhibit drug metabolism). Mildly toxic to pets.

grapes.description: Also known as: Wine grape. Perennial climbing vines in the Vitaceae family, produce clusters of berries, require pruning and support structures.
grapes.care_tips: Deep watering weekly during growing season. Consistent moisture important during fruit development. Mulch around base. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in early spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune heavily in late winter - grapes fruit on new growth from previous year's wood. Provide strong support (trellis, arbor). Harvest when fully ripe and sweet. Many varieties need winter chill. Research specific variety for exact pruning requirements. Deciduous varieties: reduce watering when dormant in winter. Toxic to pets.

guava.description: Tropical tree in the Myrtaceae family with fragrant pink or white-fleshed fruits, fast-growing and adaptable.
guava.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil moist but not waterlogged during the growing season; reduce watering in winter. Full sun essential for best fruit production (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 1-2 months during the growing season with a balanced fertilizer - guavas are moderate feeders. Prune lightly to shape and to improve air circulation, which reduces disease. Guavas are remarkably adaptable and can fruit within 2-3 years from seed. Protect from frost; mature trees tolerate brief dips to -2°C but young trees are more tender. Non-toxic to pets.

jackfruit.description: The world's largest tree-borne fruit, with individual fruits weighing up to 35 kg. A tropical evergreen producing sweet, aromatic golden flesh used fresh, dried, or as a popular meat substitute when young and unripe.
jackfruit.care_tips: Water regularly during growing season; keep soil evenly moist but never waterlogged. Full sun essential for fruit production. High humidity (60%+) preferred. Deep, well-draining, fertile soil. Fertilize quarterly with balanced fertilizer, increasing potassium during fruiting. Young trees are frost-sensitive—protect below 10°C. Fruits grow directly from the trunk (cauliflory). Can grow 15-20 meters tall; choose dwarf cultivars for containers. Latex sap is sticky—oil hands before handling fruit. Non-toxic to pets. Prune during dormancy; remove dead and diseased wood and thin to improve fruit siz

jujube.description: Also known as: Chinese date, Red date. Deciduous fruit trees in the Rhamnaceae family, also known as Chinese date or red date, drought-tolerant.
jujube.care_tips: Deep soak weekly during growing season. Drought tolerant once established. Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun essential. Fertilize in early spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune to maintain shape. Self-fertile but better with cross-pollination. Harvest when fully red and slightly wrinkled. Can be eaten fresh or dried. Very popular in China. Drought tolerant. Deciduous; reduce or withhold watering when leaves drop in fall.

kiwi.description: Also known as: Kiwifruit. Vining fruit in the Actinidiaceae family with fuzzy brown fruit and green flesh, requires male and female plants.
kiwi.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil consistently moist but well-drained; kiwis have shallow roots and are sensitive to drought. Full sun to partial shade, with protection from strong winds. Fertilize in spring with a balanced fertilizer - avoid over-fertilizing which promotes leaf growth over fruit. Both male and female vines are required for pollination (one male can pollinate up to 8 females). Provide a sturdy trellis or pergola, as mature vines become extremely heavy. Prune vigorously in winter and lightly in summer to control rampant growth. Non-toxic to pets.

kumquat.description: Small citrus trees in the Rutaceae family, entire fruit is edible including peel, cold-hardier than most citrus.
kumquat.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist during growing season. Well-drained soil essential. Full sun essential. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with citrus fertilizer. Prune to maintain size. Self-fertile. Harvest when fully orange. Entire fruit is edible including peel. Cold-hardier than most citrus - can tolerate light frosts. Can be grown in containers. Evergreen; reduce watering in winter when growth slows.

lemon tree.description: Evergreen citrus tree producing tart yellow fruits year-round in warm climates. One of the most popular container fruit trees for patios and conservatories.
lemon tree.care_tips: Water deeply when top 2 inches of soil are dry; do not let roots sit in water. Full sun essential (8+ hours for best fruiting). Acidic, well-drained soil (pH 5.5-6.5). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with citrus-specific fertilizer high in nitrogen. Prune to shape and remove suckers below the graft. Protect from frost — Meyer lemon tolerates brief dips to -3°C; Eureka is more cold-sensitive. Yellow leaves often indicate iron deficiency (use chelated iron). Excellent container plant; dwarf varieties fruit well in pots. Mildly toxic to pets (essential oils and psoralen in peel).

lime tree.description: Evergreen citrus tree producing small, green, intensely tart fruits essential in cuisines worldwide. More cold-sensitive than lemons or oranges.
lime tree.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged. Full sun essential (6-8 hours). Acidic, well-drained soil. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with citrus fertilizer. More cold-sensitive than other citrus — protect below 10°C. Key limes are smaller, more aromatic, and seedier; Persian limes are the standard grocery variety (seedless). Excellent container plant — dwarf varieties thrive in pots and can be brought indoors in winter. Mildly toxic to pets. Prune during dormancy. Remove dead and diseased wood. Thin to improve fruit size and air circulation.

longan.description: Also known as: Dragon's eye. Evergreen fruit trees in the Sapindaceae family, related to lychee, require tropical or subtropical climate.
longan.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist during growing season. Well-drained, slightly acidic soil preferred. Full sun essential. Fertilize in spring and summer with balanced fertilizer. Prune to maintain size. Self-fertile. Harvest when skin is brown and fruit is sweet. Require tropical or subtropical climate. Related to lychee. Popular in Chinese cuisine. Evergreen; reduce watering in winter when growth slows.

loquat.description: Also known as: Chinese plum. Evergreen fruit trees in the Rosaceae family with sweet, tangy fruits, popular in China and Japan.
loquat.care_tips: Deep soak weekly during growing season. Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize in spring and summer with balanced fertilizer. Prune to maintain size and shape. Self-fertile. Harvest when fully yellow-orange and slightly soft. Can tolerate some cold but protect from hard freezes. Popular in China and Japan. Evergreen; reduce watering in winter when growth slows.

lychee.description: Also known as: Lichi. Evergreen fruit trees in the Sapindaceae family with sweet, fragrant fruits, require tropical or subtropical climate.
lychee.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist during growing season. Well-drained, acidic soil preferred. Full sun essential. Fertilize in spring and summer with citrus fertilizer. Prune to maintain size. Self-fertile but cross-pollination improves yield. Harvest when skin is pink-red and fruit is fragrant. Require tropical or subtropical climate - protect from frost. Very popular in China. Evergreen; reduce watering in winter when growth slows.

makrut lime.description: Also known as: Kaffir lime, Thai lime, Limau purut. Thorny citrus in the Rutaceae family grown for its glossy double-lobed leaves and knobbly green fruit rind, the signature aromatics of Thai curries, tom yum, and Indonesian cooking; the juice is scarce and bitter, so it is a leaf-and-zest tree.
makrut lime.care_tips: Water when the top 3-5 cm of soil is dry, then water deeply; never leave the pot standing in water. Full sun outdoors or the brightest window plus a grow light indoors. Thrives at 15-32°C; tolerates brief dips to about -2°C, so pot-grow and overwinter indoors outside zones 9-11. Medium humidity (40-50%); mist in dry heated rooms. Feed every 4-6 weeks spring to autumn with a citrus fertilizer containing micronutrients. Slightly acidic, fast-draining citrus mix. Watch for scale, leaf miner, and spider mites. Harvest leaves year-round, taking no more than a third at a time; leaves and whole fruit

mandarin.description: Also known as: Tangerine. Evergreen citrus tree producing easy-to-peel, sweet, segmented fruits. The most diverse citrus group and generally the most cold-hardy.
mandarin.care_tips: Water deeply when top 2 inches of soil are dry; reduce in winter. Full sun essential. Acidic, well-drained soil. Fertilize 3-4 times per year with citrus fertilizer. The most cold-hardy citrus group — satsumas tolerate brief dips to -8°C. Easy-to-peel fruits are among the sweetest citrus. Many varieties are seedless. Excellent for containers. Harvest when fruit is fully colored and slightly soft. Mildly toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

mango.description: Tropical tree in the Anacardiaceae family with sweet orange-fleshed drupes, widely cultivated fruit.
mango.care_tips: Water deeply once or twice per week during the growing season, then reduce significantly during winter dormancy - mangoes prefer a distinct dry period to stimulate flowering. Full sun essential (8+ hours daily). Fertilize 3-4 times per year with a citrus or fruit tree fertilizer. Caution: mango sap and skin contain urushiol (the same compound as poison ivy) and can cause contact dermatitis - wear gloves when pruning. Prune after harvest to maintain manageable size. Protect from frost; tropical tree that needs consistently warm temperatures. Mildly toxic to pets; sap and skin can cause irritati

mulberry.description: Deciduous tree in the Moraceae family with sweet black, red, or white berry-like fruits, fast-growing.
mulberry.care_tips: Water regularly during the first two years to establish; mature trees are quite drought tolerant. Full sun to partial shade (6+ hours daily). Fertilize once in late winter with a balanced fertilizer - mulberries are not heavy feeders and over-fertilizing reduces fruit quality. Prune in winter to shape and remove crossing branches. Mulberries fruit prolifically and fruit stains everything it touches - avoid planting near walkways, driveways, or patios. Fast-growing trees that can reach 30-50 feet; consider dwarf cultivars for smaller spaces. Non-toxic to pets; unripe fruit and raw leaves may ca

nectarine.description: Smooth-skinned peaches in the Rosaceae family, genetic variant of peach, require winter chill.
nectarine.care_tips: Deep soak weekly during growing season. Increase watering during fruit development. Mulch around base. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in early spring with fruit tree fertilizer. Prune in late winter/early spring. Most varieties are self-fertile. Smooth skin unlike peaches. Thin fruit for larger nectarines. Protect from late frosts during flowering. Harvest when fully colored. Requires winter chill. Reduce watering when dormant in winter. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

olive.description: Evergreen tree in the Oleaceae family producing drupes for oil and table olives, Mediterranean origin.
olive.care_tips: Water deeply but infrequently once established - olives are very drought tolerant and overwatering is the most common mistake. Full sun essential (8+ hours daily). Fertilize lightly in spring with a balanced or nitrogen-focused fertilizer. Thrives in poor, rocky, well-draining soil; heavy clay causes root rot. Prune annually in late winter to maintain an open center and promote air circulation. Requires winter chill hours (200-700 depending on variety) and warm, dry summers for fruit set. Extremely long-lived - can produce for centuries. Non-toxic to pets.

orange tree.description: Evergreen citrus tree producing sweet, juicy fruits — the world's most produced citrus. Fragrant white blossoms and glossy dark green foliage.
orange tree.care_tips: Water deeply when top 2 inches of soil are dry; consistent moisture important during fruit development. Full sun essential (6-8 hours). Acidic, well-drained soil preferred. Fertilize 3-4 times per year with citrus fertilizer. Prune sparingly — mainly remove dead wood and suckers. Protect from hard frost; mature trees tolerate brief dips to -3°C. Navel oranges are best eaten fresh; Valencia is preferred for juice. Trees can fruit and flower simultaneously. Mildly toxic to pets.

papaya.description: Tropical herbaceous tree in the Caricaceae family with orange-fleshed fruits, fast-growing.
papaya.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil consistently moist but never waterlogged - papayas have fleshy trunks that rot easily in soggy conditions. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Feed heavily every 2 weeks with balanced fertilizer, as papayas are extremely fast growers that fruit within 6-12 months from seed. Excellent drainage is critical; plant on a mound if soil is heavy. Protect from wind, which can topple the shallow-rooted trunk. Cannot tolerate any frost - even brief exposure below 0°C is fatal. Toxic to pets; latex in unripe fruit and leaves is harmful. Remove dead or damaged foliage prompt

passion fruit.description: Tropical vine in the Passifloraceae family with tart-sweet purple or yellow fruits, exotic flavor.
passion fruit.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil evenly moist during the growing season; reduce in winter. Full sun essential for maximum flowering and fruit set (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 4-6 weeks during the growing season with a fertilizer low in nitrogen but high in potassium and phosphorus to promote fruiting over vine growth. Provide a strong trellis or fence for climbing, as vines grow vigorously up to 20 feet per season. Most varieties need cross-pollination from a different cultivar for reliable fruit set. Fruits are ripe when they fall from the vine or the skin wrinkles. Non-toxic to pets; unrip

pawpaw.description: Native North American tree in the Annonaceae family with custard-like tropical-flavored fruits.
pawpaw.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil consistently moist - pawpaws are understory trees naturally found along stream banks and do not tolerate drought well. Partial shade when young, transitioning to full sun for fruiting as the tree matures. Fertilize in spring with a balanced organic fertilizer; avoid high-nitrogen synthetic fertilizers. Needs a different genetic individual (not just a different branch) for cross-pollination; plant at least two unrelated seedlings. Flowers are pollinated by flies and beetles, not bees - some growers hang rotting meat near blooms to attract pollinators. Fruit bruises

peach.description: Deciduous fruit trees in the Rosaceae family with fuzzy skin and sweet flesh, require winter chill.
peach.care_tips: Deep soak weekly during growing season. Increase watering during fruit development. Mulch around base. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in early spring with fruit tree fertilizer. Prune in late winter/early spring. Most varieties are self-fertile. Thin fruit for larger peaches. Protect from late frosts during flowering. Harvest when easily twists off branch. Requires winter chill. Reduce watering when dormant in winter. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

pear.description: Deciduous fruit trees in the Rosaceae family with sweet, juicy flesh, most varieties need cross-pollination.
pear.care_tips: Deep soak weekly during growing season. Increase watering during fruit development. Mulch around base. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in early spring with fruit tree fertilizer. Prune in late winter/early spring. Most varieties need cross-pollination - plant compatible varieties. Harvest when mature but still firm - ripen off tree. Requires winter chill. Research specific type (European vs Asian) for exact requirements. Reduce watering when dormant in winter.

persimmon.description: Deciduous fruit trees in the Ebenaceae family, astringent and non-astringent varieties, popular in both USA and China.
persimmon.care_tips: Deep soak weekly during growing season. Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun essential. Fertilize in early spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune to maintain shape. Most varieties are self-fertile. Harvest astringent varieties when very soft; non-astringent when firm. Popular in both USA and China. Requires winter chill for best fruiting. Deciduous; reduce or withhold watering when leaves drop in fall.

pineapple.description: Tropical bromeliad in the Bromeliaceae family producing sweet aggregate fruits from the crown.
pineapple.care_tips: Water sparingly, allowing soil to dry between waterings - as a bromeliad, pineapple stores water in its leaf rosette and is prone to root rot in soggy soil. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily) for fruit production. Fertilize monthly during the growing season with a balanced liquid fertilizer, including foliar feeding by spraying into the rosette. Plant from the crown of a store-bought pineapple by twisting it off, letting the base dry for a few days, then planting in well-draining soil. Each plant produces only one fruit over 18-24 months, then produces offsets (ratoons) that will fruit again

plantain.description: Also known as: Cooking Banana, Plátano. Large tropical herbaceous plant producing starchy, thick-skinned fruits used as a cooked vegetable staple worldwide.
plantain.care_tips: Full sun — 6-8 hours direct sunlight daily. Keep soil consistently moist; never let it dry out completely. Thrives at 25-30°C; cannot tolerate below 10°C. Rich, well-drained soil with high organic matter (pH 6.0-7.5). Heavy feeder — fertilize monthly with balanced fertilizer. Mulch thickly to retain moisture. Protect from wind which shreds leaves. Each stem fruits once then dies — new suckers continue the cycle. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

plum.description: Deciduous fruit trees in the Rosaceae family with smooth skin, many varieties need cross-pollination.
plum.care_tips: Deep soak weekly during growing season. Increase watering during fruit development. Mulch around base. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in early spring with fruit tree fertilizer. Prune in late winter/early spring. Many varieties need cross-pollination - plant compatible varieties. Thin fruit for larger plums. Harvest when fully colored and slightly soft. Requires winter chill. Reduce watering when dormant in winter. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

pomegranate.description: Deciduous fruit trees in the Lythraceae family with jewel-like seeds, drought-tolerant once established.
pomegranate.care_tips: Deep soak weekly during growing season. Drought tolerant once established. Mulch around base. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in early spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune to maintain shape. Self-fertile. Harvest when fully colored and makes metallic sound when tapped. Can be grown in containers. Requires hot summers for best fruiting. Deciduous; reduce or withhold watering when leaves drop in fall.

pomelo.description: Also known as: Pummelo, Shaddock. Large citrus fruits in the Rutaceae family, largest citrus fruit, popular in China and Southeast Asia.
pomelo.care_tips: Deep soak regularly during growing season. Well-drained soil essential. Full sun essential. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with citrus fertilizer. Prune to maintain size. Self-fertile. Harvest when fully yellow and fragrant. Largest citrus fruit. Require warm climates - protect from frost. Popular in China and Southeast Asia. Evergreen; reduce watering in winter when growth slows.

prickly pear fruit.description: Cactus in the Cactaceae family with edible pads and sweet, colorful fruits (tunas), drought-tolerant.
prickly pear fruit.care_tips: Water very sparingly - soak soil thoroughly then allow to dry completely before watering again; in winter, suspend watering almost entirely. Full sun essential (8+ hours daily). Fertilize once in spring with a dilute cactus fertilizer or low-nitrogen blend. Do NOT mulch - prickly pear needs bare, fast-draining soil and mulch retains too much moisture causing rot. Use tongs and thick gloves when harvesting fruit (tunas), as both fruit and pads have glochids (tiny barbed spines). Extremely drought and heat tolerant once established. Pads can be rooted simply by setting a cut pad on dry soil. Non

quince.description: Deciduous tree in the Rosaceae family with aromatic golden pomes, must be cooked - ideal for preserves.
quince.care_tips: Water regularly during the first few years to establish; mature trees are moderately drought tolerant. Full sun essential for best fruit production (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in early spring with a balanced fruit tree fertilizer. Prune in late winter to maintain an open, vase-shaped canopy - quince fruits on the tips of new growth, so avoid heavy heading cuts. Fruit is too hard and astringent to eat raw but becomes beautifully fragrant and turns rosy-pink when cooked into preserves, membrillo paste, or poached. Very ornamental with large pink-white spring blossoms. Susceptible to fire blight

rambutan.description: Tropical fruit tree producing clusters of hairy red or yellow fruits with translucent, sweet, lychee-like flesh inside—the name comes from the Malay word for hair.
rambutan.care_tips: Water regularly; keep soil consistently moist, especially during flowering and fruiting. Full sun for best fruit production. Very high humidity (80%+) essential—strictly tropical, no frost tolerance. Deep, well-draining, organically rich acidic soil (pH 5.0-6.5). Fertilize quarterly with balanced fertilizer; increase potassium during fruiting. Trees are either male or female—plant both for pollination or choose grafted hermaphrodite varieties. Can grow 15-25 meters; choose grafted dwarf cultivars for smaller spaces. Non-toxic to pets. Prune during dormancy. Remove dead and diseased wood. Thin

raspberries.description: Also known as: Red raspberry. Perennial cane fruits in the Rosaceae family, produce fruit on second-year canes (floricane) or first-year canes (primocane) depending on variety.
raspberries.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (weekly deep watering). Water at base to avoid wetting fruit. Mulch around plants to retain moisture and suppress weeds. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in early spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune according to type - summer-bearing: remove fruited canes after harvest; everbearing: can be pruned for one or two crops. Support canes with trellis. Harvest when fully colored and easily detaches. Replace plants every 8-10 years. Deciduous varieties: reduce watering when dormant in winter.

starfruit.description: Also known as: Carambola, Star Apple, Five-Corner Fruit. Tropical fruit tree producing distinctive star-shaped cross-section fruits with a sweet-tart flavor.
starfruit.care_tips: Full sun — minimum 6-7 hours direct sunlight daily for fruiting. Keep soil consistently moist but never waterlogged; water deeply 2-3 times per week. Thrives at 20-35°C; young trees killed by frost, mature trees survive brief dips to -3°C. Acidic, well-drained soil (pH 5.5-6.5). Fertilize monthly during growing season. Contains high oxalic acid — toxic to those with kidney disease and mildly toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

strawberries.description: Also known as: Garden strawberry. Low-growing perennial berry plants in the Rosaceae family, produce runners for propagation.
strawberries.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Water at base to avoid wetting fruit which can cause rot. Mulch with straw or pine needles to keep berries clean and prevent soil contact. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize in early spring and after harvest with balanced fertilizer. Remove runners first year to encourage fruiting; allow runners second year to propagate. Harvest when fully red. Replace plants every 3-4 years. Research variety type (June-bearing, everbearing, day-neutral) for exact requirements. Remove old leaves and excess runners after harvest; renovate beds in late su

tamarind.description: Also known as: Tamarindo, Indian Date. Long-lived tropical tree producing pod-like fruits with tangy pulp widely used in cuisines and beverages worldwide.
tamarind.care_tips: Full sun essential — cannot grow in shade. Water regularly when young to establish deep roots; mature trees are drought-tolerant. Let soil dry between waterings. Well-drained soil; tolerates sandy, loamy, or slightly acidic conditions (pH 6.0-7.5). Thrives at 25-40°C; frost-sensitive. Slow to fruit — typically 6-8 years from seed. Fertilize annually in spring. Non-toxic to pets and humans. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

scientific_names: Prunus amygdalus (syn. P. dulcis; Sweet almond)
almond.description: Deciduous tree in the Rosaceae family producing edible nuts inside fuzzy drupes, closely related to peach. Beautiful pink-white spring blossoms.
almond.care_tips: Water deeply every 1-2 weeks during growing season; reduce in winter but do not let soil go completely dry. Full sun essential. Well-drained, sandy loam preferred — cannot tolerate waterlogged soil. Fertilize in early spring with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Prune after harvest to maintain shape and improve air circulation. Needs 300-600 chill hours. Most varieties need a cross-pollinator. Blooms early — late frosts can destroy the crop. Bitter almond contains amygdalin (toxic); sweet almond is safe to eat. Mildly toxic to pets.

cashew.description: Tropical evergreen tree in the Anacardiaceae family producing kidney-shaped nuts attached to fleshy cashew apples. Native to Brazil, now grown across the tropics.
cashew.care_tips: Water regularly during establishment; mature trees tolerate dry periods. Full sun essential. Sandy, well-drained soil preferred. Fertilize 2-3 times per year with balanced fertilizer. Prune to maintain manageable height and remove dead wood. The shell contains caustic oil (urushiol, same as poison ivy) — never eat raw cashew shells. The cashew apple (pseudofruit) is edible and used for juice. Frost-sensitive — tropical climates only. Mildly toxic to pets (shell oil is irritating).

chestnut.description: Majestic deciduous tree in the Fagaceae family producing starchy, edible nuts inside spiny burs. Important food tree across Europe and Asia for millennia.
chestnut.care_tips: Water regularly during first few years; established trees are moderately drought tolerant. Full sun essential for nut production. Acidic, well-drained, sandy loam preferred — cannot tolerate alkaline or waterlogged soil. Fertilize lightly in spring. Prune in late winter. Needs a cross-pollinator from a different variety. American chestnut was nearly wiped out by chestnut blight — Chinese chestnut is blight-resistant. Nuts are starchy (unlike most tree nuts) and can be roasted, boiled, or ground into flour. Non-toxic to pets.

hazelnut.description: Also known as: Cobnut. Deciduous shrub or small tree in the Betulaceae family producing small, round edible nuts. Wind-pollinated with distinctive catkins in late winter.
hazelnut.care_tips: Water regularly during establishment and nut development; mature plants are moderately drought tolerant. Full sun to partial shade. Adaptable to most well-drained soils. Fertilize once in early spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune suckers regularly to maintain tree form, or allow to grow as multi-stemmed shrub. Wind-pollinated — plant at least two different cultivars for cross-pollination. Harvest when husks turn brown and nuts fall naturally. Non-toxic to pets.

macadamia.description: Subtropical evergreen tree in the Proteaceae family native to Australia, producing premium, buttery-flavored nuts in extremely hard shells.
macadamia.care_tips: Water regularly — macadamias need consistent moisture, especially during nut development. Full sun for best production. Acidic, well-drained soil essential — does not tolerate alkaline conditions. Fertilize 3-4 times per year with citrus or avocado fertilizer. Protect from strong winds (shallow root system). Trees take 7-10 years to reach full production. Wind-pollinated but benefits from bee activity. Highly toxic to dogs — even one or two nuts can cause weakness, tremors, and hyperthermia. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

pecan.description: Large deciduous tree in the Juglandaceae family native to North America, producing rich, buttery nuts inside thin-shelled husks. Major commercial nut crop.
pecan.care_tips: Water deeply and regularly, especially during nut filling (July-September) — pecans are heavy water users. Full sun essential. Deep, well-drained alluvial soil preferred. Fertilize with zinc-containing fertilizer in spring — zinc deficiency is common. Prune young trees to develop a central leader. Most varieties need a cross-pollinator (Type I × Type II). Trees can take 6-10 years to bear. Alternate bearing is common. Non-toxic to pets.

pistachio.description: Deciduous tree in the Anacardiaceae family native to Central Asia, producing green-kerneled nuts that split open when ripe. Thrives in hot, arid climates.
pistachio.care_tips: Water deeply but infrequently — pistachios are very drought tolerant once established. Full sun essential; needs hot summers. Well-drained, even alkaline soil tolerated — one of few nut trees that thrives in poor, calcareous soil. Fertilize sparingly. Dioecious — plant one male per 8-10 female trees. Trees take 5-8 years to bear. Needs both hot summers and cold winters (600+ chill hours). Alternate bearing (heavy one year, light the next). Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

walnut.description: Deciduous nut tree in the Juglandaceae family producing edible walnuts in hard shells, valued for both nuts and premium timber.
walnut.care_tips: Water deeply once a week during growing season; established trees are drought tolerant. Full sun essential (6-8 hours). Well-drained, deep soil preferred — shallow or compacted soil stunts growth. Fertilize annually in early spring with balanced fertilizer. Prune in late winter when dormant to shape and remove dead wood. Black walnuts produce juglone, which is toxic to many plants — avoid planting tomatoes, apples, or azaleas within the drip line. Harvest when hulls begin to split in autumn. Trees need 400-1500 chill hours depending on variety. Mildly toxic to pets (hulls can cause GI upset).

ashwagandha.description: Also known as: Indian Ginseng, Winter Cherry, Poison Gooseberry. Adaptogenic herb from India with velvety leaves and small orange-red berries enclosed in papery husks.
ashwagandha.care_tips: Full sun essential — minimum 6-8 hours direct sunlight. Very drought-tolerant; water only when soil is completely dry. Sandy, well-draining soil with alkaline pH (7.5-8.0). Thrives at 25-35°C; frost-sensitive below -1°C. Annual in cold climates, perennial in zones 8+. Minimal fertilizer needed. Harvest roots after first year of growth. Berries are mildly toxic — keep away from children and pets. Cut plants back after the berry and root harvest.

basil.description: Also known as: Sweet basil. Annual culinary herb in the Lamiaceae family with aromatic leaves, essential in Mediterranean and Asian cuisines.
basil.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Water at base to avoid wetting leaves. Well-drained soil essential. Full sun preferred (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Pinch flowers immediately to prolong leaf production. Harvest regularly by pinching tips to encourage bushy growth. Very sensitive to cold - plant after last frost. Annual - replant each season.

bay laurel.description: Also known as: Bay leaf. Evergreen tree in the Lauraceae family with aromatic leaves used in soups, stews, and Mediterranean cooking. Can be grown as a container tree or shaped hedge.
bay laurel.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun preferred. Fertilize regularly during growing season. Harvest leaves as needed; dry before storing. Mulch to retain moisture. Mildly toxic to pets if ingested. Prune in spring to shape; container plants can be kept to 1-2 m.

borage.description: Also known as: Starflower. Annual herb in the Boraginaceae family with edible blue flowers and cucumber-flavored leaves. Used in salads, drinks, and as a companion plant for tomatoes and squash.
borage.care_tips: Water moderately, allowing soil to dry slightly between waterings - borage is fairly drought tolerant once established. Full sun to partial shade (6+ hours daily). Fertilizing is generally unnecessary; borage thrives in poor to average soil and excess nitrogen produces leggy growth with fewer flowers. Sow seeds directly outdoors as borage has a long taproot and resents transplanting. Self-seeds prolifically - deadhead to control spread, or allow it to naturalize. Harvest young leaves (older leaves become prickly) and blue star-shaped flowers for salads and garnishes. Non-toxic to pets; flowers

cardamom.description: Also known as: Green cardamom. Spice plant in the ginger family with aromatic seeds used in cooking and chai.
cardamom.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist. High humidity. Partial shade. Warm temperatures. Harvest seed pods when green and before splitting. Tropical perennial. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

catnip.description: Perennial herb in the Lamiaceae family with gray-green leaves. Known for attracting cats; leaves can be used in tea or as a calming herb for humans.
catnip.care_tips: Water moderately, allowing soil to dry between waterings - catnip is drought tolerant and prefers not to sit in wet soil. Full sun to partial shade (4-6 hours daily). Fertilize sparingly or not at all; rich soil and heavy feeding reduce the essential oil concentration that gives catnip its potency. Cut back by one-third after the first flush of flowers to encourage a second bloom. Be aware that cats will roll in, chew, and crush the plants - consider a protective cage if growing for harvest. Spreads by both runners and self-seeding; contain in pots or harvest frequently to control. Mildly toxi

chamomile.description: Herb in the Asteraceae family with daisy-like flowers used for soothing tea. German chamomile is annual; Roman chamomile is perennial. Both have apple-scented foliage.
chamomile.care_tips: Water regularly but lightly, keeping soil slightly moist - chamomile has shallow roots but does not like soggy soil. Full sun to partial shade (4-6 hours daily). Fertilizing is generally unnecessary and can reduce flower production and essential oil concentration. Sow seeds on the soil surface (they need light to germinate) in spring or fall. Harvest flower heads when petals begin to fold back from the center, typically in the morning after dew has dried. German chamomile is annual and self-seeds freely; Roman chamomile is a low-growing perennial useful as a fragrant ground cover. Mildly toxic

chervil.description: Cool-season annual herb in the Apiaceae family with delicate anise- and parsley-like flavor. Essential in French fines herbes. Best in spring and fall; bolts in heat.
chervil.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil consistently moist - chervil bolts quickly if stressed by drought. Partial shade is essential, NOT full sun; chervil is one of the few herbs that actually prefers and needs shade, especially in warm climates. Fertilize lightly once a month with a balanced liquid fertilizer. Sow seeds directly outdoors in early spring or late summer/fall, as chervil dislikes transplanting and heat. Best treated as a cool-season crop; it bolts rapidly in temperatures above 24°C. Harvest outer leaves regularly, cutting stems at the base. Flavor is delicate and lost when cooked - add f

chinese chives.description: Also known as: Nira. Perennial herbs in the Amaryllidaceae family with flat leaves and garlic flavor, essential in Chinese cuisine.
chinese chives.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize monthly with balanced fertilizer. Harvest by cutting leaves at base. Divide every 3-4 years. Perennial - returns each year. Garlic flavor. Essential in Chinese cuisine. Can be grown in containers. Edible white flowers. Herbaceous perennials die back; reduce watering when dormant. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly. Toxic to pets.

chives.description: Perennial herbs in the Amaryllidaceae family with hollow, grass-like leaves, easy to grow.
chives.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize monthly with balanced fertilizer. Harvest by cutting leaves at base. Divide every 3-4 years. Perennial - returns each year. Easy to grow. Can be grown in containers. Edible purple flowers. Reduce watering in winter when growth slows. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly. Toxic to pets.

cilantro.description: Also known as: Coriander, Chinese parsley. Annual herb in the Apiaceae family, leaves (cilantro) and seeds (coriander) are both used, bolts quickly in heat.
cilantro.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Consistent moisture prevents bolting. Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Prefer cooler temperatures - plant in spring or fall. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest leaves regularly. Bolts quickly in heat - provide shade in summer or plant in fall. Annual - replant each season. Seeds (coriander) can be harvested when brown. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

comfrey.description: Perennial herb in the Boraginaceae family with large hairy leaves. Traditionally used externally for bruises and sprains. Contains pyrrolizidine alkaloids—do not ingest; mild toxicity to pets.
comfrey.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun preferred. Fertilize regularly. Use as compost activator or mulch. Do not consume internally. Mildly toxic to pets when ingested. Harvest regularly to promote bushy growth. Pinch off flower buds to extend leaf production.

cumin.description: Annual herb in the Apiaceae family cultivated for its small, aromatic seeds — the second most popular spice worldwide after black pepper. Essential in Indian, Mexican, and Middle Eastern cuisines.
cumin.care_tips: Water moderately — keep soil evenly moist during germination and early growth, then reduce. Overwatering causes root rot. Full sun essential; needs long, hot growing season (3-4 months frost-free). Well-drained, sandy loam soil. Direct sow after last frost — does not transplant well. Seeds mature when plants turn brown; harvest entire plant and dry upside down. Flavor is much stronger when seeds are toasted before use. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

scientific_names: Bergera koenigii (syn. Murraya koenigii; Curry leaf tree)
curry leaf.description: Also known as: Curry tree, Kadi patta, Sweet neem. Small aromatic tree in the Rutaceae family whose glossy pinnate leaves are fried in oil at the start of countless South Indian and Sri Lankan dishes; unrelated to the silver-leaved curry plant (Helichrysum) or to curry powder.
curry leaf.care_tips: Water when the top 3-5 cm of soil is dry; overwatering yellows the leaves, especially in winter when growth stops. Full sun outdoors, or the sunniest window plus a grow light indoors. Thrives at 18-35°C; drops leaves below 10°C and dies at frost, so pot-grow and overwinter indoors outside zones 10-12. Medium humidity. Feed every 3-4 weeks in the growing season with a balanced fertilizer plus occasional iron for yellowing leaves. Well-draining, slightly acidic potting mix. Harvest sprigs from the top to encourage branching; leaves freeze well. Remove the suckers that spring up around the base,

dill.description: Annual herbs in the Apiaceae family with feathery leaves and seeds, both leaves and seeds are used.
dill.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun essential. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest leaves regularly. Harvest seeds when brown. Can bolt in heat - plant in spring or fall. Both leaves and seeds are used. Attracts beneficial insects. Annual - replant each season. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

epazote.description: Annual herb in the Amaranthaceae family with a pungent, medicinal flavor. Traditional in Mexican bean dishes to reduce gas. Used sparingly due to strong flavor.
epazote.care_tips: Water sparingly, allowing soil to dry between waterings - epazote is drought tolerant and actually produces more aromatic oils under slightly dry conditions. Full sun preferred (6-8 hours daily). Fertilizing is unnecessary; epazote thrives in poor, well-draining soil and excessive nutrients reduce flavor intensity. Self-seeds very aggressively and can become weedy - deadhead before seeds mature or grow in containers. Use leaves sparingly in cooking, as the flavor is very strong and the plant contains toxic compounds (ascaridole) that are harmful in large quantities. Harvest young leaves, which

herb fennel.description: Tall, feathery herb with an anise-like flavor used in Mediterranean cooking, producing edible fronds, seeds, pollen, and a crunchy bulb in the Florence variety.
herb fennel.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist; water regularly in hot weather. Full sun essential—at least 6 hours daily. Medium humidity fine. Deep, well-draining, fertile soil. Fertilize at planting with compost; side-dress with balanced fertilizer mid-season. Do not plant near dill—they cross-pollinate and produce poor-flavored seeds. Hill soil around Florence fennel bulbs to blanch them. Attracts swallowtail butterfly caterpillars. Mildly toxic to pets in large amounts. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

ginger.description: Rhizomatous herbs in the Zingiberaceae family, essential spice in Chinese cuisine, can be grown from store-bought rhizomes.
ginger.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist but not waterlogged. Well-drained, rich soil preferred. Partial shade preferred - avoid direct hot sun. Fertilize monthly with balanced fertilizer. Plant rhizome pieces with eyes pointing up. Harvest when leaves die back (8-10 months). Can be grown in containers. Essential spice in Chinese cuisine. Rhizomes can be harvested partially. Reduce watering in winter when growth slows. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

ginseng.description: Also known as: Asian Ginseng, Korean Ginseng, Red Ginseng. Slow-growing woodland herb prized for its fleshy root used in traditional medicine for centuries.
ginseng.care_tips: Deep shade essential — 80% shade mimicking forest understory. Keep soil consistently moist but well-drained; never waterlogged. Prefers cool temperatures (18-21°C) and needs a winter cold period. Rich, loamy soil with high organic matter; pH 5.5-6.5. Extremely slow-growing — roots mature in 4-6 years. Do not fertilize. Susceptible to fungal diseases in humid conditions. Non-toxic to pets and humans. Do not harvest leaves; remove only dead foliage in fall.

holy basil.description: Also known as: Tulsi. Annual herb in the Lamiaceae family, sacred in Hinduism. Aromatic leaves with clove-like flavor used in Thai cuisine and Ayurvedic medicine. Different from sweet basil.
holy basil.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil evenly moist but not waterlogged - holy basil likes consistent moisture but is more drought tolerant than sweet basil. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with a balanced organic fertilizer; avoid heavy nitrogen which reduces the aromatic essential oil content.
