Pinch flower buds to prolong leaf harvest, though the purple flowers are also edible and attractive to pollinators. Unlike sweet basil, holy basil (tulsi) has a more clove-like, peppery flavor and is traditionally used in Thai stir-fries and Ayurvedic teas rather than Italian cuis

indoor herbs.description: Culinary herbs grown indoors, require good drainage and regular harvesting to encourage bushy growth.
indoor herbs.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist but well-drained. Allow top inch to dry slightly between waterings. Avoid waterlogged soil - excellent drainage essential. Bright indirect to direct light (4-6 hours daily minimum). Medium humidity (40-50%) is fine. Fertilize monthly with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Harvest regularly to encourage bushy growth - pinch tips. Pinch flowers to prolong leaf production. Repot annually. Research specific herb for exact requirements.

culinary lavender.description: Beloved aromatic herb with silvery-green foliage and fragrant purple flower spikes prized for culinary use, essential oils, sachets, and ornamental garden borders.
culinary lavender.care_tips: Drought-tolerant once established; water deeply but infrequently, allowing soil to dry between waterings. Full sun essential—at least 6-8 hours daily. Low humidity preferred; good air circulation prevents fungal disease. Well-draining, slightly alkaline soil (add lime to acidic soils). Avoid rich fertilizer—lean soil concentrates fragrance. Prune after flowering by cutting back one-third; never cut into old wood. Mildly toxic to pets if ingested in large quantities.

lemon balm.description: Perennial herb in the Lamiaceae family with lemon-scented leaves. Used in tea, salads, and desserts. Spreads readily; can be invasive. Attracts bees.
lemon balm.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil evenly moist, but lemon balm is quite forgiving of occasional drought once established. Full sun to partial shade (4-6 hours daily); some afternoon shade in hot climates prevents leaf scorching. Fertilize sparingly - once or twice per season with compost or dilute balanced fertilizer is sufficient. Warning: lemon balm spreads extremely aggressively by both runners and self-seeding; grow in containers or use root barriers to prevent it from taking over the garden. Harvest frequently by cutting stems back to a leaf node, which keeps plants bushy and delays flowering.

scientific_names: Aloysia citrodora (syn. A. triphylla; Lemon verbena)
lemon verbena.description: Also known as: Lemon beebrush, Cedrón. Deciduous shrubby herb in the Verbenaceae family with narrow leaves that release the most intense lemon scent of any herb; used for tea, desserts, and syrups.
lemon verbena.care_tips: Water when the top 3 cm of soil is dry; it dislikes wet feet but wilts fast in containers during heat. Full sun, 6-8 hours. Thrives at 15-30°C; hardy only to about -5°C, so grow in a pot and overwinter indoors or in a frost-free shed, where it drops its leaves and goes dormant. Medium humidity. Feed monthly in spring and summer with a balanced fertilizer. Well-draining, moderately fertile soil. Spider mites and whiteflies bother indoor plants; rinse the foliage. Harvest leaves any time; flavor peaks just before the tiny lilac flowers open. Mildly toxic to pets; may cause GI upset if eaten in q

lemongrass.description: Perennial grasses in the Poaceae family with lemony flavor, popular in Asian cuisine, can be grown in containers.
lemongrass.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Well-drained, rich soil preferred. Full sun preferred. Fertilize monthly with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Harvest outer stalks at base. Divide every 2-3 years. Perennial in warm climates - treat as annual in cold. Can be grown in containers. Lemony flavor. Popular in Asian cuisine. Reduce watering in winter when growth slows. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

lovage.description: Tall perennial herb in the Apiaceae family with celery-like flavor. Leaves, stems, and seeds used in soups and stocks. Often grown as a substitute for celery.
lovage.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil consistently moist - lovage is a moisture-loving plant with deep roots. Full sun to partial shade (4-6 hours daily); appreciates afternoon shade in hot climates. Fertilize in early spring with compost or balanced fertilizer; lovage is a vigorous perennial that benefits from rich soil. Be prepared for its size - lovage grows 4-6 feet tall and should be placed at the back of the herb garden. Cut flower stalks before they bloom to direct energy into leaf production, unless saving seed. All parts are edible with an intense celery-like flavor: use leaves in soups and st

marjoram.description: Also known as: Sweet marjoram. Tender perennial herb in the Lamiaceae family with a sweeter, milder flavor than oregano. Essential in Greek and Middle Eastern cooking. Often grown as annual in cold climates.
marjoram.care_tips: Water moderately, allowing the top inch of soil to dry between waterings - marjoram prefers slightly drier conditions than most herbs and is susceptible to root rot in wet soil. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize lightly every 4-6 weeks with a dilute liquid fertilizer; over-feeding diminishes the delicate sweet aroma. Harvest before flowers open for the strongest flavor by cutting stems back to a leaf pair. Tender perennial (hardy only to about -1°C); in cold climates grow as an annual or bring containers indoors for winter. Often confused with oregano but has a sweeter, milder, m

mint.description: Perennial herbs in the Lamiaceae family with aromatic leaves, can be invasive, spreads by runners.
mint.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Prefer consistently moist but well-drained soil. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize monthly with balanced fertilizer. Harvest regularly to control growth. Very invasive - grow in containers or use barriers to contain. Spreads by runners. Can be grown indoors or outdoors. Perennial but may die back in winter. Reduce watering in winter when growth slows. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

oregano.description: Also known as: Wild marjoram. Perennial herbs in the Lamiaceae family with pungent leaves, essential in Mediterranean cuisine.
oregano.care_tips: Water when soil is dry (every 1-2 weeks once established). Well-drained soil essential. Drought tolerant once established. Full sun preferred (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize sparingly in spring. Harvest regularly by cutting stems. Pinch flowers to prolong leaf production. Perennial - may need protection in very cold climates. Flavor intensifies when dried. Reduce watering in winter when growth slows. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

pandan.description: Also known as: Screwpine, Pandanus, Daun pandan. Clumping tropical plant in the Pandanaceae family with long, strap-like fragrant leaves that flavor rice, desserts, and drinks across Southeast Asia, giving a sweet, grassy, vanilla-like aroma and a natural green color.
pandan.care_tips: Keep the soil consistently moist; it loves water and even tolerates boggy conditions but wilts in dry soil. Bright indirect light indoors or partial shade outdoors; full sun is fine in humid climates. Needs warmth at 18-35°C and dies below about 5°C, so grow in a pot and overwinter indoors outside zones 10-12. High humidity (60%+) keeps leaf tips from browning. Feed monthly in the growing season with a balanced fertilizer. Rich, moisture-retentive potting mix. Rarely flowers in cultivation; propagate from the plantlets that form at the base and on the stem. Harvest the outer leaves as needed;

parsley.description: Also known as: Curly parsley. Biennial herbs in the Apiaceae family, most commonly used as annual, curly and flat-leaf varieties.
parsley.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist (2-3 times per week). Well-drained soil preferred. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with balanced fertilizer. Harvest outer leaves regularly to encourage new growth. Biennial but usually grown as annual. Flat-leaf has stronger flavor. Can be grown indoors. Very common culinary herb. Mildly toxic to pets in large amounts. Reduce watering in winter when growth slows. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

peppermint.description: Vigorous aromatic herb with dark green leaves edged in purple and a strong, cooling menthol flavor used in teas, desserts, cocktails, and herbal remedies.
peppermint.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist; never let it dry out. Partial sun to partial shade—4-6 hours of sun ideal. Medium humidity fine. Rich, moisture-retentive soil. Fertilize monthly with balanced liquid fertilizer during growing season. Extremely invasive—always grow in containers to prevent spreading. Pinch tips regularly to promote bushy growth and prevent flowering. Harvest frequently; flavor is best just before flowering. Mildly toxic to pets (menthol can cause gastrointestinal upset).

rosemary.description: Aromatic evergreen herbs in the Lamiaceae family, drought-tolerant once established, can grow as shrub or groundcover.
rosemary.care_tips: Water when soil is dry (every 1-2 weeks once established). Avoid overwatering which causes root rot. Well-draining soil essential. Very drought tolerant once established. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize sparingly in spring. Prune regularly to harvest and maintain shape. Can grow as shrub or groundcover depending on variety. Aromatic evergreen herb. Excellent for Mediterranean gardens. Evergreen; reduce watering in winter when growth slows.

sage.description: Also known as: Garden sage. Perennial herbs in the Lamiaceae family with gray-green leaves, drought-tolerant once established.
sage.care_tips: Water when soil is dry (every 1-2 weeks once established). Well-drained soil essential. Drought tolerant once established. Full sun preferred. Fertilize sparingly in spring. Harvest leaves regularly. Prune to maintain shape. Perennial - may need protection in very cold climates. Strong flavor - use sparingly in cooking. Reduce watering in winter when growth slows.

savory.description: Also known as: Summer savory. Herb in the Lamiaceae family with peppery, thyme-like flavor. Summer savory is annual; winter savory is perennial. Traditional in bean dishes and stuffings.
savory.care_tips: Water moderately, allowing soil to dry slightly between waterings - savory prefers lean, well-drained conditions similar to other Mediterranean herbs. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize sparingly or not at all; poor to average soil actually intensifies the peppery, thyme-like flavor. Summer savory (Satureja hortensis) is an annual with a milder flavor; winter savory (S. montana) is a hardy perennial with a stronger, more pungent taste. Harvest summer savory before flowering for best flavor; winter savory can be clipped year-round. Both types make excellent companion plants for bea

shiso.description: Annual herb in the Lamiaceae family with a mint-basil flavor. Green and red varieties used in Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese cuisine. Essential for sushi and banchan.
shiso.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged. Full sun to partial shade (4-6 hours daily); some afternoon shade in hot climates prevents wilting and bitterness. Fertilize every 3-4 weeks with a balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength. Pinch growing tips regularly to encourage bushy growth and delay flowering. Available in green and red (purple) varieties - red shiso is used for coloring umeboshi and shiso juice, while green shiso is preferred fresh for sushi, sashimi, and rice wraps. Self-seeds freely and can become weedy if allowed to go to seed; deadhead or harvest

sorrel.description: Also known as: Garden sorrel. Perennial herb in the Polygonaceae family with tangy, lemony leaves from oxalic acid. Used in soups, salads, and sauces. French sorrel has milder flavor.
sorrel.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil evenly moist - sorrel's flavor becomes excessively sour and leaves turn tough in dry conditions. Full sun to partial shade (4-6 hours daily); benefits from afternoon shade in hot climates. Fertilize lightly in spring with compost or balanced fertilizer; too much nitrogen encourages excessive leaf growth with reduced flavor. Remove flower stalks promptly to prolong leaf harvest and prevent the plant from going to seed. A hardy perennial that returns reliably each spring and can be harvested for many years from the same clump. Leaves contain oxalic acid giving the si

st john s wort.description: Also known as: Klamath Weed, Goatweed. Sun-loving perennial herb with bright yellow star-shaped flowers, widely used in traditional medicine for mood support.
st john s wort.care_tips: Full sun for maximum flowering — tolerates partial shade. Drought-tolerant once established; water occasionally during dry spells. Adapts to most soil types including poor, sandy, or rocky soils. Well-drained soil preferred. Hardy to -20°C. Can become invasive — deadhead to prevent self-seeding. Contains hypericin which causes photosensitivity in livestock — toxic to horses and cattle. Mildly toxic to dogs and cats.

stevia.description: Tender perennial herb in the Asteraceae family. Leaves are intensely sweet—used as natural sugar substitute. Native to Paraguay; needs warm, frost-free climate.
stevia.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil consistently moist but well-drained - stevia does not tolerate drought well, nor does it like sitting in water. Full sun to partial shade (6+ hours daily). Fertilize every 2-3 weeks during the growing season with a balanced fertilizer at half strength; avoid high-nitrogen formulas which dilute the sweet flavor. Pinch growing tips regularly to encourage bushy growth and more leaf production. Harvest leaves before flowering for maximum sweetness; once the plant blooms, leaves become less sweet and may turn bitter. Tender perennial hardy only to about 40°F (4°C); grow

tarragon.description: Perennial herb in the Asteraceae family with anise-like flavor. French tarragon is the culinary standard; propagated by division. Essential in béarnaise and fines herbes.
tarragon.care_tips: Water moderately, allowing soil to dry slightly between waterings - French tarragon prefers lean, well-drained conditions and will develop root rot in heavy, wet soil. Full sun to partial shade (6+ hours daily); tolerates light afternoon shade. Fertilize sparingly, once or twice per season with dilute balanced fertilizer; rich soil diminishes the distinctive anise flavor. French tarragon does NOT produce viable seed and must be propagated by root division or cuttings - if you see tarragon seeds for sale, they are Russian tarragon which has inferior flavor. Divide plants every 3-4 years in spri

tea plant.description: Evergreen shrub whose leaves produce black, green, oolong, and white tea.
tea plant.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist but well-drained; never let it dry out fully. Acidic soil (pH 4.5-5.5) is essential. Partial shade in hot climates; full sun in cool ones. Fertilize in spring with an acid-loving plant fertilizer. Protect from hard frost. Harvest the young flushes of two leaves and a bud; prune to keep a low, bushy frame. Non-toxic to pets.

thyme.description: Also known as: Garden thyme. Perennial herbs in the Lamiaceae family with small aromatic leaves, drought-tolerant once established.
thyme.care_tips: Water when soil is dry (every 1-2 weeks once established). Well-drained soil essential. Drought tolerant once established. Full sun preferred (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize sparingly in spring. Harvest regularly by cutting stems. Can be grown as groundcover or in containers. Perennial - may need protection in very cold climates. Reduce watering in winter when growth slows. Remove yellowing or damaged leaves promptly.

turmeric.description: Rhizomatous herbs in the Zingiberaceae family, related to ginger, popular spice and natural dye.
turmeric.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist but not waterlogged. Well-drained, rich soil preferred. Partial shade preferred. Fertilize monthly with balanced fertilizer. Plant rhizome pieces. Harvest when leaves die back (8-10 months). Can be grown in containers. Related to ginger. Popular spice and natural dye. Requires warm climate - protect from frost. Reduce watering in winter when growth slows. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

vietnamese coriander.description: Perennial herb in the Polygonaceae family with spicy, cilantro-like flavor. Essential in Vietnamese pho and salads. Not a true coriander; thrives in warm, moist conditions.
vietnamese coriander.care_tips: Water frequently and abundantly - Vietnamese coriander is a semi-aquatic plant that thrives in consistently wet to boggy conditions and will wilt rapidly if allowed to dry out. Partial shade to full shade (3-5 hours of sun daily); unlike most herbs, it prefers shade and its leaves scorch in intense direct sun. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks with a balanced liquid fertilizer during the growing season. An excellent cilantro substitute in hot climates since it does not bolt in heat. Propagates effortlessly from stem cuttings placed in water. Grows as a spreading ground cover in tropical areas; in temp

wasabi.description: Prized in Japanese cuisine for its pungent, sinus-clearing flavor. Notoriously difficult to grow — requires cool, shady, humid conditions with clean running water.
wasabi.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist — grows naturally along mountain stream beds. Cool shade essential; cannot tolerate heat above 20°C or direct sun. Very high humidity required. Extremely slow growing — takes 18-24 months to produce a usable rhizome. Non-toxic. Remove yellowing outer leaves; the rhizome is harvested once after 18-24 months.

alfalfa.description: Perennial legume in the Fabaceae family. Major forage crop for hay and grazing. Nitrogen-fixing; deep roots. Also grown for sprouting.
alfalfa.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained, neutral to alkaline soil. Drought tolerant once established. Harvest hay at 10% bloom. Inoculate seed with rhizobia. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

grain amaranth.description: Pseudo-cereal in the Amaranthaceae family. Gluten-free grain; seeds high in protein. Drought tolerant. Ancient crop of the Americas.
grain amaranth.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Warm-season crop. Harvest when seed heads dry and seeds rattle. Thresh when fully dry. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

barley.description: Annual grass in the Poaceae family. Cereal grain for malt, feed, and food. Spring and winter types. Tolerates cooler climates than wheat.
barley.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Cool-season crop. Harvest when heads bend and kernels hard. Two-row and six-row varieties. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

black pepper.description: Tropical climbing vine in the Piperaceae family — the world's most traded spice. Produces clusters of small drupes that are dried to make black, white, or green peppercorns.
black pepper.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged — high water needs in tropical conditions. Partial shade to filtered sun; protect from intense afternoon sun. Rich, acidic, well-drained soil with high organic matter. Fertilize every 2-3 months with balanced fertilizer. Needs a support structure to climb (grows 4-5m). Very high humidity (80%+) essential. Harvest green for green peppercorns, let dry on vine for black pepper, or soak and remove skin for white pepper. Minimum temperature 20°C. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

buckwheat.description: Pseudo-cereal in the Polygonaceae family. Gluten-free; fast-growing cover crop. White flowers attract pollinators. Short season (70–90 days).
buckwheat.care_tips: Full sun. Any well-drained soil. Sow late spring to midsummer. Harvest when most seeds brown (lower seeds may shatter). Good green manure. Minimal pruning needed. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

cacao.description: The tropical tree whose seeds are fermented and processed to produce chocolate, cocoa butter, and cocoa powder—one of the world's most economically important crops.
cacao.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged; sensitive to both drought and standing water. Partial shade preferred—naturally an understory tree. Very high humidity (80%+) essential. Rich, well-draining acidic soil (pH 5.0-6.5). Fertilize monthly with balanced fertilizer during growing season. Flowers and fruits grow directly from the trunk (cauliflory). Needs temperatures above 18°C year-round. Theobromine in all parts is toxic to pets. Minimal pruning needed. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

canola.description: Also known as: Rapeseed. Oilseed crop in the Brassicaceae family. Low-erucic-acid rapeseed for edible oil and biodiesel. Yellow flowers. Spring and winter types.
canola.care_tips: Sow in early spring or fall depending on variety (spring or winter type). Full sun required. Water regularly during flowering for best seed set. Harvest when pods turn brown and seeds rattle. Prefers well-drained, fertile soil. Winter varieties need cold period for vernalization. Self-pollinating but benefits from bee activity. Non-toxic. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

cassava.description: Also known as: Manioc, Yuca, Tapioca. Tropical root crop and staple food for over 800 million people worldwide. Produces starchy tuberous roots used for flour, tapioca, and animal feed.
cassava.care_tips: Plant stem cuttings in well-drained soil after last frost. Full sun required. Water regularly during establishment, then drought-tolerant once established. Harvest roots 8-12 months after planting. Must be properly processed (soaked, fermented, or cooked) before eating to remove cyanogenic compounds. Prefers sandy loam. All raw parts toxic — must be processed before consumption. Toxic to pets. Minimal pruning needed. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

chickpea.description: Annual legume in the Fabaceae family. Desi and kabuli types. Nutrient-dense pulse; drought tolerant. Cool-season crop.
chickpea.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained, neutral soil. Inoculate with rhizobia. Harvest when pods dry and rattle. Allow plants to dry before threshing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

cinnamon.description: Tropical evergreen tree in the Lauraceae family whose inner bark is harvested and dried to produce one of the world's most important spices.
cinnamon.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil consistently moist; reduce slightly in cooler months. Partial shade to full sun — young trees prefer some protection from intense sun. Rich, acidic, well-drained sandy loam. Fertilize every 2-3 months. Bark is harvested by coppicing — cut stems at ground level during the rainy season; new shoots produce the best bark. First harvest after 2-3 years. Ceylon cinnamon has a more delicate flavor than cassia. Can be grown as a houseplant in cooler climates (aromatic leaves). Mildly toxic to pets in large quantities. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

clove.description: Tropical evergreen tree in the Myrtaceae family whose aromatic, unopened flower buds are dried to produce cloves — one of the world's oldest known spices.
clove.care_tips: Water regularly — needs consistent moisture year-round in tropical conditions. Partial shade when young; full sun once established. Rich, acidic, well-drained volcanic or loamy soil. Fertilize 2-3 times per year with organic fertilizer. Harvest flower buds when they turn pink but before they open — timing is critical for quality. First harvest after 5-7 years. Very slow-growing but extremely long-lived. Thrives near the coast in equatorial climates. Eugenol in cloves is toxic to cats and dogs — toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

red clover.description: Also known as: Meadow clover. Perennial legume in the Fabaceae family. Forage and cover crop. Nitrogen-fixing; pink flowers. Short-lived perennial (2–3 years).
red clover.care_tips: Full sun to partial shade. Well-drained soil. Inoculate seed. Harvest hay at early bloom. Good for rotation and soil building. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

white clover.description: Low-growing perennial legume commonly used as a ground cover, living mulch, and forage crop. Fixes nitrogen in the soil. Attractive to pollinators with white flower heads.
white clover.care_tips: Water occasionally — quite drought tolerant once established. Full sun to partial shade. Adapts to most soil types. Self-seeding and spreading. Tolerates mowing and foot traffic. Often used as a lawn alternative or companion plant. Non-toxic. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

arabica coffee.description: Also known as: Arabian coffee. The glossy-leaved tropical shrub that produces the world's most popular beverage, also grown as an attractive houseplant with fragrant white flowers and red cherry-like fruits.
arabica coffee.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist but not soggy; water when top 2 cm dries. Bright indirect light—scorches in direct sun. High humidity (60%+) preferred; mist regularly. Rich, well-draining, acidic soil (pH 6.0-6.5). Fertilize every 2 weeks spring through summer with balanced acidic fertilizer. May produce fragrant white flowers and red berries indoors after 3-5 years. Prefers cool nights (15-18°C). All parts except the beans are toxic to pets (caffeine). Minimal pruning needed. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

field corn.description: Annual grass in the Poaceae family. Grown for grain, silage, and ethanol. Distinguish from sweet corn; field corn harvested when kernels dry.
field corn.care_tips: Full sun. Rich, well-drained soil. Plant after soil warms. Heavy feeder—nitrogen critical. Harvest when husks dry and kernels hard (dent stage). Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

cotton.description: Annual shrub in the Malvaceae family. Grown for fiber (lint) and seed oil. Warm-season; needs long frost-free period. Upland and Pima types.
cotton.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Warm-season crop. Harvest when bolls open and lint fluffs. Defoliate before pick for cleaner harvest. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

cowpea.description: Annual legume in the Fabaceae family. Drought and heat tolerant. Black-eyed pea, crowder types. Grown for dried peas and forage.
cowpea.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Warm-season. Harvest dry beans when pods brown and rattle. Bush and vining types available. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

fava bean.description: Annual legume in the Fabaceae family. Broad bean; cool-season crop. Large seeds for drying or fresh use. Some avoid raw—contains vicine.
fava bean.care_tips: Full sun. Cool-season—plant early spring or fall. Inoculate with rhizobia. Harvest green pods when plump or dry beans when pods brown. Minimal pruning needed. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

flax.description: Annual in the Linaceae family. Grown for fiber (linen) and seeds (linseed oil, omega-3). Blue flowers. Cool-season crop.
flax.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Plant early spring. Harvest when seed capsules brown (90–110 days). Fiber types pulled when flowering. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

hemp.description: Fast-growing annual crop cultivated for thousands of years for its strong fibers, nutritious seeds, and versatile industrial applications including textiles, rope, paper, and building materials.
hemp.care_tips: Keep soil consistently moist during seedling stage; once established, moderate watering every 3-5 days. Full sun essential—at least 6 hours daily for optimal growth. Medium humidity fine. Deep, well-draining, nutrient-rich soil (pH 6.0-7.0). Heavy nitrogen feeder during vegetative growth; switch to phosphorus-potassium at flowering. Plant after last frost when soil reaches 10°C. Grows very fast—3-4 meters in one season. Mildly toxic to pets—even low-THC hemp can upset pets if eaten. Minimal pruning needed. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

hops.description: Perennial climbing vine in the Cannabaceae family. Cone-like flowers (strobiles) used in beer brewing. Dies back in winter; regrows from rhizomes.
hops.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Provide tall support (15–20 ft). Toxic to dogs—causes dangerous fever. Harvest cones when papery and aromatic (late summer). Toxic to pets. Cut bines to the ground after harvest in fall.

jute.description: Annual herbaceous plant cultivated for its strong, biodegradable bast fiber — the second most important natural fiber after cotton. Known as the 'Golden Fiber' for its silky luster.
jute.care_tips: Water abundantly — jute requires high moisture and thrives in floodplain soils. Full sun essential. Rich, alluvial, moisture-retentive soil. Warm, humid tropical climate required (minimum 20°C). Grows extremely fast (3-4m in 4 months). Harvest when plants flower; stems are retted (soaked) in water for 2-3 weeks to extract fiber. Bangladesh and India produce over 90% of world supply. Leaves of C. olitorius are edible and popular in Middle Eastern and African cuisine (molokhia). Non-toxic to pets. Minimal pruning needed. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

lentil.description: Annual legume in the Fabaceae family. Small lenticular seeds—red, green, brown. High protein pulse. Cool-season; drought tolerant.
lentil.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Cool-season crop. Harvest when pods dry and seeds rattle. Low-growing; combine or hand harvest. Minimal pruning needed. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

millet.description: Annual grass in the Poaceae family. Proso (common) millet and others. Gluten-free grain; drought tolerant. Short season (60–90 days).
millet.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Warm-season. Harvest when seed heads dry. Birds love it—harvest promptly when ripe. Minimal pruning needed. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

green gram.description: Annual legume in the Fabaceae family. Small green beans for sprouting, dals, and noodles. Warm-season; drought tolerant.
green gram.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Warm-season. Harvest dry beans when pods turn dark and rattle. Also grown for sprouts. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

mustard.description: Oilseed and condiment crop in the Brassicaceae family. Brown, yellow, oriental mustard. Seeds for oil and spice. Cool-season.
mustard.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Cool-season. Harvest when pods dry and seeds rattle. Can be used as cover crop or green manure. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

nutmeg.description: Tropical evergreen tree in the Myristicaceae family producing two spices from one fruit: nutmeg (from the seed) and mace (from the red aril surrounding it).
nutmeg.care_tips: Water regularly to maintain consistent moisture; reduce slightly during cooler dry season. Partial shade to filtered light — protect from direct afternoon sun. Deep, rich, acidic, well-drained volcanic soil. Fertilize 2-3 times per year with organic fertilizer high in potassium. Dioecious — plant both male and female trees; ratio of 1 male per 10 females. First harvest after 7-9 years. Fruits split when ripe to reveal the bright red mace covering the seed. Toxic in large doses to humans (contains myristicin); toxic to pets. Minimal pruning needed. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

oats.description: Annual grass in the Poaceae family. Cereal for oatmeal, feed, and hay. Cool-season; tolerates wetter soils than wheat. Spring and winter types.
oats.care_tips: Full sun. Tolerates heavy, moist soil. Cool-season crop. Harvest when panicles golden and kernels in hard-dough stage. Good nurse crop. Minimal pruning needed. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

oil palm.description: Tropical palm cultivated for its fruit, which yields palm oil — the world's most widely used vegetable oil. Extremely productive: produces more oil per hectare than any other crop.
oil palm.care_tips: Water regularly — needs consistent moisture and high rainfall (1800-2500mm/year). Full sun essential. Well-drained, deep, loamy soil. Fertilize heavily and regularly (4-6 times per year) with balanced fertilizer high in potassium. Begins fruiting at 3-4 years; peak production at 8-15 years. Produces fruit bunches year-round in equatorial climates. A single tree can yield 3-4 tonnes of fruit per year. Highly controversial due to deforestation concerns — sustainable certification (RSPO) encouraged. Non-toxic to pets. Minimal pruning needed. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

peanut.description: Annual legume in the Fabaceae family. Nuts develop underground (geocarpy). Valencia, Spanish, Virginia types. Warm-season; needs sandy soil.
peanut.care_tips: Full sun. Light, sandy, well-drained soil. Warm-season. Harvest when foliage yellows; dig before frost. Cure 2–3 weeks before storage. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

pigeon pea.description: Also known as: Red gram, Gandules. Drought-hardy tropical legume widely grown in South Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean for its protein-rich seeds used in dal, soups, and stews.
pigeon pea.care_tips: Drought-tolerant once established; water moderately during flowering and pod development. Full sun essential—at least 6 hours daily. Medium humidity fine. Tolerates poor soils—as a legume, it fixes nitrogen and actually improves soil fertility. Minimal fertilizer needed; too much nitrogen promotes leaves over pods. Can grow as an annual or short-lived perennial in frost-free areas. Pods can be harvested green or dry. Excellent intercrop companion. Non-toxic to humans and animals. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

quinoa.description: Pseudo-cereal in the Amaranthaceae family. Gluten-free; complete protein. Tolerates salinity and drought. Rinse seeds to remove saponins.
quinoa.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Cool-season; frost tolerant. Harvest when seed heads dry and seeds rattle. Rinse before cooking. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

rice.description: Annual grass in the Poaceae family. Staple grain grown in flooded paddies (lowland) or upland. Short-grain, long-grain, and aromatic varieties.
rice.care_tips: Full sun. Lowland rice needs flooded fields or constant moisture. Upland rice tolerates drier conditions. Harvest when panicles golden and grains hard. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

rubber tree hevea.description: Tropical tree in the Euphorbiaceae family, the primary source of natural rubber (latex). Not to be confused with Ficus elastica (rubber plant houseplant).
rubber tree hevea.care_tips: Water regularly — needs high, consistent rainfall (2000+mm/year). Full sun essential. Deep, acidic, well-drained laterite or loamy soil. Fertilize 3-4 times per year. Latex tapping begins at 5-7 years: a diagonal cut in the bark allows milky latex to flow into a collection cup. Trees can be tapped for 25-30 years. Native to the Amazon; now primarily grown in Southeast Asia (Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia produce 70% of world supply). Latex sap can cause skin irritation. Mildly toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or damaged leaves promptly.

rye.description: Annual grass in the Poaceae family. Cereal for bread, whiskey, and feed. Winter rye is cold-hardy cover crop. Tolerates poor soil.
rye.care_tips: Full sun. Tolerates poor, acidic soil. Winter rye planted fall. Harvest when heads golden. Excellent cover crop for biomass. Minimal pruning needed. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

safflower.description: Annual oilseed in the Asteraceae family. High-heat cooking oil; once used for saffron-like dye. Drought tolerant. Spiny varieties deter birds.
safflower.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Drought tolerant. Harvest when plants dry and seeds loosen. Oil and confection types available. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

sesame.description: Annual in the Pedaliaceae family. Seeds for oil and tahini. Drought and heat tolerant. Capsules shatter when ripe—harvest carefully.
sesame.care_tips: Full sun. Warm, well-drained soil. Warm-season. Harvest when lower capsules brown—plants mature unevenly. Non-shattering varieties available. Minimal pruning needed. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

sisal.description: Tropical agave cultivated for its hard, strong leaf fibers used in rope, twine, carpet, and composite materials. Each plant produces 200-250 usable leaves over its lifetime.
sisal.care_tips: Water sparingly — extremely drought tolerant once established. Full sun essential. Well-drained, even rocky or sandy soil. Minimal fertilization needed. Leaves are cut from the outer rosette starting at 2-3 years and can be harvested every 6-12 months. Plant dies after flowering (monocarpic) at 7-12 years, producing a tall flower spike up to 6m. Produces bulbils and suckers for propagation. Major production in Brazil, Tanzania, and Kenya. Leaf edges have sharp spines. Mildly toxic to pets (saponins). Minimal pruning needed. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

sorghum.description: Annual grass in the Poaceae family. Grain, syrup, forage, and biofuel. Drought tolerant. Grain, sweet, and broomcorn types.
sorghum.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Warm-season. Harvest grain when heads hard and red; syrup when stalks sweet. Frost-sensitive. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

soya bean.description: Annual legume in the Fabaceae family. Major protein and oil crop. Edamame (green), tofu, oil, feed. Nitrogen-fixing.
soya bean.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Warm-season. Harvest when pods dry and beans rattle. Inoculate with rhizobia. Rotate with corn. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

sugar beet.description: Root vegetable grown commercially for sugar production. Produces a large white conical root with up to 20% sugar content; accounts for about 30% of world sugar production.
sugar beet.care_tips: Direct sow seeds 2cm deep after last frost, spacing 15cm apart. Full sun required. Keep soil consistently moist during root development. Harvest after 90-100 days when roots are 7-10cm diameter. Prefers loose, well-drained soil free of rocks. Fertilize at planting with balanced fertilizer. Cool-season crop; best in spring or fall. Non-toxic. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

sugarcane.description: Perennial grass in the Poaceae family. Tropical crop for sugar and ethanol. Tall canes store sucrose. Ratoons (regrowth) for multiple harvests.
sugarcane.care_tips: Full sun. Tropical—frost kills. Plant stem cuttings (setts). Harvest when canes mature (12–24 months). Needs abundant water and heat. Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

oil sunflower.description: Annual in the Asteraceae family. Confection (snack) and oil types. Oil types have small black seeds; high in linoleic acid.
oil sunflower.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Warm-season. Harvest when back of heads yellow and seeds dry. Protect from birds with bags or netting. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

sweet potato.description: Perennial vine in the Convolvulaceae family, grown as annual. Starchy tuber roots; not a potato. Orange, white, purple flesh. Warm-season.
sweet potato.care_tips: Full sun. Light, sandy soil. Warm-season. Plant slips. Harvest before frost when roots reach size. Cure 1–2 weeks for storage. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

teff.description: Annual grass in the Poaceae family. Tiny gluten-free grain; staple in Ethiopia. Drought tolerant. Seeds minuscule—harvest carefully.
teff.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Warm-season. Harvest when seed heads dry. Cut and cure in field; thresh carefully—seeds easily lost. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

tobacco.description: Annual herb in the Solanaceae family. Leaves contain nicotine; grown for commercial tobacco. Ornamental Nicotiana species differ. Not for consumption.
tobacco.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Water regularly. Toxic to pets—nicotine in all plant parts. Keep away from animals and children. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

wheat.description: Annual grass in the Poaceae family. World's major cereal crop. Bread wheat (T. aestivum) and durum. Spring and winter types by planting season.
wheat.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Winter wheat planted fall; spring wheat in spring. Harvest when heads golden and kernels hard (combine or cut when dry). Remove damaged or diseased plant material.

yerba mate.description: Subtropical holly tree native to South America whose leaves are brewed into mate — a traditional caffeinated beverage central to the culture of Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay, and southern Brazil.
yerba mate.care_tips: Water regularly to keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged. Partial shade to filtered sun — grows naturally in the understory. Acidic, well-drained, red laterite soil rich in iron. Fertilize 2-3 times per year. Harvest by pruning branches — the plant regrows vigorously. First harvest after 3-4 years. Leaves are dried and often smoked to produce the traditional mate tea, traditionally consumed from a gourd (mate) with a metal straw (bombilla). Contains caffeine, theobromine, and many antioxidants. Non-toxic to pets.

adzuki sprouts.description: Bean sprouts from adzuki beans. Crunchy, mild, nutty. Harvest in 4–6 days. Rinse 2–3× daily.
adzuki sprouts.care_tips: Soak seeds 8-12 hours. Rinse 2-3× daily; drain thoroughly. No light needed during sprouting. Harvest in 3-5 days when tails are 1-2 inches. Sweet, nutty flavor. No fertilizer needed. Rich in protein, fiber, and folate. Discard any batch that smells sour or shows mold.

alfalfa sprouts.description: Classic delicate sprouts from alfalfa seeds. Mild flavor; harvest in 5–7 days. Rinse 2–3× daily.
alfalfa sprouts.care_tips: Soak seeds 4-8 hours. Rinse 2× daily; drain well. Keep in dark first 3 days, then move to indirect light for greening. Harvest in 5-7 days. Mild, nutty flavor. No fertilizer. Rich in vitamins K and C. Store refrigerated up to 5 days. Discard any batch that smells sour or shows mold.

amaranth microgreens.description: Colorful microgreens from amaranth. Pink or green; mild. Harvest at first true leaves (7–12 days).
amaranth microgreens.care_tips: Sow on moist medium; mist to keep damp. Do not cover seeds (need light to germinate). Bright indirect light once sprouted. Mist 1-2× daily. Harvest in 8-12 days. Vibrant magenta stems with mild, earthy flavor. Rich in protein and lysine. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

arugula microgreens.description: Peppery microgreens from arugula seeds. Fast-growing. Harvest at first true leaves (7–10 days).
arugula microgreens.care_tips: Sow on moist medium; press gently. Mist 1-2× daily. Bright indirect light. Harvest in 7-10 days at first true leaves. Spicy, peppery flavor—milder than mature arugula. No fertilizer. Fast growing; great for beginners. Rich in vitamins A and K. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

basil microgreens.description: Aromatic microgreens from basil. Intense flavor. Harvest at first true leaves (10–14 days).
basil microgreens.care_tips: Soak seeds 2-4 hours (mucilaginous coating). Sow on moist medium. Mist 1-2× daily. Bright indirect light. Harvest in 10-16 days. Concentrated basil aroma. Slow germinator—be patient. Rich in polyphenols. Remove yellowing or damaged leaves promptly.

beet microgreens.description: Vibrant red-stemmed microgreens from beet. Earthy, sweet. Harvest at first true leaves (10–14 days).
beet microgreens.care_tips: Soak seed clusters 8-12 hours. Sow on moist medium, press in. Mist 1-2× daily. Bright indirect light. Harvest in 10-14 days. Stunning ruby-red stems with earthy, sweet flavor. Each 'seed' produces multiple sprouts. Rich in iron and betalains. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

broccoli raab microgreens.description: Mild mustard-like microgreens from broccoli raab. Harvest at first true leaves (8–12 days).
broccoli raab microgreens.care_tips: Sow on moist medium; mist to keep damp. Bright indirect light. Harvest in 7-10 days at cotyledon stage. Slightly spicy, broccoli-like flavor with a hint of mustard. No fertilizer. Rich in sulforaphane and vitamins A and C. Harvest by cutting at soil level when cotyledons or first true leaves appear.

broccoli sprouts.description: High-sulforaphane sprouts from broccoli seeds. Nutritious; harvest in 4–6 days. Rinse 2–3× daily.
broccoli sprouts.care_tips: Soak seeds 6-8 hours. Rinse 2× daily; drain thoroughly. Keep dark first 3 days, then bright indirect light. Harvest in 5-7 days. Mild, slightly spicy. One of the richest food sources of sulforaphane—a potent antioxidant. Store refrigerated. Rinse and drain well before eating; discard any batch that smells sour or shows mold.

buckwheat sprouts.description: Nutty sprouts from buckwheat groats. Hulled for eating. Harvest when 1–2 in (3–5 days).
buckwheat sprouts.care_tips: Soak seeds 15-30 minutes only (over-soaking causes mushiness). Rinse 2× daily; drain very well. Bright indirect light for greening. Harvest in 7-10 days. Mild, lettuce-like flavor. Remove hulls before eating. Rich in rutin and complete protein. Rinse and drain well before eating; discard any batch that smells sour or shows mold.

carrot microgreens.description: Fine, feathery microgreens from carrot. Slow to germinate. Harvest at first true leaves (14–21 days).
carrot microgreens.care_tips: Sow on moist medium; press in. Keep moist—mist 2× daily. Bright indirect light. Slow germinator; harvest in 14-18 days. Concentrated carrot flavor; wispy, feathery tops. Patience required—one of the slower microgreens. Rich in beta-carotene. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

cilantro microgreens.description: Strong cilantro flavor in microgreen form. Harvest at first true leaves (12–14 days).
cilantro microgreens.care_tips: Gently crush seed husks before soaking 8-12 hours. Sow on moist medium. Mist 1-2× daily. Bright indirect light. Harvest in 14-21 days. Full cilantro aroma; slow germinator. Each husk produces 2 plants. Rich in vitamins A and K. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

clover sprouts.description: Mild, delicate sprouts similar to alfalfa. Harvest in 5–7 days. Rinse 2–3× daily.
clover sprouts.care_tips: Soak seeds 4-8 hours. Rinse 2× daily; drain well. Keep dark first 3 days, then move to indirect light. Harvest in 5-7 days. Mild, fresh, slightly sweet flavor. Tiny and delicate. No fertilizer. Rich in isoflavones and vitamins A and C. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

garden cress.description: Peppery, fast-growing sprouts. Harvest in 5–7 days. Can grow on paper towel.
garden cress.care_tips: Sow on moist paper towel or medium; seeds stick when wet (mucilaginous). Mist 1-2× daily—do not rinse. Bright indirect light. Harvest in 5-7 days. Peppery, tangy flavor. One of the fastest and easiest microgreens. Rich in vitamins A, C, and K. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

dill microgreens.description: Aromatic dill flavor. Harvest at first true leaves (10–14 days).
dill microgreens.care_tips: Sow on moist medium; press gently. Mist 1-2× daily. Bright indirect light. Harvest in 14-21 days at cotyledon stage. Concentrated dill flavor—excellent with fish and eggs. Slow germinator; requires patience. Rich in antioxidants. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

fenugreek sprouts.description: Aromatic, slightly bitter sprouts. Curry-like. Harvest in 4–6 days. Rinse 2× daily.
fenugreek sprouts.care_tips: Soak seeds 8-12 hours. Rinse 2× daily; drain well. Keep dark. Harvest in 3-5 days. Slightly bitter, maple-like flavor; popular in Indian cuisine. Quick and easy to grow. Rich in iron, protein, and soluble fiber. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

kale microgreens.description: Nutritious microgreens; mild cabbage flavor. Harvest at first true leaves (8–12 days).
kale microgreens.care_tips: Sow on moist medium; press gently. Mist 1-2× daily. Bright indirect light. Harvest in 8-12 days. Mild, slightly sweet—less bitter than mature kale. Purple or green varieties. No fertilizer. Rich in vitamins A, C, K, and calcium. Harvest by cutting at soil level when cotyledons or first true leaves appear.

leek sprouts.description: Mild, sweet allium flavor, gentler than onion sprouts. Harvest at first true leaves (10–14 days).
leek sprouts.care_tips: Soak seeds 8-12 hours. Sow on moist medium; keep damp. Mist 1-2× daily. Bright indirect light. Harvest in 12-14 days. Delicate onion-leek flavor, milder than mature leeks. Thin, elegant garnish. Rich in folate and vitamin K. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly. Toxic to pets.

lentil sprouts.description: Bean sprouts from lentils. Earthy. Harvest in 3–5 days. Soak 8 hrs first.
lentil sprouts.care_tips: Soak seeds 8-12 hours. Rinse 2-3× daily; drain thoroughly. Keep dark. Harvest in 3-5 days when tails are 1/2-1 inch. Mild, slightly sweet, earthy. Best cooked lightly or added to stir-fries. Rich in protein, iron, and folate. Rinse and drain well before eating; discard any batch that smells sour or shows mold.

mizuna microgreens.description: Mild, mustard-like Japanese green. Harvest at first true leaves (8–12 days).
mizuna microgreens.care_tips: Sow on moist medium; press gently. Mist 1-2× daily. Bright indirect light. Harvest in 7-10 days. Mild, peppery mustard flavor with serrated leaves. Japanese green; popular in salad mixes. Fast grower. Rich in vitamins A and C. Harvest by cutting at soil level when cotyledons or first true leaves appear.

mung bean sprouts.description: Classic Asian bean sprouts. Crunchy; harvest when 2–3 in (4–6 days). Rinse 2–3× daily.
mung bean sprouts.care_tips: Soak seeds 8-12 hours. Rinse 2-3× daily; drain thoroughly. Keep dark for thick, white sprouts. Harvest in 3-5 days. Crisp, mild, slightly sweet. Staple in Asian cuisine—stir-fries, pho, spring rolls. Rich in vitamin C and protein. Discard any batch that smells sour or shows mold.

mustard microgreens.description: Spicy, pungent microgreens. Red or green. Harvest at first true leaves (6–10 days).
mustard microgreens.care_tips: Sow on moist medium; press gently. Mist 1-2× daily. Bright indirect light. Harvest in 7-10 days. Spicy, horseradish-like kick—among the most flavorful microgreens. Yellow, brown, or red varieties. Fast grower. Rich in vitamins A, C, and K. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

onion sprouts.description: Mild onion-flavored sprouts with a gentle allium bite. Harvest at first true leaves (10–14 days). Pre-soak seeds before planting.
onion sprouts.care_tips: Soak seeds 8-12 hours. Sow on moist medium; keep damp. Mist 1-2× daily. Bright indirect light. Harvest in 10-14 days when 3-4 inches tall. Mild onion flavor; excellent garnish for soups and salads. Thin and elegant. Rich in quercetin and vitamin C. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly. Toxic to pets.

pea shoots.description: Young pea plants grown from seeds, harvested for tender shoots and leaves. Quick-growing microgreen with sweet pea flavor.
pea shoots.care_tips: Soak seeds 12-24 hours. Sow densely on moist medium. Water daily; drain well. Bright indirect light for greening. Harvest in 10-14 days by cutting above first node—may regrow for second harvest. Sweet, fresh pea flavor. Excellent in salads and stir-fries. Rich in vitamins A and C. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

radish microgreens.description: Spicy, colorful. Fast-growing. Harvest at first true leaves (6–10 days).
radish microgreens.care_tips: Sow on moist medium; press gently. Mist 1-2× daily. Bright indirect light. Harvest in 5-8 days. Spicy, peppery crunch. One of the fastest and easiest microgreens to grow. Red-stemmed varieties are visually striking. Rich in vitamins A, B, C, E, and K. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

sesame sprouts.description: Nutty, tender sprouts from sesame seeds. Harvest when 1–2 in (4–6 days). Rinse 2× daily. Hulled seeds preferred.
sesame sprouts.care_tips: Soak seeds 4-8 hours. Rinse 2× daily; drain well. Keep in dark. Harvest in 3-5 days. Mild, nutty sesame flavor. Small and delicate. Rinse thoroughly to remove seed coats. Rich in calcium, iron, and healthy fats. Rinse and drain well before eating; discard any batch that smells sour or shows mold.

shiso microgreens.description: Mint-basil flavored microgreens from shiso (perilla). Green or red. Harvest at first true leaves (10–14 days).
shiso microgreens.care_tips: Sow on moist medium; press gently—seeds need light. Mist 1-2× daily. Bright indirect light; warm conditions. Harvest in 14-21 days. Complex flavor—minty, basil-like with anise notes. Green or purple varieties. Slow germinator. Prized in Japanese cuisine. Remove yellowing or damaged leaves promptly.

soybean sprouts.description: Large bean sprouts from soybeans. Crunchy; cook before eating. Harvest when 2–3 in (4–6 days). Rinse 2× daily.
soybean sprouts.care_tips: Soak seeds 12 hours. Rinse 2-3× daily; drain thoroughly. Keep dark and weighted for thick sprouts. Harvest in 4-6 days. Mild, bean-like flavor; best cooked (blanched or stir-fried). Staple in Korean cuisine (kongnamul). Rich in protein, isoflavones, and vitamin C. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

sprouts microgreens.description: Young seedlings harvested within 1-3 weeks of germination. Sprouts are grown in water only; microgreens are grown on a thin layer of soil or growing medium. Nutrient-dense and easy to grow indoors year-round. Popular mixes combine varied flavors, colors, and textures.
sprouts microgreens.care_tips: Mist or water lightly 1-2 times daily to keep seeds and growing medium moist. Never let dry out, but avoid standing water which causes mold. Bright indirect light preferred (a windowsill or grow light). Good air circulation essential to prevent mold and damping off. No fertilizer needed — seeds contain all necessary nutrients. Use clean, food-safe containers and fresh seeds. Harvest sprouts in 3-7 days, microgreens in 7-14 days. Rinse sprouts twice daily. Succession sow every few days for continuous harvest. Harvest by cutting at soil level when cotyledons or first true leaves appear.

sunflower sprouts.description: Nutty, crunchy sunflower sprouts. Use hulled seeds. Harvest when 1–2 in (7–10 days).
sunflower sprouts.care_tips: Soak seeds 8-12 hours. Sow on moist medium; cover 2 days for germination. Mist 1-2× daily. Bright indirect light once sprouted. Harvest in 7-12 days when cotyledons are fully open. Nutty, crunchy flavor. Rich in protein, vitamin E, and healthy fats. Remove hulls before eating. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

tatsoi microgreens.description: Mild brassica; spoon-shaped leaves. Harvest at first true leaves (8–12 days).
tatsoi microgreens.care_tips: Sow on moist medium; press gently. Mist 1-2× daily. Bright indirect light. Harvest in 7-10 days. Mild, creamy mustard flavor with rounded spoon-shaped leaves. Asian green; excellent in salad mixes. Fast grower. Rich in vitamins A, C, and calcium. Harvest by cutting at soil level when cotyledons or first true leaves appear.

turnip microgreens.description: Mild, slightly peppery. Harvest at first true leaves (8–12 days).
turnip microgreens.care_tips: Sow on moist medium; press gently. Mist 1-2× daily. Bright indirect light. Harvest in 7-10 days. Mild, slightly spicy, turnip-like flavor. Fast and reliable grower—good for beginners. Rich in vitamins A, C, and K. Harvest by cutting at soil level when cotyledons or first true leaves appear.

watercress sprouts.description: Peppery, nutrient-dense sprouts from the aquatic watercress plant. One of the oldest known leaf vegetables. Rich in iron, calcium, and vitamins K and C. Harvest in 5-7 days. Keep constantly moist—watercress naturally grows in shallow running water.
watercress sprouts.care_tips: Mist 2× daily—keep constantly moist; watercress is semi-aquatic. Bright indirect light. Harvest in 5-7 days. Peppery, slightly bitter flavor. Can grow on wet paper towel without soil. Rich in iron, calcium, and vitamins K and C. One of the oldest known leaf vegetables. Discard any batch that smells sour or shows mold.

wheatgrass.description: Juiced or chewed; nutrient-dense. Harvest when 6–8 in (7–10 days). Second cut possible.
wheatgrass.care_tips: Soak seeds 8-12 hours. Sow on moist medium or coconut coir. Water 1-2× daily; avoid waterlogging. Bright indirect light. Harvest at 6-7 inches (7-10 days) by cutting above the root. Juice fresh for maximum nutrition—rich in chlorophyll, vitamins A, C, E, and minerals. Discard any batch that smells sour or shows mold.

allium.description: Ornamental flowering bulbs in the Amaryllidaceae family, include edible onions and ornamental varieties.
allium.care_tips: Keep soil moist during growth and flowering. Allow to dry after foliage dies back. Plant bulbs in fall. Full sun preferred. Well-drained soil essential. Fertilize when shoots emerge. Ornamental varieties have large, spherical flower heads. Naturalize well. Allow foliage to die back naturally. Deterrent to many pests. Perfect for borders and cut flowers. Bulbs go dormant after flowering; reduce watering when foliage dies back. Toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

amaryllis.description: Large flowering bulbs in the Amaryllidaceae family, popular for indoor winter forcing, can rebloom with proper care.
amaryllis.care_tips: Keep soil moist during active growth and flowering. Reduce watering after flowering as foliage dies back. For forcing: plant in fall, keep in cool dark place until shoots appear, then move to bright light. For outdoor: plant in spring in warm climates. Bright indirect to direct light. Fertilize monthly during active growth. Can rebloom with proper dormancy care. Large, showy flowers. Perfect for holiday displays. Toxic to pets. Deadhead after flowering but leave foliage until it yellows naturally to feed the bulb.

anemone.description: Also known as: Poppy anemone. Spring-blooming tuberous perennials. Anemone blanda (early) and A. coronaria (poppy). Plant in fall; dormant after flowering.
anemone.care_tips: Keep moist during growth and bloom. Full sun to partial shade. Plant tubers in fall. Reduce watering when foliage dies back. Allow foliage to yellow before removing. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

bluebell.description: Also known as: English bluebell, Wood hyacinth. Spring bulbs in the Asparagaceae family that carpet woodlands with nodding violet-blue bells; the English species is protected in the UK, and the vigorous Spanish species and hybrids can take over gardens.
bluebell.care_tips: Water in spring while in leaf if the season is dry; keep bulbs dry and undisturbed during summer dormancy. Partial shade under deciduous trees is ideal; tolerates sun in cool climates. Hardy to about -25°C; needs winter chill. Medium humidity. No fertilizer needed; a leaf-mould mulch in autumn is enough. Humus-rich, well-draining soil. Plant bulbs 10 cm deep in autumn; let foliage die down naturally to feed the bulb. Spreads by seed and offsets, so deadhead Spanish bluebells to limit self-seeding and never dump bulbs in the wild. Toxic to pets; all parts contain cardiac glycosides. Remove yell

bulbs.description: Plants that grow from underground storage organs (bulbs, corms, tubers, rhizomes). Many are spring-flowering and require a winter chilling period.
bulbs.care_tips: Water moderately during active growth — keep soil moist but not waterlogged. Reduce watering as foliage yellows and dies back after flowering. Do not cut foliage until fully brown — leaves feed the bulb for next year. Plant at depth of 2-3 times bulb height. Full sun to partial shade depending on species. Fertilize at planting and again when shoots emerge in spring with balanced bulb fertilizer. Lift and store tender bulbs before frost in cold climates. Many spring bulbs need a winter chill period to bloom. Research specific species for exact requirements. Deadhead after flowering but leave fo

calla lily.description: Also known as: Arum lily. Tuberous aroid with elegant spathe flowers in white, pink, or dark cultivars. Grown as houseplant or garden bulb; goes dormant after bloom.
calla lily.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist during growth and flowering. Reduce watering when foliage yellows; allow dormancy. Bright indirect light indoors; full sun to partial shade outdoors. Well-draining soil. Fertilize monthly during active growth. Toxic to pets and humans if ingested; causes mouth and throat irritation. Remove spent flower stems at the base; trim yellowed foliage once dormancy begins and keep the rhizomes dry until spring.

camassia.description: Also known as: Common camas, Small camas. Native North American bulb producing tall spikes of starry blue, purple, or white flowers in late spring—historically an important food source for Indigenous peoples.
camassia.care_tips: Water regularly during spring growth and flowering; allow to go dry after foliage dies back in summer (summer dormant). Full sun to partial shade. Medium humidity fine. Prefers moist, moisture-retentive clay or loam soil that dries out in summer—perfect for seasonal wet meadows. Minimal fertilizer needed; top-dress with compost in fall. Plant bulbs in fall, 10-15 cm deep. Naturalizes beautifully in lawns and meadows. Leave foliage to die back naturally. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

canna.description: Tender rhizomatous bulbs with bold foliage and tropical flowers. Summer bloomer; lift before frost or mulch in zone 8+.
canna.care_tips: Full sun. Rich, moist soil. Water regularly in summer. Fertilize monthly. Lift rhizomes after frost; store dry over winter. Replant in spring. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

scientific_names: Scilla forbesii (syn. Chionodoxa forbesii; Glory of the snow)
glory of the snow.description: Early spring bulb with blue star flowers. Naturalizes well. Plant in fall. Dormant after bloom.
glory of the snow.care_tips: Full sun to partial shade. Well-drained soil. Plant bulbs in fall. Keep moist during growth; reduce when foliage dies. Allow foliage to yellow naturally. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

crocosmia.description: Also known as: Montbretia. Cormous perennial with arching stems of fiery funnel-shaped flowers in summer. 'Lucifer' is one of the bestselling garden plants worldwide.
crocosmia.care_tips: Water regularly during active growth; reduce after flowering. Full sun for best flowering; tolerates light shade. Well-drained soil — corms rot in waterlogged winter conditions. Fertilize in spring as growth emerges with balanced fertilizer. Plant corms 8-10cm deep. Clumps spread vigorously and should be divided every 3-4 years. 'Lucifer' is the most reliable variety with intense red flowers. Montbretia can be invasive in mild, wet climates (listed as invasive in parts of UK and New Zealand). Non-toxic to pets. Deadhead after flowering but leave foliage until it yellows naturally to feed the b

crocus.description: Early spring flowering bulbs in the Iridaceae family, among first flowers to bloom, naturalize well.
crocus.care_tips: Keep soil moist during growth and flowering (spring). Allow to dry naturally after foliage dies back. Plant bulbs in fall (6-8 weeks before ground freezes). Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize when shoots emerge. Among first flowers to bloom in spring. Naturalize well - will spread over time. Allow foliage to die back naturally. Perfect for naturalizing in lawns or under trees. Bulbs go dormant after flowering; reduce watering when foliage dies back. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

saffron crocus.description: Fall-blooming crocus. Red stigmas yield saffron spice. Dormant summer; leaves appear spring, flowers fall.
saffron crocus.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Water when leaves present (spring) and during bloom (fall). Harvest stigmas when flowers open. Dry before storing. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

daffodils.description: Also known as: Jonquil. Spring-blooming bulbous perennials in the Amaryllidaceae family, planted in fall, naturalize well and are deer-resistant.
daffodils.care_tips: Keep soil moist during growth and flowering (spring). Allow to dry after foliage dies back. Plant bulbs in fall (6-8 weeks before ground freezes) with pointed end up, 4-6 inches deep. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize when shoots emerge and after flowering with bulb fertilizer. Allow foliage to die back naturally - don't cut until yellow. Naturalize well and multiply over time. Deer and rodent resistant. Excellent for naturalizing in lawns and gardens. Bulbs go dormant after flowering; reduce watering when foliage dies back. Toxic to pets. Deadhead after flowering but leave foliage until it

dahlia.description: Also known as: Garden dahlia. Tender tubers with showy summer flowers. Thousands of cultivars. Lift before frost; store dry over winter.
dahlia.care_tips: Full sun. Rich, well-drained soil. Water regularly; stake tall varieties. Deadhead for continuous bloom. Lift tubers after frost; store in cool, dry place. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset.

freesia.description: Fragrant spring corms. Plant in fall (mild climates) or spring. Tubular flowers in many colors. Tender—lift in cold zones.
freesia.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Plant corms 2 in deep. Keep moist during growth. Reduce when foliage yellows. Lift and store in cold-winter areas. Deadhead after flowering but leave foliage until it yellows naturally to feed the bulb.

fritillaria.description: Also known as: Snake's head. Spring bulbs with nodding, checkered or crown-shaped flowers. Snake's head (F. meleagris) and crown imperial. Plant in fall.
fritillaria.care_tips: Full sun to partial shade. Moist, well-drained soil. Plant bulbs on side (hollow crown). Keep moist during growth. Dormant after flowering. Toxic to pets. Deadhead after flowering but leave foliage until it yellows naturally to feed the bulb.

gladiolus.description: Also known as: Garden gladiolus. Summer flowering bulbs in the Iridaceae family with tall spikes of colorful flowers, excellent for cut flowers.
gladiolus.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist during growth and flowering (summer). Plant corms in spring after last frost. Full sun essential (6-8 hours daily). Fertilize when shoots emerge and during flowering. Stake tall varieties. Lift corms in fall in cold climates and store over winter. Allow foliage to die back before lifting. Excellent for cut flowers. Plant in succession for continuous blooms. Bulbs go dormant after flowering; reduce watering when foliage dies back. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset. Deadhead after flowering but leave foliage until it yellows naturally to feed the bulb.

hyacinth.description: Fragrant spring flowering bulbs in the Asparagaceae family, can be forced indoors or grown outdoors.
hyacinth.care_tips: Keep soil moist during growth and flowering. Allow to dry after foliage dies back. Plant bulbs in fall (6-8 weeks before ground freezes). Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize when shoots emerge. Very fragrant flowers. Can be forced indoors with pre-chilling. Naturalize slowly. Allow foliage to die back naturally. Perfect for spring borders and containers. Bulbs go dormant after flowering; reduce watering when foliage dies back. Toxic to pets. Deadhead after flowering but leave foliage until it yellows naturally to feed the bulb.

dutch iris.description: Hybrid spring bulb with slender stems and elegant flowers in blue, purple, white, or yellow. Plant in fall for spring bloom; goes dormant after flowering.
dutch iris.care_tips: Plant bulbs in fall, 4–5 inches deep. Full sun. Well-drained soil essential. Water during spring growth and bloom; allow foliage to yellow before cutting back. Fertilize when shoots emerge. Bulbs go dormant in summer—no watering needed. Suitable for beds, borders, and cut flowers. Toxic to pets. Deadhead after flowering but leave foliage until it yellows naturally to feed the bulb.

lilies.description: Also known as: Lily. Bulbous perennial flowering plants in the Liliaceae family with showy trumpet-shaped or recurved flowers, many are fragrant.
lilies.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist during growth and flowering (spring-summer). Allow to dry slightly after flowering. Well-drained soil essential - avoid waterlogged conditions. Full sun to partial shade depending on species. Fertilize when shoots emerge and after flowering with bulb fertilizer. Plant bulbs in fall or early spring. Mulch to keep roots cool. Remove spent flowers but leave foliage until yellow. Divide bulbs every 3-4 years. Many are fragrant. Research specific type for exact requirements. Bulbs go dormant after flowering; reduce watering when foliage dies back. Toxic to pets. Deadhead afte

asiatic lily.description: Early summer lily with upright, unscented flowers. Cold hardy. Plant in fall or spring. Multiply by scales or division.
asiatic lily.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Plant bulbs 4–6 in deep. Keep moist during growth. Stake if needed. Highly toxic to cats—can cause fatal kidney failure. Toxic to pets. Deadhead after flowering but leave foliage until it yellows naturally to feed the bulb.

mini calla lily.description: Also known as: Compact calla. Compact Zantedeschia with smaller spathes. Colors include pink, yellow, orange. Toxic to pets.
mini calla lily.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light indoors; full sun to partial shade outdoors. Fertilize during growing season. Toxic to pets and humans if ingested; causes mouth and throat irritation. Remove spent flower stems at the base; trim yellowed foliage once dormancy begins and keep the rhizomes dry until spring.

oriental lily.description: Fragrant late-summer lilies. Large, often spotted flowers. Stargazer and Casablanca types. Toxic to cats.
oriental lily.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry — excellent drainage essential to prevent bulb rot. Partial shade preferred, especially afternoon shade in hot climates. Intensely fragrant blooms in late summer (July-August) in white, pink, or red. Stake tall stems before flowering. Acidic to neutral soil preferred. Do not plant near Tiger Lilies, which can transmit Lily Mosaic Virus asymptomatically. Mulch to keep roots cool. Highly toxic to cats — can cause fatal kidney failure. Deadhead after flowering but leave foliage until it yellows naturally to feed the bulb.

tiger lily.description: Orange Turk's-cap lily with black spots. Lilium lancifolium. Naturalizes; can spread. Toxic to cats.
tiger lily.care_tips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Full sun to partial shade — tougher and more adaptable than Oriental Lilies. Blooms early to mid summer with recurved orange spotted flowers. Produces bulbils in leaf axils that drop and grow into new plants — naturalizes readily. Very cold hardy and disease resistant. Asymptomatic carrier of Lily Mosaic Virus — keep away from Oriental and Asiatic Lilies. Highly toxic to cats — can cause fatal kidney failure. Deadhead after flowering but leave foliage until it yellows naturally to feed the bulb.

muscari.description: Early spring bulb with grape-like blue flowers. Naturalizes aggressively. Plant in fall. Dormant after bloom.
muscari.care_tips: Full sun to partial shade. Well-drained soil. Plant bulbs in fall. Keep moist during growth. Allow foliage to yellow. Can spread—contain if desired. Deadhead after flowering but leave foliage until it yellows naturally to feed the bulb.

ranunculus.description: Spring tuber with layered, rose-like flowers. Soak tubers before planting. Plant in fall (mild) or spring. Dormant after bloom.
ranunculus.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Soak tubers 4 hrs before planting. Keep moist during growth. Reduce when foliage yellows. Lift in cold zones. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

garden ranunculus.description: Tuberous perennial producing exquisite, densely layered paper-thin petals in warm shades of yellow, orange, red, pink, and white; a favorite for spring bouquets.
garden ranunculus.care_tips: Soak dried tubers (claw-side down) for 3-4 hours before planting. Water regularly during active growth to keep soil evenly moist but never soggy. Full sun to light shade in hot climates; prefers cool spring temperatures (10-20°C) for best blooms. Well-drained soil is critical — tubers rot in wet conditions. Fertilize every 2 weeks during growth with balanced liquid fertilizer. Stop watering when foliage yellows after blooming; lift tubers in cold zones (below zone 8) and store dry. Toxic to pets — all parts contain protoanemonin. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

scilla.description: Early spring bulb with blue bell flowers. Siberian squill naturalizes well. Plant in fall. Dormant after bloom.
scilla.care_tips: Full sun to partial shade. Well-drained soil. Plant bulbs in fall. Keep moist during growth. Reduce when foliage dies. Allow leaves to yellow naturally. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

snowdrop.description: One of the earliest spring bulbs, often blooming through snow. Dainty nodding white flowers with green markings appear from late winter to early spring.
snowdrop.care_tips: Plant bulbs in fall, 7-10cm deep and 7cm apart. Moist, well-drained soil during growing season; tolerate summer dormancy dry-out. Partial shade under deciduous trees is ideal — they bloom before leaves emerge. Do not remove foliage until it yellows naturally. Best divided 'in the green' (while still in leaf) after flowering. Naturalizes well in lawns and woodland. Mildly toxic if ingested. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

tuberose.description: Highly fragrant summer bulb. White tubular flowers. Tender—lift before frost. Used in perfumery.
tuberose.care_tips: Full sun. Well-drained soil. Plant when soil warm. Water regularly. Stake if needed. Lift tubers after frost; store dry. Replant in spring. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset. Deadhead after flowering but leave foliage until it yellows naturally to feed the bulb.

tulips.description: Spring-blooming bulbous perennials in the Liliaceae family, planted in fall for spring flowers, many varieties available.
tulips.care_tips: Keep soil moist during growth and flowering (spring). Allow to dry after foliage dies back. Plant bulbs in fall (6-8 weeks before ground freezes) with pointed end up, 6-8 inches deep. Full sun preferred. Fertilize when shoots emerge and after flowering with bulb fertilizer. Allow foliage to die back naturally to feed bulbs - don't cut until yellow. Many varieties are treated as annuals in warm climates. Research variety type for exact requirements and bloom time. Bulbs go dormant after flowering; reduce watering when foliage dies back. Toxic to pets. Deadhead after flowering but leave foliage

amazon sword.description: Also known as: Broadleaf Amazon Sword, Paniculatus Sword. Popular background aquarium plant with large, bright-green rosette leaves that can grow up to 50 cm tall.
amazon sword.care_tips: Moderate to high light — 10-12 hours per day for strong growth. Plant roots firmly in nutrient-rich substrate; root tabs recommended. pH 6.5-7.5. Heavy root feeder — iron-rich substrate or fertilizer essential. Propagates via runner shoots which can be separated. Grows large — best as background or centerpiece plant. Non-toxic and safe for all aquarium inhabitants. Remove dead or yellowing leaves. Thin overcrowded plants to maintain water quality.

anubias.description: Hardy, low-light aquarium plant with thick dark green leaves that grows attached to rocks and driftwood.
anubias.care_tips: Low to moderate light preferred — too much light promotes algae growth on leaves. Never bury rhizome in substrate — attach to rocks or driftwood. pH 6.5-7.8. Very slow grower — new leaf every 2-3 months. No CO2 needed. Minimal fertilization. Extremely resilient and nearly indestructible. Non-toxic to all fish, shrimp, and snails. Remove dead or yellowing leaves. Thin overcrowded plants to maintain water quality.

aquatic plants.description: Plants that grow fully or partially submerged in water, include floating, submerged, and emergent types.
aquatic plants.care_tips: Fully submerged or floating in water - no soil watering needed. Maintain water quality - clean, oxygenated water essential. Full sun to partial shade depending on species. Fertilize with aquatic plant fertilizer tablets placed in soil or water. Remove dead leaves and flowers regularly. Control algae growth. Some species are invasive - check local regulations. Water depth varies by species. Research specific plant for exact requirements. Perfect for ponds and water gardens. Aquatic; winter care varies by Hardiness Zone. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

arrowhead.description: Also known as: Duck potato. Aquatic pond plant (Sagittaria)—not the houseplant Arrowhead plant (Syngonium). Arrow-shaped leaves; grows in shallow water or pond edges. Edible tubers (duck potato).
arrowhead.care_tips: Shallow water (2–12 in) or saturated soil. Full sun. Plant in pond margin or container. Divide when crowded. No soil watering—plant in water. Remove dead or yellowing leaves. Thin overcrowded plants to maintain water quality.

bog plants.description: Plants adapted to constantly wet or waterlogged soil, ideal for water gardens and pond edges.
bog plants.care_tips: Keep soil constantly moist or waterlogged - never allow to dry out. Can grow in shallow water (up to 6 inches). Full sun to partial shade depending on species. Fertilize monthly during growing season with aquatic plant fertilizer. Ideal for water gardens and pond edges. Some species spread aggressively - contain with barriers. Remove dead foliage. Research specific plant for exact requirements. Adapted to constantly wet conditions. Aquatic; winter care varies by Hardiness Zone. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly. Cut spent flower stalks at the base.

cattails.description: Emergent wetland plants in the Typhaceae family, grow in shallow water or wet soil, can be invasive.
cattails.care_tips: Grow in shallow water (6-12 inches) or constantly wet soil. Never allow to dry out. Full sun preferred. Fertilize sparingly if at all. Spreads aggressively by rhizomes - contain with barriers or grow in containers. Remove seed heads to prevent spread. Can be invasive - check local regulations. Perfect for pond edges and water gardens. Provides wildlife habitat. Aquatic; winter care varies by Hardiness Zone. Remove dead or yellowing leaves. Thin overcrowded plants to maintain water quality.

duckweed.description: Tiny floating plants. Rapid spread; provides shade and filtration. Can be invasive. Often used in aquariums and small ponds.
duckweed.care_tips: Floats on still water. Full sun to partial shade. No planting—add to water surface. Control spread; remove excess. Provides habitat for tiny aquatic life. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

giant water lily.description: Also known as: Amazon water lily, Victoria water lily. The largest water lily in the world, with circular floating pads up to 3m in diameter that can support the weight of a child. White flowers bloom at night.
giant water lily.care_tips: Fully aquatic — grow in still, warm water at least 60 cm deep. Full sun essential — at least 8 hours daily for pad development. Very high humidity (naturally provided by water). Rich, heavy clay-loam pond soil topped with gravel. Feed heavily with aquatic plant fertilizer tablets pushed into soil monthly. Water temperature must stay above 20°C — grown as annual in temperate climates. Each pad lives about 2 weeks before being replaced. Pads have sharp spines underneath.
