Flowers open white at night, turn pink by morning. Non-toxic. Remove dead or yellowing leaves. Thin overcrowded plants to main

hornwort.description: Also known as: Coontail, Rigid Hornwort. Fast-growing rootless aquatic plant that floats or can be anchored, excellent for nutrient absorption and algae control.
hornwort.care_tips: Medium light preferred — very high or very low light causes needle shedding. Can float freely or be weighted down; has no true roots. Tolerates 10-30°C, with optimal growth at 22-28°C. pH 6.0-7.5. Very fast grower — up to 10 cm per week under ideal conditions. Trim regularly and remove fallen needles to keep tank clean. Excellent biological filter, absorbing ammonia, nitrates, and phosphates. Non-toxic and safe for all aquarium fish and invertebrates.

horsetail.description: Ancient, primitive plant with hollow, jointed, bamboo-like stems and no true leaves or flowers. A living fossil — horsetails date back over 350 million years to the Carboniferous period.
horsetail.care_tips: Keep soil consistently wet to waterlogged — horsetails are semi-aquatic and naturally grow in ditches, stream banks, and boggy ground. Partial shade to full sun. Adaptable to any soil. Do not fertilize. CAUTION: Extremely invasive — spreads aggressively by deep rhizomes that are nearly impossible to remove once established. Always grow in containers sunk into the ground or in lined beds. Popular for modern, minimalist garden design (architectural vertical lines). Used historically for polishing metal (silica in stems). Mildly toxic to livestock if consumed in large quantities; mildly toxic to

indoor aquatics.description: Aquatic plants grown indoors in water containers or hydroponic setups.
indoor aquatics.care_tips: Keep roots submerged in water at all times. Change water weekly to prevent stagnation and algae growth. Use filtered or distilled water to avoid mineral buildup. Bright indirect light preferred. Add liquid fertilizer monthly at quarter strength. Clean container monthly. Some plants can transition from soil to water. Perfect for hydroponic setups or decorative water containers. Research specific plant for exact requirements. Remove yellowing or damaged leaves promptly.

java fern.description: One of the most popular beginner aquarium plants, grows attached to rocks and driftwood rather than planted in substrate.
java fern.care_tips: Low to moderate light — avoid high-intensity lighting which causes brown spots. Do not bury rhizome in substrate — attach to driftwood or rocks with thread or glue. pH 5.5-7.5. No CO2 injection needed. Propagates via plantlets on leaf tips. Very slow grower. Non-toxic and safe for all fish, shrimp, and snails. Remove dead or yellowing leaves. Thin overcrowded plants to maintain water quality.

java moss.description: Also known as: Bogor Moss, Mini Moss, Christmas Moss (similar). Fast-growing aquatic moss that clings to surfaces, ideal for aquascaping and providing fry shelter.
java moss.care_tips: Low to moderate light — higher light speeds growth but may encourage algae. Attach to driftwood, rocks, or mesh with thread or glue; it will self-attach over time. Tolerates 15-30°C, a wide comfort range. pH 6.0-7.5. No CO2 or fertilizer required but both boost growth. Trim regularly to prevent dense mats that trap debris. Absorbs nitrates and phosphates, improving water quality. Non-toxic and safe for all aquatic life.

lotus.description: Also known as: Sacred Lotus, Indian Lotus. Aquatic perennial with iconic round leaves and showy flowers rising above the water. Edible roots (lotus root), seeds, and leaves widely used in Asian cuisine. Spiritual significance in many cultures.
lotus.care_tips: Grow in shallow to deep water (6-24 inches). Never allow to dry out. Full sun essential. Fertilize with aquatic plant fertilizer tablets. Plant tubers in spring. Beautiful flowers bloom above water. Edible roots (lotus root), seeds, and leaves. Can be invasive - contain with barriers. Important in Chinese culture and Buddhism. Requires water garden or pond. Aquatic; winter care varies by Hardiness Zone. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

scientific_names: Aegagropila brownii (syn. A. linnaei) (Marimo moss ball)
marimo moss ball.description: Spherical green algae colony that grows naturally in cold, clear lakes. A popular low-maintenance aquatic novelty plant.
marimo moss ball.care_tips: Low to moderate indirect light — avoid direct sunlight which causes browning and algae overgrowth. Keep in cool water (10-20°C); temperatures above 25°C can kill them. Change water every 1-2 weeks and gently squeeze to remove debris. Freshwater only; pH 6.5-7.5. Gently roll the ball periodically to maintain its round shape. Extremely slow-growing at about 5 mm per year. Non-toxic to fish, shrimp, and pets. Pick off any brown or decaying patches; if a ball falls apart, re-roll the pieces into smaller balls.

papyrus.description: Tall marginal aquatic. Egyptian papyrus grows in shallow water or wet soil. Dramatic upright stems with fluffy tops.
papyrus.care_tips: Shallow water or saturated soil. Full sun. Tropical—protect from frost. Can grow in submerged pots. Fertilize occasionally in growing season. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly. Cut spent stems at the base.

pickerelweed.description: Emergent aquatic plants in the Pontederiaceae family with spikes of blue flowers, ideal for pond margins.
pickerelweed.care_tips: Grow in shallow water (up to 12 inches) or constantly wet soil. Never allow to dry out. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize monthly during growing season with aquatic plant fertilizer. Spreads by rhizomes - may need containment. Remove spent flowers to prevent self-seeding. Perfect for pond margins and water gardens. Attracts pollinators. Provides wildlife habitat. Aquatic; winter care varies by Hardiness Zone. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

scientific_names: Cyperus alternifolius subsp. flabelliformis (syn. C. involucratus) subsp. flabelliformis (syn. C. involucratus; Umbrella papyrus)
umbrella palm.description: Cyperus (umbrella plant) for water gardens. Stems topped with umbel leaf whorls. Thrives in saturated soil or shallow water.
umbrella palm.care_tips: Shallow water or saturated soil. Full sun to partial shade. Keep roots wet. Tropical—protect from frost. No soil watering—grown in water. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

water hawthorn.description: Floating aquatic with fragrant white flowers. Aponogeton blooms spring and fall. Submerged planting; leaves float.
water hawthorn.care_tips: Plant in 6–18 in water. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize with pond tabs. Can go dormant in hot summer. Flowers float on surface. Remove dead or yellowing leaves. Thin overcrowded plants to maintain water quality.

scientific_names: Pontederia crassipes (syn. Eichhornia crassipes) (Floating water hyacinth)
water hyacinth.description: Floating aquatic with purple flowers. Highly invasive—illegal in some areas. Provides shade and filtration. Check local regulations.
water hyacinth.care_tips: Floats on still water. Full sun. No planting—add to surface. Remove excess to control spread. Illegal in many US states—check before growing. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

water iris.description: Iris species adapted to wet conditions, grow in shallow water or boggy soil, ideal for water gardens.
water iris.care_tips: Grow in shallow water (up to 6 inches) or constantly wet, boggy soil. Never allow to dry out. Full sun to partial shade. Fertilize monthly during growing season with aquatic plant fertilizer. Divide every 3-4 years to maintain vigor. Remove dead foliage. Perfect for pond edges and water gardens. Some species can be invasive - check local regulations. Aquatic; winter care varies by Hardiness Zone. Toxic to pets—rhizomes especially; keep away from pets. Cut back dead foliage in late fall.

water lettuce.description: Floating rosettes resembling lettuce. Spreads rapidly. Invasive in warm climates. Provides shade. Check local regulations.
water lettuce.care_tips: Floats on still water. Full sun. No planting—add to surface. Control spread; remove excess. Illegal in some areas. Tropical—frost kills. Toxic to pets—keep away from pets. Remove dead or yellowing leaves. Thin overcrowded plants to maintain water quality.

water lily.description: Classic floating aquatic. Leaves and flowers float on surface. Plant in pots at pond bottom. Hardy and tropical types.
water lily.care_tips: Full sun. Plant in soil at 6–18 in depth. Use aquatic pots. Fertilize with pond tabs. Remove yellow leaves. Trim roots when repotting. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset if ingested.

butterwort.description: Also known as: Pinguicula. Carnivorous plants in the Lentibulariaceae family with sticky leaves that trap insects, include temperate and tropical species.
butterwort.care_tips: Constant moisture with distilled or rainwater ONLY - never tap water. Keep in tray of water (1-2 inches deep). Bright indirect light preferred. High humidity (60-70%+) preferred. Use only sphagnum peat moss or specialized carnivorous plant soil. Don't fertilize - they get nutrients from insects. Temperate species require dormancy; tropical species do not. Sticky leaves trap small insects. Research specific species for exact requirements. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

carnivorous plant.description: Plants that attract, trap, and digest insects and other small prey. Adapted to nutrient-poor boggy conditions with high humidity and acidic, low-nutrient soil.
carnivorous plant.care_tips: Use only distilled, rainwater, or reverse-osmosis water — minerals in tap water damage or kill carnivorous plants. Keep soil consistently moist; many prefer the tray method (sitting in 1 inch of water). Use nutrient-free soil (pure peat or sphagnum with perlite — never potting mix). Bright light essential (4-6 hours direct sun or strong grow lights). High humidity (50-80%) preferred. Never fertilize through soil. Do not trigger traps for fun — wastes plant energy. Many temperate species require winter dormancy (cool, reduced light). Research specific genus for exact requirements. Remove flower

cobra lily.description: Also known as: Darlingtonia. Unique carnivorous plant in the Sarraceniaceae family native to California and Oregon, requires cool conditions.
cobra lily.care_tips: Constant moisture with distilled or rainwater ONLY - never tap water. Keep in tray of water (1-2 inches deep). Prefer cool conditions - avoid heat. Bright indirect to direct light. High humidity (60%+) preferred. Use only sphagnum peat moss or specialized carnivorous plant soil. Don't fertilize - they get nutrients from insects. Require dormancy period in winter. Unique cobra-like appearance. Very challenging to grow outside native range. Remove dead traps and flower stalks (unless saving seed). Avoid trimming active traps.

cape sundew.description: Popular tropical sundew from South Africa, easy to grow and forgiving of beginners. No dormancy required. Produces tall flower stalks and abundant sticky dew.
cape sundew.care_tips: Constant moisture with distilled or rainwater ONLY - never tap water. Keep in tray of water (1-2 inches deep). Bright indirect to direct light (6-8 hrs ideal). High humidity (50-70%) preferred. Use only sphagnum peat moss or specialized carnivorous plant soil. Don't fertilize - they get nutrients from insects. No dormancy needed. One of the easiest carnivorous plants to grow. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

nepenthes.description: Tropical pitcher plants (monkey cups) from Southeast Asia with hanging pitcher traps. Highlanders and lowlanders have different temperature needs.
nepenthes.care_tips: Constant moisture with distilled or rainwater ONLY - never tap water. Water when top of medium feels dry; avoid waterlogging. Bright indirect to filtered light. High humidity (60-80%+) essential - often grown in terrariums. Use only sphagnum moss or specialized carnivorous plant mix. Don't fertilize - they get nutrients from insects. No dormancy. Research highlander vs lowlander requirements for your species. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

pitcher plant.description: Carnivorous plants with modified leaves forming pitcher-shaped traps, include temperate and tropical species.
pitcher plant.care_tips: Constant moisture with distilled or rainwater ONLY - never tap water. Keep in tray of water (1-2 inches deep). Bright indirect to direct light depending on species. High humidity (60-70%+) preferred. Use only sphagnum peat moss or specialized carnivorous plant soil. Don't fertilize - they get nutrients from insects. Temperate species require dormancy; tropical species do not. Fill pitchers with water if they dry out. Research specific species for exact requirements. Remove dead traps and flower stalks (unless saving seed). Avoid trimming active traps.

sarracenia.description: Also known as: Trumpet pitcher. North American pitcher plants native to boggy regions. Upright or hooded pitchers trap insects. Require winter dormancy. Can be grown outdoors in zones 6-9.
sarracenia.care_tips: Constant moisture with distilled or rainwater ONLY - never tap water. Keep in tray of water (1-2 inches deep). Bright indirect to full sun (4-6 hrs). High humidity (60%+) preferred. Use only sphagnum peat moss or specialized carnivorous plant soil. Don't fertilize - they get nutrients from insects. Require dormancy in winter (cooler temps, reduced watering). Fill pitchers with water if they dry out. Remove flower stems and any damaged or rotting leaves promptly.

sundew.description: Also known as: Drosera. Carnivorous plants in the Droseraceae family with sticky, dewy leaves that trap insects.
sundew.care_tips: Constant moisture with distilled or rainwater ONLY - never tap water. Keep in tray of water (1-2 inches deep). Bright indirect to direct light depending on species. High humidity (60%+) preferred. Use only sphagnum peat moss or specialized carnivorous plant soil. Don't fertilize - they get nutrients from insects. Temperate species require dormancy; tropical species do not. Dewy appearance indicates healthy plant. Research specific species for exact requirements. Remove dead traps and flower stalks (unless saving seed). Avoid trimming active traps.

venus flytrap.description: Also known as: VFT. Most famous carnivorous plant in the Droseraceae family, native to North Carolina, requires dormancy and pure water.
venus flytrap.care_tips: Constant moisture with distilled or rainwater ONLY - never tap water (minerals kill them). Keep in tray of water (1-2 inches deep). Reduce watering in winter dormancy but keep slightly moist. Bright indirect to direct light (4-6 hours daily). High humidity (60%+) preferred. Use only sphagnum peat moss or specialized carnivorous plant soil. Don't fertilize - they get nutrients from insects. Require dormancy period in winter (cooler temperatures, reduced light). Don't trigger traps unnecessarily - each trap can only close a few times. Remove flower stems and any damaged or rotting leaves promptl

air plants.description: Epiphytic plants in the Bromeliaceae family that grow without soil, absorb water and nutrients through their leaves.
air plants.care_tips: Soak weekly for 20-30 minutes in room temperature water. Mist 2-3 times per week between soaks. Shake off excess water after soaking - water left in center causes rot. Ensure good air circulation - never keep in closed containers. Bright indirect light preferred. High humidity (50%+) preferred. Fertilize monthly by adding fertilizer to soak water at quarter strength. Grow without soil - mount on wood, rocks, or display in air. Research specific species for exact requirements. Remove dead leaves or spent bloom spikes. Minimal pruning needed for air plants.

dendrobium orchid.description: Large orchid genus with cane-like stems and sprays of flowers. Many types: nobile (cool rest), phalaenopsis-type (warm), others. Epiphytic.
dendrobium orchid.care_tips: Water when medium is nearly dry (weekly to bi-weekly). Never let sit in water. Bright indirect light - some tolerate more sun. High humidity (50-70%) preferred. Fertilize monthly with orchid fertilizer at quarter strength. Use bark-based orchid mix. Rest period varies by type - nobile needs cool dry rest for blooms. Research specific hybrid for exact cycle. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

epiphytes general.description: General category for plants that grow on other plants - see specific categories (Orchids, Bromeliads, Air Plants) for detailed care.
epiphytes general.care_tips: Mist regularly (daily to weekly depending on species). Soak mounted plants weekly for 15-30 minutes. Ensure good drainage - never let sit in water. Bright indirect light preferred. High humidity (50-70%) preferred. Fertilize monthly with diluted fertilizer. Grow without soil - mount on wood, bark, or in specialized epiphyte mix. Good air circulation essential. Research specific plant type for exact requirements - see Orchids, Bromeliads, Air Plants for detailed care. Remove dead leaves or spent bloom spikes. Minimal pruning needed for air plants.

lichen.description: Symbiotic organism (fungus + algae/cyanobacteria) growing on bark, rocks, or soil. Rarely cultivated; use for identification or terrarium accent.
lichen.care_tips: Mist regularly to maintain moisture - lichens absorb from air. High humidity and good air circulation. Bright indirect to low light depending on species. Do not fertilize. Display on bark or rocks. Very slow growth. Difficult to cultivate outside natural habitat - most are wild-collected for display. No pruning; let displayed pieces dry between mistings so they do not rot.

mosses.description: Non-vascular bryophytes that require constant moisture and high humidity, absorb water through leaves.
mosses.care_tips: Mist daily or multiple times per day to maintain constant moisture. Never allow to dry out completely - even brief drying can kill moss. High humidity (80%+) essential - use terrarium or enclosed space. Bright indirect to low light preferred; direct sun dries moss quickly. Use distilled or rainwater - tap water minerals can harm moss. Acidic conditions preferred. Perfect for terrariums and moss gardens. Very challenging to maintain outside natural habitat. No pruning needed; brush off fallen debris and trim the edges to keep the carpet tidy.

oncidium orchid.description: Epiphytic orchids with spray-like flower stems, often yellow "dancing lady" blossoms. Includes many intergeneric hybrids (Oncostele, etc.).
oncidium orchid.care_tips: Water when medium is nearly dry (weekly to bi-weekly). Never let sit in water. Bright indirect light - more light than Phalaenopsis. High humidity (50-70%) preferred. Fertilize monthly with orchid fertilizer at quarter strength. Use bark-based orchid mix. Good air circulation. Pseudobulbs store water - slight wrinkling is normal between waterings. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly. Cut the spent flower spike at the base.

orchids.description: Large family of epiphytic and terrestrial plants in the Orchidaceae family, many are popular houseplants with specific care needs.
orchids.care_tips: Water when potting medium is nearly dry (weekly to bi-weekly). Never let sit in water. Bright indirect light preferred - avoid direct sun. High humidity (50-70%) preferred. Fertilize monthly with orchid fertilizer at quarter strength. Use specialized orchid potting mix (bark, sphagnum moss). Repot every 2-3 years. Good air circulation essential. Many species are epiphytic. Research specific genus for exact requirements. Remove dead leaves or spent bloom spikes. Cut spent flower spikes at the base once they turn brown.

resurrection fern.description: Epiphytic fern in the Polypodiaceae family that can survive extreme drought by curling up and appearing dead.
resurrection fern.care_tips: Mist regularly (2-3 times per week). Soak mounted plants weekly for 15-30 minutes. Can survive drought by curling up - will revive when watered. Bright indirect light preferred. High humidity (50-70%) preferred. Fertilize monthly with diluted fertilizer. Grow without soil - mount on wood or bark. Good air circulation essential. Epiphytic - grows on trees in nature. Very drought tolerant for a fern. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

spanish moss.description: Also known as: Graybeard. Air plant (Tillandsia usneoides) that hangs in draping strands. No roots in soil - absorbs moisture through leaves. Grows on trees in Southeast US.
spanish moss.care_tips: Mist or soak 2-3x per week. Can dunk in water 10-20 min weekly. Shake off excess - never leave waterlogged. Bright indirect light. High humidity (50%+) preferred. No soil - hang or drape on branches, driftwood. Good air circulation. Tolerates mild freeze. Do not use copper - it is toxic to Tillandsia. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

xerographica air plant.description: Large, sculptural air plant with silvery curly leaves. Xeromorphic - needs less water than most Tillandsia. Drought tolerant.
xerographica air plant.care_tips: Mist 2-3x per week; soak 1-2x per month for 30-60 min. Shake off excess - water in crown causes rot. Thick leaves mean less frequent watering than other air plants. Bright indirect light. High humidity preferred. No soil - display on wood or in air. Tolerates neglect better than most air plants. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

vanda orchid.description: Monopodial orchids with strap leaves and large, colorful flowers. Often grown bare-root in baskets or with minimal media. Need high light and humidity.
vanda orchid.care_tips: Water daily to every few days when grown bare-root; when potted, water when nearly dry. Mist roots frequently. Bright light - more than Phalaenopsis. High humidity (60%+) essential. Fertilize weekly at quarter strength. Use coarse bark or grow in slatted basket without media. Good air circulation. Can bloom multiple times per year. Remove dead leaves or spent bloom spikes. Cut spent flower spikes at the base once they turn brown.

vanilla.description: Climbing orchid (Vanilla planifolia) that produces the vanilla bean. Grows as a vine; needs support. Tropical, high humidity and warmth. Also grown commercially as one of the world's most valuable spices.
vanilla.care_tips: Water when medium is nearly dry (2-3x per week when growing). High humidity (80%+) essential - greenhouse or terrarium ideal. Bright indirect to filtered light. Fertilize monthly with orchid fertilizer. Use orchid bark mix. Provide sturdy support for vining growth. Flowers only with maturity (several years) and hand-pollination. Beans develop after pollination. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

alpine aster.description: Compact alpine aster with daisy-like flowers in late spring to summer. Cold hardy, suited to rock gardens and alpine troughs.
alpine aster.care_tips: Light watering (every 1-2 weeks). Allow to dry between waterings. Excellent drainage essential - use rocky, gritty mix. Full sun preferred. Drought tolerant once established. Fertilize sparingly in spring. Perfect for rock gardens. Shear after flowering to contain. Alpine; reduce watering when dormant; avoid winter wet. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

alpine plants.description: Plants adapted to high-altitude, rocky conditions with excellent drainage, many are drought tolerant.
alpine plants.care_tips: Light watering (every 1-2 weeks). Allow to dry between waterings. Excellent drainage essential - use rocky, gritty soil mix. Avoid waterlogged soil which causes root rot. Full sun preferred. Many are drought tolerant once established. Fertilize sparingly in spring. Perfect for rock gardens. Adapted to high-altitude, rocky conditions. Research specific species for exact requirements. Alpine; reduce watering when dormant; avoid winter wet. Deadhead after flowering. Remove dead foliage in early spring. Avoid heavy pruning.

aubrieta.description: Mat-forming alpine perennial in the Brassicaceae family with masses of spring flowers, excellent for rock gardens.
aubrieta.care_tips: Light watering (every 1-2 weeks). Allow to dry between waterings. Excellent drainage essential. Full sun preferred. Drought tolerant once established. Fertilize sparingly in spring. Shear after flowering to maintain shape. Mat-forming habit. Masses of spring flowers. Perfect for rock gardens, walls, and slopes. Very cold hardy. Alpine; reduce watering when dormant; avoid winter wet. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

alpine bellflower.description: Low-growing alpine bellflowers with blue or purple bells. Cold hardy, suited to rock gardens and crevices.
alpine bellflower.care_tips: Light watering (every 1-2 weeks). Allow to dry between waterings. Excellent drainage essential. Full sun to light shade. Fertilize sparingly in spring. Perfect for rock gardens and walls. Very cold hardy. Alpine; reduce watering when dormant; avoid winter wet. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

alpine pink.description: Tiny alpine pink with single flowers, often pink or white. Compact cushion form. Cold hardy, ideal for rock gardens.
alpine pink.care_tips: Light watering (every 1-2 weeks). Allow to dry between waterings. Excellent drainage essential - alkaline soil preferred. Full sun. Drought tolerant once established. Fertilize sparingly. Shear after flowering. Perfect for rock gardens. Alpine; reduce watering when dormant; avoid winter wet. Mildly toxic to pets—may cause GI upset. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

edelweiss.care_tips: Light watering (every 1-2 weeks). Allow to dry between waterings. Excellent drainage essential - use rocky, gritty soil mix. Avoid waterlogged soil. Full sun preferred. Very drought tolerant once established. Fertilize sparingly if at all. Perfect for rock gardens and alpine gardens. Challenging to grow outside alpine conditions. Symbol of the Alps. gentian.description: Also known as: Gentiana. Alpine and woodland plants in the Gentianaceae family with intense blue flowers, prefer cool, moist conditions.
gentian.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist but well-drained. Prefer cool, moist conditions. Excellent drainage essential. Full sun to partial shade depending on species. Fertilize sparingly in spring. Perfect for rock gardens and alpine gardens. Many species are challenging to grow. Adapted to high-altitude conditions. Research specific species for exact requirements. Alpine; reduce watering when dormant; avoid winter wet. Deadhead after flowering. Remove dead foliage in early spring. Avoid heavy pruning.

lewisia.description: Also known as: Bitterroot. Alpine succulents with rosettes and showy flowers in pink, magenta, or white. Needs sharp drainage; crown must stay dry.
lewisia.care_tips: Water when soil is dry; avoid wetting crown - rot is common. Excellent drainage essential - grow in sloping rock or gritty mix. Full sun to light shade. Plant crown above soil level. Fertilize sparingly. Perfect for rock gardens. Challenging in wet climates. Alpine; reduce watering when dormant; avoid winter wet. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

alpine primrose.description: Delicate alpine perennials forming rosettes of leaves with clusters of jewel-toned flowers in spring, native to mountain meadows and rocky crevices of Europe and Asia where they endure harsh winters under snow cover.
alpine primrose.care_tips: Keep soil evenly moist during spring growth and flowering; reduce watering in summer heat and winter. Partial sun with afternoon shade in hot climates—full morning sun is ideal. Medium humidity fine; good air circulation essential to prevent crown rot. Excellent drainage critical—use gritty, mineral-rich alpine mix (50% grit to 50% compost). Minimal fertilizer; light top-dressing with fine gravel and lean compost in autumn.
